x: Further flare ups in the USA-Iran conflict this week have only added to the disruption in the tanker market. This will help to sustain the current high earnings and valuations environment, and with no solution in sight, it is fair to say levels on both are likely to increase in the near term. While other modern units remain under discussion in the MR space, 12-year-old unit LVM AARON (50k dwt Dae Sun 2014) was the only sale in this subsector, selling to Besiktas for USD 35.5M. Elsewhere, Greek buyers are reported to have purchased scrubber fitted CABO SAN VINCENTE (63k dwt STX 2008)*Ice 1A for USD 22M.   Capesize bulkers are leading the way for dry tonnage, breaking through the USD 50k/day threshold on the spot market. Would-be sellers of capes are now likely to think twice before committing ships unless buyers can beat last done, given the bumper earnings are also bleeding into term rates. Such is displayed by scrubber fitted CAPE CONDOR (180k dwt Koyo 2010) selling this week for USD 39M, mere days after scrubber fitted ERATO (180k dwt Imabari 2010) was sold for USD 38M. Asset pricing across all sizes on dry remains firm, however there appears to be no shortage of buyers given the earnings on offer.

Record profits in the crude space continue to fuel rampant tanker buying appetite. Lofty valuations, even for this market, are being met by buyers who are targeting prompt tonnage, often bypassing usual concerns such as yard or survey dates. The suezmax sector has seen particular action this week with new benchmarks being set across the curve. Scrubber fitted CAPE BENAT (156k dwt Rongsheng 2010) sold at USD 62.5M to Lila Global, and SS due ANTIGUA I (157k dwt New Times 2016) sold for USD 90M.    The dry bulk market action is more modest by comparison, but still healthy for this time of year. Owners are in a luxurious position of having the option to sell ageing tonnage at firm valuations, or indeed just keep operating their ships in healthy earnings environments. The supramax sector was busiest this week with a flurry of transactions, helping to price the older end of the curve. With the Q4 supra/ultra futures curve sitting around the USD 20K/day mark, buyers are clearly plentiful. The 20-year-old benchmark was set with SPAR SCORPIO (53k dwt Chengxi 2006) sold for USD 11.5M despite surveys being due in October of this year.

The disruption in the tanker market shows no sign of easing, and arguably we are at one of the furthest points from resolution we’ve seen so far in the USA-Iran conflict. The prevailing factors are tightening lists and causing rates to surge. Incredible returns are there to be made, seen in the confidence shown from an unknown buyer rumored to have bought the VLCC HELLSTUGUTINDEN (299k dwt Universal 2003) for a sensational USD 57M.   While the tanker market keeps making headlines, the dry space is bringing in consistent returns, keeping prices firm. Capesize rates have strengthened in recent weeks, which will attract buyers at both ends of the age curve. Pricing the older end of the curve, we have JIAN FA (175k dwt SWS 2004) sold this week at USD 18.5M. A quiet week, otherwise, due to holiday season.

Nothing quite sums up the current value environment quite like the sale of 2-year-old scrubber fitted Suezmax BRISTOL (157k dwt Hyundai Samho 2024) at USD 123M. This figure sees former owners CMB.Tech banking a gain of USD 56.9M on the asset it purchased in 2021 at a reported total cost of USD 66.4M. Not only is the gain noteworthy, but the confidence in this tanker market is such that there are also willing buyers at these levels. Not to be outshone, the clean market was also the stage for a significant transaction this week with ON PROSPER/PROMISE (50k dwt HHI 2026) sold at USD 59M each to GEM. This will effectively reprice modern MR tanker values.   A fairly uneventful week in the dry market as we enter prime summer holiday time in Southern Europe. Pricing across the market has remained firm alongside consistent earnings, and buyers are there to snap up any available tonnage. Vessels from good yards will be main beneficiaries as seen the sale of GRAMOS (61k dwt NACKS 2019), sold to Greek buyers for USD 34.5M. Older panamax bulkers continue to fetch a premium, seen in 18-year-old FRANCESCO CORRADO (77k dwt Oshima 2008) bought by Korean buyers for USD 15M.

ADNOC’s expansion of their fleet is once again the headline story, as more details emerge from their ongoing buying spree. An en bloc deal on two Frontline VLCCs FRONT HUMBER/VEFSNA (297/298k dwt Hyundai Samho/HHIC 2017) for USD 270M stands out for the sheer size of transaction, but importantly it shows that experienced owners are willing to sell units in this market in order to crystalise gains following the recent prolific rise in values. Regarding the earnings market, talks are open between Iran and Oman on a ‘Navigation Plan’ for Hormuz, so we could potentially see some easing of the vast inefficiencies being experienced by tanker owners and charterers, time will tell. Older units are still being sold for huge premiums, with this week GRIT (298k dwt Daewoo 2003) sold for USD 50M.  Dry remains a very open avenue for liquidity, with plenty of action in the 10–15-year-old age range. There is a precarious feel to macro fundamentals, however, which is likely to impact dry charter rates going forward. A sustained high energy cost scenario would potentially weaken the overall manufacturing space, and it feels we are a long way from any solution from the main cause of this (USA/Iran). Capesize values appear to be softening slightly, with SS passed ORANGE TIGER (181k dwt Imabari 2011) bought by Mercuria for USD 36.5M.

ADNOC has made a splash in the VLCC market this week, acquiring at least five units for use in their own trading operations. The deals have prompted debate over whether the prices paid are representative of the wider market or instead reflect the lucrative and highly specific employment intended for the vessels. It remains to be seen, however, whether other owners will view these levels as grounds to raise their own price expectations.  Dry bulk earnings remain healthy, giving Sellers little incentive to soften their price expectations. Despite firm asset values, liquidity remains elevated in the 15-year-old space, with several transactions reported this week. Kamsarmax sisters ARTVIN/ORDU (81k dwt HMD 2012/2011) were sold en bloc to Korean buyers for USD 39m.

Never a dull moment in the tanker market as this week oil eclipsed USD 100/bbl for the first time since May, amid renewed involvement in the general conflict by the Houthis. Threats and attacks against vessels transiting the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait mean that we are presented with a two-chokepoint problem, which would exacerbate the already extraordinary market conditions tankers (and global oil flows) are facing. Wider economic fears are shaking markets, with most hoping that a resolution can be found quickly so that we are not faced with a sustained high oil price environment. Buyers are cautiously watching the unfolding situation, with second-hand sales effectively grinding to a halt. This week STST J19 EVA HONGKONG (19k dwt Usuki 2017) sold for USD 30M.    Amid the headline grabbing tanker market, dry has remained consistent. Earnings have not budged for the past few weeks, and sellers of tonnage are largely able to set lofty price targets for any buyers willing to meet them. The allure of these earnings are enough for some buyers, as we are seeing a steady stream of sales. China remains one of the prime destinations for second hand capes as this week sisters AANYA/AASHNA (179k dwt HHIC 2012) sold for USD 75M en bloc to Chinese buyers. The sale that stole the show this week, however, is ultramax SEACON TOKYO (66k dwt Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2023) selling for USD 41.6M, a figure that will have owners and brokers rethinking their values.

Further escalation in the Middle East is a worrying scenario as much for the global markets as it is for tanker owners and operators. Production shut-ins, lower export capacities, and eventually higher oil prices are hardly things the global economy needs right now, and the effect on tanker rates should be negative as cargoes dwindle. Rates have however, remained resilient so far during the disruption and are at very healthy levels, meaning we are unlikely to see softening in tanker values anytime soon. Sizeable premiums are still being paid on older units, seen in the sale of 2x Ice class 1A suezmax pair ALASKA/ARCHANGEL (163k dwt Hyundai 2006) at USD 50.75M each.  Quiet week once again on the dry second-hand front, likely a combination of the exasperating conditions in the Middle East and the beginning of summer holidays. The general situation on dry is rosy, with earnings consistent across all sectors, and values firm. Some action to report this week as Meghna continue their ultramax buying spree with scrubber fitted pair BRITTA/BENJAMIN OLDENDORFF (62k dwt Oshima 2020) at just over USD 37M each.

Strait of Hormuz crossings have almost ground to halt as USA and Iran trade blows once again, proving the fragility of the MOU. While disruption can boost earnings, tanker owners still need the free flow of cargo, and the new strikes are a cause for concern. This week, scrubber fitted GH HOLIDAY (157k dwt New Times 2016) was sold for USD 81M to GNMTC, setting a new benchmark in this sector.   Like on the wet, dry owners and charterers will be closely observing the deteriorating situation in Hormuz. Earnings in the meantime have remained consistent, and values too are strong, which will certainly keep owners happy. There is a “school’s out” feel in the market this week with less second-hand activity than usual, and buyers perhaps taking a step back in these complicated conditions. On the modern front, ultramax WF ARTEMIS (63k dwt Iwagi Zosen 2020) sold to Meghna for USD 36.5M.

The tanker market continues its watchful approach to the second-hand space in the aftermath of a fragile reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Owners will be tested through the remainder of the 60-day MOU, where volumes are unlikely to move much. Rates in general are coming under downward pressure, with crude buyers not rushing to replenish in the short term. Across the clean market, particularly in the Atlantic, MR rates have returned to normal levels following an intensely profitable period, as lower volumes result in ships outweighing the number of cargoes available. This week Y/Knot emerged as buyers of LR2 JAG LOKESH (105K dwt HHI 2009) for USD 44.1M.   The dry market is providing the liquidity this week, albeit at levels that give a cautious feel. The global macro situation, despite a lower oil price potentially helping the outlook, is still very unpredictable. Rising interest rates and a much-speculated over-inflated stock market will cast some doubt into the minds of buyers, which could fuel a bearish feel to the market. That said there is still plenty of opportunity for those willing to invest at these levels. This week, ADNOC bought SS passed HAATO (61K dwt Shin Kasado 2011) for USD 23.5M.

Tanker rates are grabbing headlines in the aftermath of the confusing yet tangible progress which has been made on opening the Strait of Hormuz. The market is offering some levels of correction to the extraordinarily high levels that we have seen in the last months, however at numbers that will satisfy owners. In the shadow of continued newbuild ordering, a quieter week in the second-hand space as buyers observe how the next phase of the Middle East saga plays out. In the specialised market, STST J19 GREENWICH PARK (19k dwt Fukuoka 2011)* SSDD due 06/26 was sold to Vietnamese buyers at USD 22.8M.  Easing, though fragile, conditions in the Strait of Hormuz are a positive for the dry market. Lower and more consistent crude pricing will give confidence for the general macro demand outlook, while an open Strait will release trapped cargoes and allow countries within the Gulf to resume dry trading. Rates though appear to be looking on the toppy side, with the market understandably cautious about 2H 2026. Still, plenty of liquidity in the second hand space, most notably scrubber fitted capesize LADY DEENA (182k dwt JMU 2020) selling to Chinese buyers at USD 70M. Scrubber fitted 2020 blt capesize units have increased in value by 10% in the past year, seen against the sale of last done unit ex BULK GINZA (182k dwt Imabari 2020) which sold to GENCO at USD 64M in May 2025.

While not a full deal per se, the framework agreed and signed this week between USA and Iran will provide the tanker market with lower supply side risk, and hopefully some seldom seen stability. It is likely we will see a tug of war between owners and charterers over the next few weeks as the situation unfolds, though what is certain is that the market will be carefully watching the fortunes of laden crude tankers in their attempts to leave the Gulf. Buyers are still there to meet sellers’ lofty expectations on crude tonnage, seen in suezmax COSMO SAIL (159K dwt Hyundai Samho 2007) selling for USD 49.5M.   News coming from the Middle East will be positively received by the dry bulk market, hoping increased crude supply side security will keep oil prices at more sustained and manageable levels, allowing more general macro investment confidence and activity. Rates remain strong across dry and as usual there is a consistent stream of transactions. This week, MONT BLANC HAWK (81K dwt Imabari 2017) was sold for USD 32.2M.

Tanker market earnings may be cooling slightly but transactions this week prove that buyers’ confidence in this disrupted market remains sky high. CMBTech owned scrubber fitted suezmax pair BREST/BRUGGE (157K dwt Hyundai Samho 2023) are reported sold at USD 112M each, well in excess of the last Korean built resale units (albeit with later delivery) which were sold to Teekay in May at USD 95M each. Numbers like this are sure to make every modern suezmax owner think twice about their youngest units. As a result of this pricing, newbuilding remains a popular choice for investors, with healthy numbers being reported.   Those expecting an avalanche of deals to be reported after the Posidonia week will be slightly disappointed, however it is worth remembering that the general market fundamentals have not changed, and the overall geopolitical position is arguably at it’s most tense in weeks. Sellers of older capesize units are being rewarded for their patience, seeing excellent exits such as KERKIS (176K dwt Namura 2007)*SSDD due in November 26, sold for USD 25.5M.

No second-hand transactions are reported in the tanker market this week, though not due to any change in sentiment, which remains strong. Newbuilding continues to be the preferred outlet for investors in this sector, with activity particularly focused on larger crude tonnage.    Earnings across dry are in keeping with the overall buoyant shipping markets, with the lower than usual reported sales likely due to Posidonia 2026 taking place in Athens this week. SSDD due Supramax AE MARS (53K DWT Yangzhou Dayang 2006) was sold for USD 9.05M.

Scorpio this week announced the sale of 4x scrubber fitted LR2 units STI CONDOTTI/BROADWAY/WINNIE/LAUREN (109K DWT Daehan 2014/15) for a total of USD 285.8M, representing a figure of xs USD 70M per vessel. In this context it is worth remembering that only a month ago, the market was in shock at scrubber fitted 2018 blt Japanese Afras being sold in the mid USD 70M range. Deadlock in the Middle East, plus the disruption that entails, and the potential booming aftermath of a resolution is seemingly more than enough for buyers to justify the levels being paid today. Longer term question marks remain over the increased fleet growth we will see in the coming years, however this feels like a distant worry for owners and buyers alike as the short-term uncertainty reigns supreme.   There is unrelenting momentum in the dry bulk market, with average capesize spot rates climbing 12% from last week alone to a high of USD 46K/day on Thursday. Buyers still see legs in this bulk run, despite total demand growth reaching 6%, which is usually seen around the peaks of dry cycles. This confidence is seen in the fact 20 buyers registered interest in Tess 82 KEY HUNTER (82K DWT Tsuneishi 2011), which was eventually sold to Greek buyers for USD 21M. Elsewhere, the benchmark has been set for 10 year old capesize units, with scrubber fitted EHIME QUEEN (181K DWT Imabari 2016) selling for USD 59M to Chinese buyers.

Those in the market wondering what the top and bottom of the VLCC values curve looks like are in luck this week, as we report sales of 2002 and 2026 built units. Granted these are different countries of build, but the picture is as clear as it can be for owners and prospective buyers of this size of tanker. LAS PALMAS (306K DWT Hengli 2026) has been purchased by Trafigura for USD 163M, while Scrubber fitted ABIE (302K DWT Samsung 2002) was sold at USD 40.5M. Those on the selling side are happy to exit at these historic levels, so long as buyers continue to chase these units; a scenario that shows no signs of letting off. This tanker market is feeding off the lingering Hormuz disruption, and there is more than enough uncertainty to prolong the higher earnings environment while any bearish arguments can be countered with a potential post Hormuz resolution bounce.    The dry market has generally been the substory in the shipping world of late, but rates and values are surging upwards. The high volume of reported transactions this week is likely a culmination of recent weeks but still represents significant dealmaking and notable buyer confidence in this market. As usual among dry, we are seeing transactions centred around 10–15-year-old + age range with a couple of modern units sprinkled in. Of those modern units, in a rare mini cape transaction, Asyad bought LOWLANDS AMBER/CRIMSON (100KDWT OSHIMA 2021/20) for USD 75.M en bloc.

The tanker market continues to defy the broader geopolitical uncertainty, with sentiment underpinned by firm earnings and a steady flow of buyers prepared to meet owners’ price expectations. That said, crude buyers seem to have taken a breather this week as ever increasing pricing pushes more would be buyers into the yards. In the MR sector, Turkish buyers committed USD 20.8M for ice-classed ROYAL JASMINE (53K DWT GSI 2008), while AUTAN (51K DWT SPP 2009) changed hands at USD 23.5M. The pricing achieved for these vintage units further reinforces the depth of demand for mid-aged tanker tonnage, particularly where prompt trading flexibility or niche specifications are involved.  A busy time indeed across the dry market as earnings remain firm. This week saw a cluster of modern handysize resales emerge from Ciner, with CLACTON, MARGATE, EASTBOURNE and PORTSMOUTH (40K DWT Jiangmen Nanyang 2024) reportedly sold to Norden at USD 30.5M apiece. The sellers in this transaction represent the target blueprint for buyers seeking modern units in this market, in the sense they have a modern fleet with a stacked orderbook, and are more likely to listen to potential suitors. Chinese buyers were particularly active this week, acquiring both JOY (81K DWT Chengxi 2019) for USD 31.5M and HUAYANG LILY (63K DWT China Shipping 2016) at USD 25.2M. Elsewhere, Greek buyers secured SUMAQ QUEEN (51K DWT Imabari 2017) for USD 25M.

Resolution of the conflict in the Middle East seems no closer despite some encouraging headlines this week. That said, there appears to be a steady supply of buyers willing to transact at current levels, while giving owners attractive exit points across the size and age curve. All the confusing ongoing diplomacy aside, values show no signs of softening with suezmax tankers this week setting new levels for mid aged ships as 15-year-old STELLA (164K DWT Hyundai 2011) sold for USD 67M.    The BDI crossed the 3000-point mark for the first time since 2023 on the back of the recent run, whilst contending with perhaps a quieter week than usual due to holidays in China. There appears to still be room for even higher levels on the larger sizes, with some predicting Capesize will hit the USD 50K/day mark in the coming weeks. The majority of second-hand activity is limited as usual to the rgn 15-year-old tonnage, with the exception of 85K DWT wide beam Kamsarmax pair SEACON NOLA/HAMBURG (85K DWT Huangpu Wenchong 2023) begin sold for USD 36M each.

Confidence in the strength of this crude tanker market shows no signs of waning as buyers continue to pay the ever increasing price asks. Monte Nero are reported to have paid USD 140M en bloc, for scrubber fitted suezmax pair FRONT ULL/FRONT IDUN (156K DWT Rongsheng 2014/15), a figure well in excess of the price these ships were ordered for over a decade ago. Owners expectations on Aframax pricing are also being met, with scrubber fitted Aframax pair SOUTHERN REVERENCE/PUSAKA BORNEO (108K DWT Tsuneishi 2018) sold for USD 75M and USD 78M respectively. These are only the second and third transactions in the eco Aframax space this year, setting well needed benchmarks for this vintage.   While not quite at the towering heights of the tanker market, the dry space is still providing healthy returns and strong values. Buyers are not shying away either, this week GENCO purchased scrubber fitted capesize LOWLANDS SPIRIT (182K DWT Imabari 2019) for USD 67M, which interestingly represents the most modern capesize sale of the year so far. Modern dry deals have been hard to come by, perhaps we are now at a price point where we might see a few more sellers coming to the table.

Scorpio are accounting for most of the action this week with the announcement of 6 sales across their MR and LR2 fleet. They have been consistent over the last 6 months in selling out assets, taking advantage of the scarce availability of these vessels and the elevated prices on offer. Buyers are ready to pounce on these opportunities as once you start looking at more modern units, the high pricing usually encourages potential suitors to the newbuilding yards instead. Despite various extensions of ceasefires, the situation in the Middle East remains largely the same, with brent crude trading today at its highest levels in ceasefire conditions, meaning that the market will need a little more than a fragile ceasefire in order to normalise.   A relatively slow week for dry liquidity, understandable given a strange combination of near-term strength and longer-term uncertainty in the market. Earnings are strong across the size ranges for now, while long term macro sentiment is being eroded as the war in the Middle East drags on. Some rare modern transactions this week with Niovis purchasing 2x resale ultramax units (64K DWT New Dayang 2027) for USD 36.5M each.

In the last few hours, it has been announced that the Strait of Hormuz is completely open to commercial shipping traffic as Israel have agreed a 10-day ceasefire with Lebanon. Iran has said that while this ceasefire is in place, the Strait is open. Worth noting that the US blockade of ships calling to Iran is (at the time of writing) still in place. Shipowners will likely approach this with trepidation in the next 24-48 hours however, it seems to be a step in the right direction for the overall global economic outlook. Given the length of the war, enough time has now elapsed for owners to reposition previously redundant vessels, meaning the remaining cargoes will have increasing competition and should see some downside. Now if cargoes come available in the Persian Gulf, then owners will likely be scrambling to position ships appropriately. A rather poignant reminder of where we are in terms of pricing was seen this week with sale of 20-year-old VLCC KASAGISAN (302K DWT Mitsui 2006) for USD 61M, changing hands to a willing buyer for 3 times the expected residual value. Elsewhere, buyers are in hot pursuit of prompt MR tankers, with this week scrubber fitted ARDMORE ENGINEER (49K DWT STX 2014) bought by GESCO for USD 35.5M.  Activity on dry remains healthy, helped by improving rates and lower bunker costs (from recent highs) seemingly giving confidence to buyers. Sentiment will likely improve on a potential easing situation in the Middle East however, it is just too early to tell what is going to happen. Decisions can be reversed very quickly, and the situation remains fragile at best. This week, separate Chinese buyers bought Newcastlemax pair RTM CARTIER / RTM ZHENG HE (206K DWT HHIC Philippines 2012) for USD 46M each.

While a potentially positive step for global stability, the fragile ceasefire agreed between the US/Israel and Iran is still very much yet to be proven. The reality is that no universally agreed framework is in place to allow free passage of all vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, meaning that even with the optimistic headlines, nothing has really changed. Buyers are seemingly taking a step back this week, treading carefully as uncertainty reigns.  Dry is still providing liquidity to the second-hand space in general, with buyers being encouraged by robust earnings currently on offer. Scepticism remains however on the long-term prospects for the dry market, which would suffer in the event the war continues to drag on, and sustained higher oil prices lead to a larger macroeconomic demand slowdown. Secondhand liquidity is concentrated around the 15-year-old mark, with modern ships still hard to come by. This week post panamax OHSHU MARU (92K DWT Namura 2011) sold for USD 16.2M (SSDD due 06/26).

A handful of sales to report this week but in general tanker deals are a tough ask, particularly anything modern on the crude side due to the earnings possibility currently on the table. Scorpio have shown themselves to be proven sellers in recent times, taking advantage of the ongoing firming in tanker pricing, and this week selling scrubber fitted MR pair STI BROOKLYN/STI BLACK HAWK (49K DWT SPP/HMD 2015) for USD 35M each. It is worth noting that there are plenty of tanker buyers still out there, but the focus is more geared towards readying themselves for an easing of the disruption in the Persian Gulf and a subsequent softening in rates and pricing.   Converse to the tanker market, buyers seem to be readily finding an outlet for investment in the dry second-hand market, and it appears these buyers are aligning on two developing trends. The first of which is that the Handysize market, at current rates and Cal27 estimations of around the USD 12-13K/Day mark, is earning in line with the larger and more expensive supramax sector and thus is providing a lower price entry point and better financial return – hence the increased number of sales in this size range. The second trend is to do with energy security as a result of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Some players are backing a run on coal activity, as more and more energy importers seek alternatives to trapped LNG exports in the Persian Gulf. One such player is Bright Navigation, buyer of JOHN M CARRAS (82K DWT DSME 2012) for USD 18.2M.

A notable fall in recorded sales this week as the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East intensifies. The disruption is such, that even if the war was to end today and the Strait of Hormuz was to be reopened immediately, oil markets and cargo flows in the best case would take c.4 months to return to normal levels. As a result, it is likely oil and energy prices will remain high despite some headlines claiming the war to be nearing an end. It is good news for some owners in the short term however, with scarcely believable returns on offer across crude and products sectors. Those willing to take money off the table will find no shortage of suitors, however most will find it hard to pass up the immediate earnings environment even if lofty price targets are met by buyers. Some activity though this week, with DPP trading MR HIGH SEAS (49K DWT HMD 2012) sold for USD 27.6M.  The dry market is suffering similarly to the tanker space in terms of liquidity. Pricing is firm, alongside earnings that have come off in the short term, while also facing questions over longer term macro demand, should the conflict in the Middle East continue. It appears that buyers are less sensitive to pricing and earnings outlook, and having quality tonnage on the water is the primary concern. This is evidenced by FRONTIER GARLAND (181K DWT Imabari 2011) selling at USD 36.5M, sold at a time where capesize rates have retreated from previous Q1 highs.

There is no such thing as an uneventful week in the tanker market at the moment, as this week it has emerged that MSC/Sinokor have dipped their toe into the Suezmax market. It is as yet unknown whether this is just a toe, or indeed if the ship owning giant is set to make a similar splash like it did in the VLCC market this year. The Suezmax space will be much more difficult to ‘corner’ due to its fragmented nature but given the aggressivity of MSC/Sinokor seen so far this year, it would be shortsighted to write off such a play. Elsewhere, vintage J19 BUM SHIN (19K DWT Shin Kurushima Akitsu 2003) was sold for USD 7.5M.  Activity across the dry second-hand market remains slightly subdued, with ever-increasing uncertainty in long term macro sentiment, so long as the conflict in the Middle East continues. That said, buyers are closely watching which vessels are made available for sale, with quality Japanese tonnage at the top of everyone’s wish lists. This week, buyers fought it out for MG MERCURY (84K DWT Imabari 2016) with a rumoured 6 names in the mix. The ship was eventually sold for USD 28.5M, basis surveys due in August 2026.

As predicted in this report last week, we are seeing a slowdown in reported transactions while the ongoing conflict in the Middle East unfolds. Spot earnings, while having cooled off on the larger crude tonnage this week, continue to be extremely elevated and highly volatile. In a market with more questions than answers at the moment, one thing has been made clear; Iran will keep disrupting the Hormuz Strait so long as this conflict is active. Of course, this tactic is not without blowback on Iran’s own crude export markets but is a steadfast disruption tactic against its aggressors and the global shipping markets. This week, high spec scrubber fitted IMOII MR sisters FINNANGER/FJELLANGER (46K DWT HMD 2009/10) were sold for USD 48M en bloc.   The conflict has given the dry market a rude awakening. Prior to the beginning of March, dry was looking like the darling of the shipping markets following a stellar start to the year and a widely reported rosy outlook for the rest of 2026. However, now we are imagining the consequences of a sustained high oil price environment – something that could lead to a general macro/dry slowdown. Second-hand availability lists remain tight at this stage, something that would potentially keep prices firm as buyers fight it out over sales candidates. An example of this is seen this week in ultramax ABILITY (64K DWT Shin Kurushima 2021) which was sold for USD 37M with delivery SSDD passed to Greek buyers.

Clearly, a lot has changed since the previous report last Friday. A long-predicted US-Israel bombing campaign on Iran commenced over the weekend to leave tanker owners (particularly crude owners) bracing themselves for heavy disruption. Most would have expected rates to rise, though few would have dreamed of the highs we are now seeing. A monstruous $696,803/day is being reported for scrubber fitted KALAMOS (317K DWT SWS 2010), which has comfortably set the record for highest rate recorded on a spot VLCC voyage. Shockwaves are being felt in the second-hand market, where already elevated price asks are shooting up in response to the new earnings norm, that is, if candidates are still being considered for sale. Sales reported this week are likely to be some of the last with a ‘pre-war’ pricing, and we would expect the number of sales reported to fall sharply as the market adjusts to what is going on. Time will of course tell in this very unpredictable environment. This week Scrubber Fitted Aframax GREEN ATTITUDE (112K DWT COSCO 2018) was sold for USD 70M.    The dry market finds itself in a curious spot. A buoyant Q1 means that values are rising steadily, but sellers are disincentivised to part ways with tonnage. This is due to healthy rate predictions for the rest of the year and into 2027, and the fact that replacement tonnage is so hard to come by. Thus, if you sell your 15-year-old ship, yes you will receive a nice sum in return, but there is no guarantee you can find a 5-year-old equivalent to reinvest in, one would only be left with newbuildings as an option to deploy capital. Competition is fierce on any available candidates particularly quality tonnage (Japanese built units), with a rumoured 15 interested parties in SPIRIT OF HO-PING (82K DWT Tsuneishi 2011) which was eventually bought by Greek buyers for USD 19.4M. All this leaves dry with an ever growing list of buyers, and a seemingly shrinking list of candidates, something that will only influence values one way.

The sky really is the limit it seems for the tanker market as earnings go from strength to strength. Last done VLCC rates are being eclipsed by the following fixtures, leading to a game of cat and mouse between owners and charterers. Those who have waited will be the beneficiaries of the rates squeeze, while others who locked in TCs below USD 100K/day will now be feeling slightly hard done by. Buyers this week are paying more attention to the smaller crude sizes, where values have been steadily pushing north so far this year. Buyers in this space need to move quickly and be gutsy in order to capture this earnings environment, as it will feel they are chasing a runaway market. This week Scrubber fitted STENA SUNSHINE (159K DWT Samsung 2013) was bought by Thenamaris for USD 61M.   The Capesize sector has garnered the most attention in the dry space so far this year, and those who have yet to move are running out of time. Owners are seeing TC rates rise steadily, and unless buyers are there to match the ever-increasing prices, owners will be more than happy to withdraw candidates and accept the healthy returns. Modern ships are the hardest to come by, so generally buyers are restricted to the c.15-year-old range. Outside of the largest sizes, the dry sector is still providing an outlet for buyers looking for steel on the water. Competition is rife, and a rumoured 10 buyers were fighting out for Kamsarmax THREE SASKIAS (82K DWT JMU 2014), which eventually sold for USD 26.75M, setting a new benchmark in this sector.

The Sinokor machine continues to gather momentum this week as we enter a new era for the VLCC space. Such a singular concentration of vessel ownership has not been seen in the history of this market, and the South Korean outfit are showing no signs of letting up as 11 Dynacom VLCCs were confirmed this week. TC rates are quickly surpassing last done levels, from USD 90k/day to USD 100K/day reported for one year, which is justifying the historically high valuations for VLCCs. It’s not just the larger ships that are benefitting, sentiment is also engulfing most tanker segments, where sellers are increasingly confident to hold their positions.    Predictably, with Lunar New Year celebrations in full swing this week, the dry market has taken a breather. It is a rosy picture otherwise across the sector, as rates are expected remain strong throughout 2026. While not having the dramatic movement of the tanker market, dry is being seen as a safe bet and provides buyers with a more accessible entry point. This week ultramax ONLY YOU (60K DWT Sanoyas 2017) was sold for USD 28.3M.

While Sinokor has stolen the headlines so far this year with its raid on VLCCs, the increased liquidity and pricing have spurred many others into action to crystalise gains at these levels. One could argue that the turbulent geopolitical situation isn’t going anywhere, particularly during the current US administration, and there could be further upside for tanker owners, but prudent shipowners have sold vessels into buyers willing to take the exposure at these levels. On modern units, buyers are paying for the prompt delivery and long life of the asset, whereas those operating at the other end of the age curve are taking on more risk at these elevated levels. This week Thenamaris purchased scrubber fitted suezmax pair EMERALDWAY/SUNRISEWAY (158K DWT SWS 2022) for USD 88M each en bloc. In the mid aged LR2 space, scrubber fitted sisters FS DILIGENCE/ENDEAVOR (108K DWT Namura 2012) were sold for USD 43M each en bloc.   Lunar New Year celebrations will likely curtail what has been a strong start to the year for the dry market. Many analysts are touting a healthy 2026, so a slowdown will surely prove to only be temporary. Capesize demand has been relentless over the past 12 months, and we have seen values rise accordingly. This week EPIC (182K Odense 2010) was sold to European buyers at USD 32.3M while CAPE BRAZIL (177K DWT SWS 2010) was sold for USD 31.2M. There was some action in modern Ultramaxes, with BERGE TATEYAMA (63K DWT Shin Kasado 2020) sold to Turkish buyers at USD 34.5M.

This week’s sales are not representative of the raucous undercurrent of the present tanker market. The high level of enquiry and numerous ongoing discussions suggest that more second hand activity is to come. Pricing remains firm and shows no signs of respite, which may encourage prospective investors to seek better value down the newbuilding avenue. This week, scrubber fitted MARAN PYTHIA (158K DWT HHI 2009) was sold to Greek Buyers for USD 46M. The excitement isn’t limited to the crude space, MRs and LR1s have seen an uptick in demand, particularly in the mid age (rgn 15-year-old) bracket. SSDD passed sisters ELANDRA BALTIC/FJORD (51K DWT HMD 2011) were sold for USD 24.5M each en bloc.   A relatively quiet week in the dry market despite the strong start to the year. Predictably, China remains the source of much of the buying interest for ageing bulk carriers. Upcoming Lunar New Year may curtail this demand for the coming weeks, but this will likely be a temporary blip as appetite remains high across the range of sizes from Chinese buyers. In the only ECO transaction of the week, MGJ bought DARYA TAPTI (35K DWT Shikoku 2015) for USD 18.9M.

Despite crude tankers dominating tanker activity since the start of the year, this week as seen a flurry transactions in the product space with eight MR units changing hands. The chinese controlled resale LIANYUNGANG WUZHOU WZ465 (49k DWT 2026) was sold for USD 45M, in line with the last comparable transaction concluded in November 2025, despite it offering a prompter delivery. Notably, SEAWAYS MADELEINE/GRACE (49k DWT HMD 2008) were sold en bloc at USD 16.8M each, compared to same-age sisters from the same owners that achieved USD 16.2M in December 2025. This suggest heighten price volatility for older units, while modern tonnage remains more stable. Elsewhere, ARISTARCHOS (79k DWT Onomichi 2017) was sold for USD 44M, establishing a welcome new benchmark in an otherwise illiquid segment.   Dry bulk asset values continue to remain stable this week, with underlying chartering market  proving to be resilient throughout the start of this year. Stealing the headlines this week was Spar’s acquisition of NANTONG XIANGYU XY149/XY150 (63k DWT 2026), purchased en bloc for USD 72m.

Following an explosive start to the year, tanker activity has somewhat flattened this week. Rates remain firm, with owners confidently holding strong on their price expectations. Values for mid-aged MR tankers remain resilient, reflected in the sale of GREEN PLANET (50K DWT Dae Sun 2014), which achieved USD 31M. In the Handy tanker market, the HTM EVEREST (37K DWT HMD 2010) was sold for USD 20M establishing a welcomed benchmark in a relatively illiquid second hand market.  On the dry cargo front, volumes remain high with FRONTIER KOTOBUKI (174K DWT Namura 2011) sold to Global Chartering at USD 31.4M, a correction from last done sale of the MIRACLE (180K DWT Tsuneishi Cebu 2011) at USD 32M, suggesting that Cape values of similar vintage may have reached their peak.

The frenzied start to the year continued in the tanker market this week, not only due to the emergence of further Sinokor deals but other transactions cementing these new price levels. The Sinokor activity is impacting values across the crude space, and sellers are now more confident than ever that their price asks will be matched. For anything 5 years or older, this provides an attractive exit for owners. Scrubber fitted VLCC pair HUNTER/SERENDIPITY (299K DWT Hyundai Samho 2021) were bought by Trafigura for USD 125M each, while Scorpio continue take advantage of these favourable prices with the sale of scrubber fitted LR2 STI KINGSWAY (109K DWT Sungdong 2015) for USD 57.5M to Paragon Mobility.  On the dry bulk side, the excitement seems more measured. By this we mean seeing the usual premiums on more modern ships with a long trading life ahead of them, and a busier, more opportunistic environment at the other end of the age curve. Buyers have been in hot pursuit of Newcastlemaxes over the past 6 months and have had to pay premium levels for modern ships, seen in the sale this week of scrubber fitted NORD PALLADIUM (209K DWT SWS 2021) at USD 76.25M to Zhejiang Shipping. Further to this, ultramax STARRY NIGHT (61K DWT NACKS 2022) received a firm USD 32.5M from undisclosed buyers.

Few would have expected this start to the new year. Rumours have been swirling around the market from Monday this week on a huge VLCC deal involving various new TCs, extended TCs and 2nd hand S&P transactions to Sinokor. Details continue to emerge on number of ships sold, and quantity/length of the TCs, though what has caught the eye is that many of the ships were not known sales candidates, and they come from a vast spread of counterparties. Frontline, CMB Tech, TMS, Capital, Dynacom and Advantage are among the known sellers thus far, proving that in this market everything is for sale at a price. Elsewhere beyond the Sinokor excitement, Greek buyers have acquired zinc coated scrubber fitted MR pair MARITIME TRANQUILITY/COMITY (49K DWT GSI 2020) for USD 39.2M each.    No such fireworks in the dry market this week but it is worth noting this could be a fruitful period for dealmaking in this sector this year. With many market analyst touting great things across dry throughout 2026, the seasonal Q1 lull up to and including Chinese New Year could provide buyers the opportunity to increase their market exposure at potentially the softest prices they will see all year. Levels are still historically high, but owners will be open to taking money off the table to themselves reinvest or expand further. The mid-aged capesize second hand space is proving ever busy with MINERAL HONSHU (181K DWT Koyo 2012) selling for a firm USD 37.1M.

It was said in this report a few weeks ago that owners would be hard pressed to ignore buyers willing to transact at current levels, and it appears that some have caved to the extensive amount of enquiry in the market. Larger owners, for example Scorpio, have been wisely executing sales of sub 10 year old assets while simultaneously ordering new ships, ensuring fleet modernisation whilst cashing in on historically strong values of older units. This week they announced the sales of scrubber fitted STI GALLANTRY/GOAL (109K DWT GSI 2016) for USD 52.3M each. Elsewhere, SFL took money off the table with the sale of suezmax pair SFL OTTOWA/THELON (159K DWT Bohai 2015) for USD 57M each.   A quieter than usual week in the second hand dry market, and for good reason. Robust earnings over the last few months have resulted in strong pricing, and with seasonal softening expected in Q1 2026, buyers are more likely to wait. That said, the market goes into the winter break in a strong position, leaving owners hoping for more of the same in the new year. This week, kamsarmax THERESA HAINAN (81K DWT Sainty 2013) was sold for USD 16.8M.

With the festive season now in full swing, owners will be reflecting on 2025 and looking ahead to next year. For the tanker market, owners will be hoping this current market can sustain for as long as possible, however will know that volatility in earnings works both ways. MRs appear to be at the top of buyers' wishlists, having seen increased TC appetite that makes sense of current value levels. Sisters SEAWAYS OLIVE/STAR (49K HMD 2008) were sold at USD 16.2M each.  The usual healthy liquidity is seen in the bulk market this week. As has been the story all year, buyers from the Far East appear to be dominating this market and have been the destination for many European owned ships. There has been particular appetite for Capesize bulkers, which have pushed in value over the recent period. This week DENSA SHARK (179K DWT Hyundai 2012) was sold to chinese buyers for USD 32.5M with TC attached until June 2026. Elsewhere, Ultramax IVS WINDSOR (60K DWT Oshima 2016) was sold to Greeks at USD 26M.

The small number of sales being reported this week in the tanker market somewhat underplays the current market conditions. Yes, large older crude tonnage is still in demand seen in the sale of TOWADA (305K DWT Mitsubishi 2006) but behind the scenes, there is even more interest swirling around scarcely available modern units, with buyers increasingly keen to transact. Price asks are still toppy, which explains why many are choosing the newbuilding route, but with geopolitical influences more changeable than ever, sellers would be short sighted to hold out against firm buyers in such historically high markets.   The dry market is still looking very prosperous with many underlying factors signalling this prosperity is going nowhere. Underlying market demand growth is on an upswing, while commodities prices are looking bullish. Second hand vessel demand remains strong, and there is more liquidity on modern tonnage than in other sectors. This week Blumenthal purchased ice 1C URSULA MANX (82K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2021) for USD 33.85M.

The tanker market is flying into the festive period with healthy earnings across the board. This will put buyers at the mercy of sellers, who will be rethinking their price expectations accordingly. The Russia-Ukraine conflict was rather the catalyst of this current overall tanker market run throughout the last few years, however, this week market analysts and owners alike are imagining a market beyond the conflict, after positive talks between US and Ukrainian officials. It still feels a long way away, but peaceful resolution could drastically reshape the tanker market.    The BDI hit its highest levels since December 2023, as rates hold firm. Capesize rates are leading the way, and the strong demand for second hand candidates is only increasing. Tonnage hungry buyers are acting quickly and decisively, particularly in the c.15 YO range, which is encouraging owners of such units to see what bids they can attract. Values are changing rapidly; this week NGM sold PACIFIST (181K DWT Koyo 2011) for USD 32M (SSDD due January 2026), this is compared to SSDD freshly passed 1-year older scrubber fitted sister SEAUNITY (181K DWT Koyo 2010) sold at USD 30.5 at the start of the month

Sky high sentiment in the tanker market is driving activity forward with some unexpected results. Okeanis have purchased scrubber fitted resales NORTH STAR/VIKING STAR (157K DWT Daehan 2025/2026) for USD 97M per unit, setting a new benchmark for the sector. These units were ordered by Atlas in 2023 for USD 84M each, and the owners will reap significant upside by delivering the units into a strong, tonnage hungry market. This will only add fuel to the fire of the current ordering, as owners bet on future strong markets. Elsewhere in the clean sector, MR rates and activity continue to push higher. It will be interesting to see how the market will react to an extensive number of deliveries in Q1 26.    The story is similar on the dry side, sentiment high as a result of robust and consistent earnings. 2020 Bulkers this week sold off the last of their vessels in a deal worth USD 145.5M, Scrubber fitted Newcastlemax pair BULK SYDNEY/SANTOS ( 208K DWT New Times 2020) acquired by Genco. Buyers have been clambering for Newcastlemaxes in the last few months to try and capitalise on healthy long term employment opportunities in this sector. Staying in the larger sizes there is significant demand around the 15-year-old mark, mostly form Far Eastern buyers. LAKE DOLPHIN (179K DWT Hanjin Hi 2011) was sold for USD 30.5M, while FORTUNE VIOLET (181k DWT Imabari 2012) achieved USD $34M.

High spirits this week as much of the tanker market gathered in Dubai for Bahri week, in a time where earnings are holding strong into the winter months. Unsurprisingly in the second-hand space, good spec suezmax units with prompt delivery are attracting a significant amount of market interest. A number of offers were seen on Scrubber fitted STENA SUNSHINE (159K DWT Samsung 2013), which eventually sold to Greek buyers at USD 58M. Despite this, it is worth pointing out that in a period of little over a month, there have been 30 new VLCC and nearly 20 Suezmax orders, showing that plenty of other buyers in the market prefer to focus on newbuildings, rather than compete at these premium levels in the second-hand market. Otherwise, it was the MR market which saw further liquidity, with Montfort purchasing pumproom pair MAERSK MARU/MISSISSIPPI (48K DWT Iwagi Zosen 2011/10) for USD 44M en bloc.   A busy week, as ever, in the dry market. In an overall sense, the momentum is with this market despite the incoming usual seasonal slowdown. It will be interesting to assess whether this slowdown will affect asset values in any way, or whether the underlying optimism of the next year or so will carry values over this period. In the ultramax space, GRACE HARMONY (60K DWT Onomichi 2015) was sold for USD 24.8M.

Barhi week will take centre stage over the next week, and in general owners will be attending with smiles on their faces given the sustaining strength in the tanker market. Liquidity on modern ships has slowed yet continues, with Tankerska purchasing Scrubber fitted LR2 PLATANOS (114K DWT Namura 2019). Elsewhere in the product space, an active week for Scorpio with the announcement of the sale of 4x 2014 blt scrubber fitted MR units to Torm and the acquisition of 4x scrubber fitted MR resales from Jingjjiang Nanyang shipbuilding.    Much of the market were in Hamburg this week for Eisbein, where there is a mix of optimism and excitement for the next dry market run. Despite this optimism, there is still a disconnect between asset prices and earnings. New candidates in the market are expected to beat last done, and owners will not be rushed into accepting the first bid that comes their way. Competition is particularly rife within the c.15yo supramax sector, where eight sales were reported this week. Scrubber fitted Capesize SEAUNITY (181K DWT Koyo 2010) was sold for USD 30.5M, helping price an abundance of candidates in this area of the market.

After the recent run on modern tonnage, the tanker second hand market has had a much more subdued week. Overall bullish earnings sentiment remains however, and VLCCs are leading the way with several fixtures reported well in excess of USD 100K/day. Owners will be hoping these levels sustain into a healthy winter market. In the clean space, Ice 1A SEAWAYS GATUN/HERUN (47K DWT HMD 2007) sold to Champion tankers for USD 12.7M each, the conservative price levels owing to strict KYC from the sellers.   A US - China trade ‘truce’ will excite the dry market after talks between the two nations took place this week in Busan, South Korea. Tariffs will be trimmed but crucially for panamax owners, China have agreed to buy 12 million metric tonnes of soybeans through January and 25 million tonnes annually for the next 3 years. This soybean deal is one thing, but the wider market will welcome easing tensions and general stability between the two nations. In the standout transaction of the week, ultramax CMB BRUEGEL (63K DWT Shin Kasado 2021) was bought by Meghna for USD 32.8M, this follows up these buyers’ purchase of DRAFTDODGER (66K DWT Mitsui 2016) at USD 26.2M last month.

Seasonally stronger crude markets, combined with an increasing US sanction effort against Russia has buoyed the tanker earnings market as selected owners are reporting VLCC rates breaching the USD 100K/day mark. This push in rates is expected to filter into the rest of the sector, which will likely keep second hand values looking strong towards the end of the year. ASYAD have offset their recent spending spree with the sale of scrubber fitted VLCC SAIQ (299K DWT Universal 2011) for USD 57M with TC attached until April at USD 41K/day. This is while another similar vintage VLCC scrubber fitted NAVE CONSTELLATION (296K DWT Dalian 2010) was sold for USD 52.5M, showing there is plenty of demand for this vintage of VLCC at these levels, despite their age. Elsewhere MRs PTI HUDSON/NILE (49K DWT SPP 2016) were sold to Chinese buyers with TC attached at USD 33M.   A busy week across the dry market sees market players jostling for position and tonnage. Q3 rates remained consistent and there is widespread optimism for the years ahead, so one could speculate the bottom of the market from a values perspective is firmly in the rearview mirror. A notable variable that will need to be dealt with in 2026 however, is vessel deliveries. Certain subsectors are in line for high growth, particularly Kamsarmax and Ultramax, so buyers will be hoping for some opportunity here. In the standout transaction this week, EBE Belgium purchased scrubber fitted Newcastlemax BULK SAO PAOLO (208K DWT New Times 2020) for USD 72.75M. There has been a recent spike in demand for Newcastlemax units as owners look to take advantage of longer employment opportunities on offer for these vessels.

Buyers expecting modern tanker values to drop have their hopes firmly dashed by now. The recent rush of modern tanker transactions has continued with a headline deal between Metrostar and Delta Tankers, the latter purchasing suezmax sisters CRUDE ZEPHYRUS/LEVANTE (156K DWT New Times 2021) for USD 156M. This is interesting as it represents an age of asset which would have been ordered for substantially less than it is worth today, while having had almost 5 years of trading in mostly strong tanker markets. Representing a very understandable decision to take money off the table on desirable assets, this sale could encourage others to do the same. Elsewhere, PNSC have been busy acquiring Scrubber fitted STAVANGER POSEIDON (50K DWT Hyundai Vietnam 2020) for USD 44.15M, and scrubber fitted aframax pair NAFSIKA (112K DWT Sumitomo 2022) / LORAX (109K DWT Sumitomo 2022) for USD 75M each.   While the China-USA port fee battle has caused more than its fair share of headaches this week, it is unlikely to have a notable impact on the overall market. Sales in the dry market appear to have taken a brief pause, perhaps while the market makes sense of the new rulings, but it is worth remembering that overall sentiment is high and many sales candidates are reflecting this in their price ask.

The modern transactions this week have taken the tanker market by surprise, setting fresh valuation benchmarks across several segments. The scrubber fitted ECO BEL AIR/BEVERLY HILLS (157K DWT Hyundai 2019) were sold en bloc to Performance for USD 152M, marking the first modern suezmax sale since the NORDIC THUNDER (157K DWT Hyundai 2017) achieved USD 66M in June 2025. Scrubber fitted VLCC LANDBRIDGE PROSPERITY (308K DWT Dalian 2016) changed hands for USD 85M.   In the dry bulk market, liquidity remains strong for both modern and older tonnage. The scrubber fitted MINERAL SHOU GANG INTERNATIONAL (206K DWT Qingdao Yangfan 2019) was sold to Chinese buyers for USD 65.5M, adding to the recent wave of modern newcastlemax sales. Demand for modern ultramaxes continues to stay high with scrubber fitted IMABARI QUEEN (60K DWT Sanoyas 2016) being sold at USD 23.7M, a price that appears favourable for buyers British Bulkers. In the handysize sector, BEN 1 (35K DWT Jiangdong 2015) changed hands for USD 14.7M.

Mixed sentiment this week across the larger crude sizes, and a range of opinion on the strength of Q4 earnings. On the back of the recent rally, where VLCCs have seen spot rates of around USD 100K/day, it seems bizarre to question earnings but softer FFAs and a quiet Chinese market with the beginning of Golden Week has people thinking on the resilience of this crude market. On second hand tonnage, modern, large transactions remain at a premium, but it is the clean space that is picking up once again. MRs enjoyed plenty of liquidity at the beginning of the year, and this looks to be returning as prices appear to have bottomed out. T MATTERHORN (47K DWT Iwagi Zosen 2010) sold for USD 20M, with SSDD due in Dec 25 and TC attached until Q1 26.   The dry market appears to be flourishing; values have corrected upwards across the sector very rapidly and there is a healthy amount of buying interest across each subsector. While there are some submarket fundamentals that warrant this buoyant outlook, other subsectors are seeing values increase despite potentially testing times ahead. To this point, the ultramax sector has a reported 179 ships to be delivered in 2026, the highest number in a decade, but values and demand for candidates are both still very strong. This week ANDIAMO (63K DWT Shin Kasado 2019) sold for USD 30.5M, against last done 2019 ultramax MONA LISA (63K DWT Imabari 2019) at USD 29.5M back in August.

Liquidity in the tanker market is still an issue, with modern units particularly difficult to come by. That said, sentiment is buoyant, leading some to even wonder if perhaps we are at the beginning of a supercycle. Sentiment, however, is one thing, and owners know there are plenty of deliveries and much potential uncertainty ahead. In the afra sector, YINGHAO CONFIDENCE (107K DWT Tsuneishi 2010) was sold for USD 36M.  Headlines were stolen this week with Asyad purchasing scrubber fitted Newcastlemax trio BULK SANTIAGO/SANDEFJORD/SHENZHEN (207K DWT New Times 2019/2020) en bloc at USD 209M, with delivery in early 2026. Newcastlemax units have experienced a sharp spike in demand over recent months, with a handful of deals concluded recently and enquiry still high. The dry sector is seeing a general rise in value, particularly illustrated in the Ultramax sector where sales are beating last dones. BULK CASTOR (66K DWT Mitsui 2015) was sold for USD 24.2M and BEAUTY LILY (63K China Shipping Jiangsu 2015) sold at USD 22.25, showing the 10-year-old benchmarks for the sector and the current delta between Japanese and Chinese built units.

The story on tanker market remains largely the same this week, though with increasing anticipation of a strong period of earnings for crude tonnage. Modern units remain at a premium, shown in the sale of LR2 SILVERSTONE (113K DWT SWS 2025), bought by Transpetrol for USD 75M. Liquidity is increasing at the other end of the age curve with OLYMPIC SEA/SKY (104K DWT SWS 2008) being sold at USD $29.5M each.   Several ships taking offers this month has provided the dry market with somewhat of a recalibration. Firstly, in the ultramax sector, BULK CASTOR (66K DWT Mitsui 2015) took offers on Tuesday and is rumoured to have seen levels in the mid 24Ms. The final figure is likely to exceed this, given the reported sale of scrubber fitted AFRICAN CHEETAH (66K DWT Mitsui 2014) at USD 24M, following the same bidding process. Capesize WAKAYAMA MARU (181K DWT Koyo 2013) was bought by Asyad for USD 37M, setting the new benchmark for a non eco Japanese cape. Spot rates across the smaller sizes are at similar levels to the peaks of last year, and comparative asset prices suggest there could be some further upside for owners in what is now a seller’s market.

Despite the ongoing support from the underlying freight markets, tanker SnP activity remains subdued. Modern assets remain particularly challenging to transact with a resilient bid/offer spread, while values of older tonnage appear to have bottomed out, leading sellers to hold back and reassess. In the mid-aged VLCC market, the scrubber-fitted FPMC KNIGHT (301K DWT Universal 2011) was sold for USD 55M.  Dry cargo markets are also yielding better-than-expected returns for owners. Although we are witnessing higher second-hand activity including more modern vessels changing hands, current rates are similarly consolidating sellers' expectations.  This week, Precious Shipping secured the wide beam ultramax sisters JAL KALPAVRIKSH/KALPATARU (66K DWT, Mitsui 2021) for USD 32.55 million each.

Only a trickle of tanker sales to report in the first week back since the official end of summer. Overall, the underlying factor remains, particularly across more modern tonnage, that asset values are on the high side compared to current achievable TC rates. On spot however, there is a mixed story with VLCCs ending the week strongly, while products experience more variable conditions. In the Aframax market, scrubber fitted BLUE PRINCE (109K DWT Hudong Zhonghua 2009) sold for USD 32.7M.    A seemingly extremely busy week in the dry market. This is likely due in part to many returning from summer holidays, with broker channels and information streams up and running once again, but also perhaps a symptom of the overall perception that brighter times are on the horizon for the dry market, with the hope that the TC market will mirror the current buoyant spot earnings. The majority of sales have occurred in the 10+yo space, with investors sensing now is the time to strike for a potential asset play. In the only modern transaction, open hatch LILAC HARMONY (38K DWT Tsuneishi Cebu 2020) sold for USD 25.05M.

Sales activity in the tanker sector was limited this week, with the only reported transaction being the sale of the MR SEAWAYS MIA (49k dwt HMD 2008) at $16.5 million. Despite the subdued volume, the deal underscores continued liquidity in the MR segment and suggests a slight firming in values for MRs of this age.  On the dry side, activity remains robust. Notable sales include the HERUN ZHEJIANG (181k dwt SWS 2017), sold for $48 million - marking the second eco Capesize sale recorded this year. Eco Ultramaxes continue to change hands with Belships rumoured to offload the four Chinese blt units BELATLANTIC/BELINDA/BELMONT/BELSOUTH* (63k dwt Jiangsu Hantong 2016/2015*) for $83.6 million en bloc to Singaporean Buyers.

These summer periods tend to give time for reflection for those in the tanker markets, and, generally speaking, this summer is no different. Crude earnings have dropped off since a spike in June, and product rates are languishing. This has resulted in a well-documented reshuffling in the products market, with very healthy liquidity in the MR space, particularly in the c.15-year-old range where values appear to have hit a floor. This sentiment seems to have spread into the Aframax/LR2 space which is attracting added attention from opportunist investors. Scrubber fitted BLUE PRINCE (109K DWT Hudong Zhonghua 2009) was sold this week for USD 32.25M, as part of three vessels sold in this size range.    Dry cargo charter brokers hoping to enjoy their summer break have been glued to their desks this week in a flurry of activity in the charter market. Healthy returns are spurring owners into action to capture these earnings in what has mostly been an uninspiring sector over recent times. The supramax – ultramax sector has seen a bump in SNP activity this week, as pricing has fallen into line for investors. CP CHONGQING (63K DWT Chengxi 2016) was sold this week for USD 21M, in line with other similar units sold. Elsewhere, scrubber fitted Capesize PACIFIC WEST (175K DWT Jinhai 2012) sold for USD 23.2M, in line with last done similar unit scrubber fitted GOLDEN ZHOUSHAN (175K DWT Jinhai 2011) sold at USD 22M earlier this month.

KMG of Kazakhstan are reported to have bought scrubber fitted LR2 resale pair LAMU / DUNE (113K DWT COSCO Yangzhou 2025) at USD 72M each, in line with non scrub LR2 HESPERIA TIDE (115K DWT Zhoushan Changhong 2025), bought last week by Polembros for USD 70M. In the MR sector, despite the less than exciting rates on offer, buyers are still seeing value in 15–17-year-old units. There has been a large amount of liquidity in this age bracket with buyers taking a chance that those bumper spot earnings seen last year will return.    The dry market is showing resilience, with healthy returns across the sector. These elevated rates are already fuelling an increase in buying interest, though sellers will be keen to extract as much value as possible and units will be priced accordingly. It was a busy week in the Kamsarmax sector, seeing five sales. Scrubber fitted ULTRA LION (81K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2015) was sold for a better than anticipated price of USD 24.8M, signalling a potential recovery in pricing for this sector, which corrected so sharply towards the end of 2024.

The pre summer rush appears to have been short lived, with only a handful of reported sales this week. Standing out, however, is resale LR2 HESPERIA TIDE (115K DWT Zhoushan Changhong 2025), bought by Polembros for USD 70M, adding to the 4 other LR2 units they have on order at the same yard. Old VLCCs continue to see relatively high levels of enquiry, with CITY OF TOKYO (303K DWT Universal 2004) selling at a firm USD 41.5M, despite earnings being in the usual summer lull. Elsewhere, the LR1 KOI (74K DWT STX 2010) was sold to Greek interests at USD 23.3M, following a sharp correction in values in this sector.   Usually, the excitement and volatility are reserved for spot cape earnings, however, this week all sizes across dry are enjoying a rush in spot returns. Rates particularly in the panamax sector are firming sharply, sitting at USD 15k/day, having spent the majority of the year closer to USD 10K/day. This will likely disincentivise sellers of tonnage, frustrating buyers who are now seeing the price asks of potential candidates rising. In the Kamsarmax sector, the attractiveness of yard is plain to see this week with sale of the Tess 82 ULTRA PUMA (81K DWT Tsuneishi 2016) selling at USD 25M versus a younger yet Chinese built AVICL ATERMIS (81K DWT Jiangsu Jinling 2019) being sold at USD 24.5M.

MR tankers continue to be the focus of investors with values having stabilised in recent weeks, following a notable correction since the peak of summer 2024. Sellers have done extremely well over the last few years in terms of earnings, so despite the fact they are not selling at the peak, units are leaving fleets likely having repaid their initial investment and more. PTI HUANG HE (50K DWT SPP 2016) was bought by Greek buyers, which will help price units in this range.   The dry market  has had a bumper week in activity but the story remains the same. That is, there is healthy liquidity across older units but a lack of supply on more modern ships. The unusually high amount of activity may be attributed to the incoming summer holidays, with much of Northern Europe taking time away from the desk over the coming weeks. A significant range of sizes transacted this week gives little away in terms of buying preference, which could support the narrative that buyers are seeking tonnage to position themselves for potentially better markets over the next year. Interestingly, capesize GOLDEN ZHOUSHAN (175K DWT Jinhai 2011) sold for USD 22M, below many price expectations.

The tanker market has absorbed recent news developments and geopolitical tensions with little disruption and volatility. There was a brief spike in VLCC spot rates, however this has since fallen away with the market normalising. This week, Yasa acquired scrubber fitted VLCC C.SPIRIT (313K DWT HHI Gunsan 2013) for USD 67.5M, against last done 2013 scrubber fitted VLCC CAPTAIN X KYRIAKOU (300K DWT HHI Ulsan 2013) sold in September 2024 for USD 80M. Elsewhere MRs continue to change hands given the recent correction on pricing with 4 further sales this week. Most notably, NORD OCEANIA (49K DWT Onomichi 2018) sold for USD 36.5M, levels that this time last year restricted buyers to non eco tonnage.   Emerging news of a US-China trade deal being struck will have not only the global stock markets rallying but could also provide some life to the steady yet unexciting dry market. Earnings have been stable for the most part, aside from the usual capesize rollercoaster, with many touting a stronger 2026. This trade agreement could be the first green shoots of the next prosperous period for dry owners. Brave maritime continue their run on Japanese tonnage this week as they picked up ARIES SAKURA (39K DWT Shin Kurushima 2020) for just under USD 26M. Elsewhere, scrubber fitted capesize PACIFIC EAST (176K DWT SWS 2012) sold for USD 27.5M.

Headlines in the tanker market have been stolen by two rare modern transactions this week. On the VLCC front DHT reported their acquisition of the the scrubber fitted VLCC PAPALEMOS 320K DWT HYUNDAI 2018 for USD 107 million while Delta Tankers have reportedly purchased the NORDIC THUNDER 157K DWT HYUNDAI 2017 for USD 65 million. Both transactions setting some welcomed benchmarks across both crude segments in an ever-evolving geopolitical landscape. In the product sector ADNOC have sold their LR1 sisters BANI YAS and YAMILAH-III 75K DWT STX 2010/2011 for USD 22.2 million each. A notable decrease from the last comparable transaction of FLAGSHIP WILLOW 75K DWT SPP 2012 at USD 27.8 million in February 2025.   Dry markets were equally active this week with CMB selling their Newcastlemax MINERAL HIROSHIGE 208K DWT IMABARI 2019 basis a forward delivery for USD 65 million while the scrubber fitted Capesize BULK GINZA 182K DWT IMABARI 2020 was sold to Genco for USD 64 million. Lastly In the handysize sector the NY TRADER III 39K DWT JIANGMEN NANYANG 2016 was sold by clients of Nisshin to a European buyer for USD 16.8 million.

Almost a clean sweep for MRs this week as the sector remains the focus of second-hand tanker buyers. This has been the story on tanker S&P throughout the last months primarily due to the recent correction in pricing, but also the anticipated deliveries to take place this year. Most of the MRs sold this week are SS due, indicating sellers will take market offerings in order to avoid spending more on SS due units. Scrubber fitted NORDTOKYO (50K DWT Samsung HI Geoje 2020) was sold for USD 38.2M, against last done scrubber fitted EDEN (49K HMD 2020) at USD 40M back in March of this year.   A much quieter than usual week on dry, where liquidity has not been an issue so far this year. The underlying story, however, remains the same where majority older ships are transacted amongst the rare modern sale. Values have been sliding gradually against the consistent yet uninspiring earnings market, seen in scrubber fitted BRIGHT PEGASUS (82K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2013) which sold for USD 17.8M this week, against scrubber fitted BRIGHT GEMINI (82K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2013) from same sellers which sold for USD 23M back in September 2024.

As much of the market descended on Oslo for Norshipping the story in the tanker second hand market remained the same, with MRs still providing the majority of activity. Values appear to be stabilising, having corrected significantly from the heights of the market during summer last year. Torm continued the sell out of their older units, with Chemsea acquiring TORM DISCOVERER/VOYAGER (45k dwt Brodotogir 2008) for USD 34M en bloc. Elsewhere, Navios provided the market with a new benchmark in the Afra sector, acquiring resale sisters (115k dwt Zhoushan Changhong 2026) for USD xs 67M each, from Pro Tanker Investment.  Similarly this week was not one of great change for the dry bulk market. Rates on the smaller and medium size tonnage are unremarkable, and capesize returns have calmed down somewhat after a recent spike. This is resulting in a consistent story for the second-hand space, with occasional modern transactions and mostly c.15-year-old ships being sold into Far Eastern buyers. In the one modern transaction this week, Greek buyers picked up scrubber fitted Kamsarmax AOM SOPHIE II (81k dwt Sanoyas 2020) for USD 31.5M, in line with last done units. In the Capsesize sector, Costamare bought IMPERATOR AUSTRALIS (176k dwt Shanghai Jiangnan Changxing 2012) for USD 25.5M, from Japanese sellers.

MR sales continue to provide liquidity to the tanker second hand market. Despite some recent stability on values basis last dones, it would not be surprising to see values correct further amid significant deliveries to come throughout the rest of 2025. At the older end of the spectrum, PS CAPRI (49K DWT STX Jinhae 2011) sold for USD 18M, in line with last done GLENDA MELODY (49K HMD 2011) at USD 17.9M. Younger units NORD JEWEL*/JOY (49K JMU 2018) *scrubber fitted, sold for just under 74M en bloc to Paragon Mobility, in line with last done en bloc transaction PS ATENE/MILANO (49K DWT HMD 2018).    Further question marks over the legality and implementation of President Trump’s sweeping tariffs this week mean a similar story of uncertainty in the shipping markets. That said, the dry market remains consistent and active, although unexciting. Competition is still fierce for large handy bulkers, seen in BUNUN ORCHID (37K DWT I-S Shipyard 2021) bought by Stealth for USD 25M. Elsewhere, Indian buyers acquired the Kamsarmax trio CL GRACE/MONA/TIFFANY (81K DWT Yangfan 2012/2013) for USD 45M en bloc.

The Product sector continues to see a healthy amount of activity with three MR sales to report this week. The GLENDA MELODY 47K DWT HMD 2011 l) was sold for $17.9 million to after nearly a year on the market. Enquiry levels for older vessels remains strong in the Crude sector with GMS being the reported buyers of the scrubber-fitted VLCC M. STAR 314K DWT KAWASAKI 2008 for $46 million, still offering a compelling exit opportunity for owners of similar vintaged VL’s.   Far eastern players continue to drive activity in the dry bulk sector with KEY ACTION (82K DWT TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN) ending up in Chinese hands for $15.1 million - a price reflective of the segment’s subdued earnings experienced throughout this year. Conversely, modern tonnage remains scarce, compelling buyers to compete for the limited candidates available.

Sellers of tankers are not pressed to sell, and it seems that eventually one will find a buyer in spite of current high asset values. Long time sales candidate NEW NAXOS (299K DWT Universal 2003) has changed hands this week for USD 33M, beating last done AUSTRALIS (299K DWT Universal 2003) which sold earlier in the year at USD 28M. Despite the healthy returns available in the earnings market, these levels provide an attractive exit point for owners, exhibited by Teekay selling suezmax pair ASPEN SPIRIT/CASCADE SPIRIT (156K DWT Rongsheng 2009) for USD 37.5M each to Nigerian buyers. The story is not quite so rosy in the products market, where we continue to see price correction. SEAWAYS CITRON/SEAWAYS FRONTIER (49K DWT HMD 2007) sold for USD 14M each, a far cry away from the USD c.25M they were seeking last summer.   The dry market continues its unremarkable run this week, that said in these uncertain times, owners will be very satisfied with the reliable returns they are seeing. HMM are back in a purchasing mood with the acquisition of scrubber fitted Newcastlemax LUISE OLDENDORFF (207K DWT Hyundai 2015) for USD 51M, otherwise it appears that the most likely buyers for second hand bulk carriers are located in China. In the capesize sector THALASSINI AVRA (182K DWT Universal 2011) sold for USD 29M, to Chinese buyers.

The search for renewed benchmarks in the tanker market has been a fruitless task for a while now, however, this looks to be changing at least in the MR space. An Increased liquidity is driving the ongoing value correction, indicating more activity in the segment as these corrected levels continue to attract the attention of opportunistic players. Pumproom MR ANNA M (47K DWT Iwagi Zosen 2010) sold in xs of USD 17M, almost 35% less than what she could have expected this time last year.  There remains healthy activity across the dry market despite a somewhat dreary outlook for the rest of 2025. Most will be well placed to ride out this current storm, with rates remaining comfortably above OPEX for the time being. The next few months could see an increase in buying interest, as buyers look to position themselves to catch potential predicted upside in 2026-2027. That said, modern tonnage remains at a premium and these buyers will likely need to beat last done on these units in order to secure tonnage. In the modern ultramax space, scrubber fitted AQUAVITA LIME (63K DWT Nantong Xiangyu 2021) sold for USD 30.5M.

The VLCC space continues to provide liquidity to the tanker second hand market amid a strong spot market earnings environment. China’s buying appetite for VLCCs is also showing no respite, as LAYLA (317K DWT Hyundai 2007) sold for USD 46.75M. Chinese buyers are also being linked to at least 2 of the 3x scrubber fitted VLCCs sold from CMB.Tech this week, HAKATA/HAKONE (302K DWT Universal 2010) & IRIS (314K DWT HHI 2012) which generated a profit for the Brussels listed owner of USD 96.7M, though no official sale price has been disclosed. In the face of weakening, yet historically still above average, rates and an influx of newbuildings to come this year, there is an ongoing correction in MR values. In this space, CELSIUS PHILADELPHIA/PORTSMOUTH (50K DWT Jiangsu Newyangzi 2021) were sold to IMS with TC attached at USD 35.5M each.   In the face of widely reported bearish sentiment, the dry market is delivering solid yet unremarkable returns. The all too familiar feeling that no one is pressed to sell remains a barrier to entry for opportunist buyers but will provide comfort to owners and investors with skin already in the game alike. That said, there is still a fair level of liquidity ranging across sizes and subsectors. This week, Turkish buyers were reported on the sale of ANSAC MOON BEAR (33K DWT Shin Kurushima 2017)*Open Hatch at USD 18.7M.

Tanker headlines this week were stolen by scrubber fitted VLCCs LANDBRIDGE GLORY/WISDOM 307K DWT Dalian 2019/20, which sold to Oman Shipping co (Asyad) for USD 205M. This timing is seen as somewhat curious for Chinese built VLCCs given uncertainty over USTR and the evolving, yet potentially easing, tariff situation. MRs it appears, are close to bottoming out, seen in SS/DD due TAMIAT NAVIGATOR (46K DWT HMD 2010) at USD 18M, a unit that would have transacted closer to USD 30M this time last year.   Easter holidays are likely to have had an impact on the lower-than-average number of dry sales this week, although this is coinciding with fewer firm enquiries in the market on the back of the much-reported growing uncertainty and general geopolitical instability. That said, rates remain consistently above opex levels, though doing little to excite potential investors. In a rare transaction of a modern handy, NORD ABIDJAN (37K DWT Minaminippon 2020) *OHBS was sold for USD 25.5M.

In a turbulent week across global markets, at least tanker S&P remains predictable. There seems to be no end in sight for Chinese appetite for older VLCCs, with eye watering sums being paid for ships close to 20 years old.
