Mid USD 40Ms in a normal market would typically buy you a c.10 year old unit, let alone 18 year old DD due EUROHOPE (306K DWT Daewoo 2007). Chinese buyers are leading the way this year in terms of S&P buying activity, however with the emerging USA-China trade war one can only speculate how the next few months will pan out. Elsewhere MR values appear to have stabilised following a rapid correction over the last few quarters, with PS ATENE (49K DWT HMD 2018) selling in line with her sisters at USD RGN 37M.   Extremely high levels of activity this week in the Dry sector, possibly as a result of recent rallies causing buyers to act, sensing an opportunity. Subsequently though, these rallies in general have cooled off. Furthermore, escalation of the Trump tariffs and the emergence of a trade war involving the leading global economies will potentially leave these buyers with an anxious few months ahead. That said, at least in terms of port calls, the largest dry bulk carriers will be sheltered from the proposed USTR, minimising the impact on this sector. Unfortunately, the 90-day delay announced by President Trump rather kicks the can down the road on what impact USTR and tariffs will have on the market. In the standout transaction of the week, Indonesian buyers Jholin bought modern Ultramax trio OAKGATE/MAPLEGATE/DIONISIS (60K/63K DWT Oshima/Iwagi Zosen/I-S 2018/2019) for USD 32M each.

Despite only two tanker sales to report this week, plenty of discussions are ongoing. Uncertainty is of course all around and owners are contemplating their next moves. However, there is no sense of urgency to buy and values for Chinese built tankers remain very vulnerable in lieu of USTR and how that plays out in the end. Several Korean tankers built 2016-2018 are privately touted for sale but the bid/ask spread is quite wide at the moment.    Values for MRs and Handytankers continue to slide as seen by the sale of EASTERLY CANYON 36K DWT HMD 2009 at $16m. In comparison, a sistership was sold one year ago for $22m, representing almost 30% decline in one year.  In the dry sector we continue to see increased liquidity for older ships. 14 sales across the board with the bulk of transactions within Supramax and Kamsarmax segments; mostly Chinese buyers for older and non-eco vessels, transactions that reaffirm weakening in asset values. Western sellers are sitting on the fence or taking this opportunity to dispose of their older ships. A notable transaction in the illiquid Babycape segment, is JUBILANT DEVOTION 117K DWT 2016 SANOYAS sold to Alberta for $26.5m.

A growing sense of uncertainty is gripping shipping markets with very little visibility and clarity offered by the US administration on the various trade policy proposals tabled over the past couple of weeks. Market players are opting for a wait and see approach in hope to gain some additional comfort and plan their next moves accordingly. A sentiment that has had a direct impact on both second hand and newbuilding activity with a limited number of transactions to report. On the product tanker front, the PS MILANO (Abt 50k dwt Hyundai 2018) was again committed this week at Usd 37m after failing to materialise at similar levels earlier this year.   The dry cargo markets have seen one additional Newcastlemax changing hands, with the Japanese controlled GLOBAL COMMANDER (Abt 208k dwt Universal 2010) being sold at Usd 31.7m basis surveys due in June this year. Bringing the tally, in what would be considered a relatively illiquid segment, to a total of 6 units transacted so far this year.

A rare modern MR transaction took place this week, in turn highlighting the recent sharp correction that has taken place in this sector. Scrubber fitted EDEN (49K dwt HMD 2020)*SSDD due was sold for USD 40M, a correction particularly well illustrated against the scrubber fitted 2014 blt Torm-Sinokor vessels sold in Q3 last year at USD 42.5m. Otherwise, vintage VLCCs are still proving popular, with NEW NAXOS (299K dwt Universal 2003) being sold at USD 33.5M.    An unremarkable week across dry, with the recently rallying capesize rates dipping to below USD 20k/day, a reminder to market players that despite some recent optimism, the outlook for 2025 is still very mixed. Sticking to the script of the recent times, mostly older ships are transacted this week, but with the exception of ATLANTIC BRAVE (33K dwt Shin Kurishima 2016) being sold for a below market USD 17.8M, even with a reported WW delivery range.

No real rhyme or rhythm to the activity in the tanker sector this week. Perhaps quite symptomatic of the current environment whereby, aside from modern units, no obvious plays are presenting themselves. Yes, there is some opportunity for high margin trades, however this tends to come with future sanction risk. Aside from that, the market has a bloated feel to it with owners’ ideas still on the high side. MARLIN AMBER (49K DWT COMEC 2015) at sub-USD 30M is a continuation of the MR values correction, but buyers are still waiting for further reductions before the space becomes top priority.   Despite a buoyant week in terms of transactions, the underlying story remains the same. That story being of course that younger ships still very much in demand (but hard to come by), while older units provide the liquidity. Capesize rates continue to rally, hitting their highest levels since November last year. The rally has trickled down into the smaller sizes, providing some much-needed optimism. Chinese buyers were once again showing their unwavering appetite for tonnage, taking 4x Panamax/Kamsarmax from ArcelorMittal. It was also a busy week in the handy sector, helped by the en bloc transaction of ERHAN/DOGAN/ORHAN (38K/35K dwt SPP 2013) for USD 45M.

Despite a relatively busy week, the transactions tell a story of the difficulties plaguing the current tanker markets. Pricing clarity has been hard to come by, particularly on older tonnage where trading history and KYC scrutiny form a key part of the deal. Such is the uncertainty on pricing, that we see 2x VLCCs sold, USD 10M difference in price despite only being one year apart in age. Also laid bare are the changes seen in the modern MR space. Empire Navigation bought Scrubber fitted NORD SWIFT (49K DWT STX 2015) for USD 33.25M, marking a significant correction from last done transactions in Summer last year where comparable units were transacted at xs USD 42M. Buyers can still be found on older tonnage too with TORM offloading 3x older units for USD 15M each, lower than their original ideas when initially marketed, but still at extremely healthy levels for 20-year-old MRs.  A mixture of headlines this week as momentum and confidence are being built in the earnings market, represented in cape futures eclipsing USD 20K/day, while also one of shipping’s most influential players John Fredriksen turned his back on the segment entirely. Fredriksen sold his 40.8% stake in Golden Ocean to Saverys family lead CMB.Tech, ensuring the company remains in experienced shipping hands, while giving him an exit at a premium. Overall, sentiment in the dry market remains cautious, with industry eyes and hopes pinned mostly on Chinese demand for shoots of genuine recovery. Transaction wise, scrubber fitted DREAM STAR (81K DWT Tadostsu 2014) was sold from Japanese control to Greeks Brave Maritime for USD 20.5M. Elsewhere, ss/dd freshly passed KMARIN OSLO (63K DWT Jiangsu New Hantong 2015) sold for USD 22M.

Tanker transactions gave some clarity to pricing this week, firstly with a significant suezmax transaction and a new benchmark on 15-year-old MRs. Scrubber fitted GOLDWAY/DIAMONDWAY (154K DWT SUNGDONG 2016) were sold for USD 136M en bloc to NAT, the first transaction on 2016 blt suezmax since 2023. Product sector continues to see increasing popularity, with buyers sensing an opportunity off the back of the recent price corrections. NH SIRI/ERLE (49K DWT HMD 2010) were bought en bloc at USD 45M, effectively pricing a 15-year-old MR at USD 22.5M, a far cry from Q3 last year where similar units would have been priced closer to thirty.  The dry market is experiencing the usual seasonal bounce, however, owners and charterers are still unsure given the ever changing geopolitical landscape. This has resulted in an uncertain TC market, with few players willing to commit to extended employment in light of this increased uncertainty. Overall on a second hand basis, the situation remains the same, with the majority of activity limited to older tonnage, and modern tonnage very desirable for prospective buyers. In the standout transaction of the week, HMM picked up scrubber fitted Newcastlemax ORIENTAL DRAGON (207K DWT IMABARI 2014) for USD 49.2M.

MR tankers have largely been ignored by SnP players so far this year with subdued rates leading Sellers to gradually correct expectations in hope to entice any potential Buyers. An exercise that seems to bear its fruit this week with a notable bump in reported transactions, setting some welcomed benchmarks in the product space. HANSA OSLO (51K DWT STX JINHAE 2007) was sold for USD 17.2M, a drop of almost 25% on what she was asking in Q3’24, but interestingly still higher than the USD 15M that was paid for her when she was bought in 2022.  Dry bulk is still providing an avenue for investment where willing sellers are found, however, this remains mostly on the older end of the spectrum. Owners who have ridden out this seasonal downturn are seeing a rise in sentiment as China’s imported iron ore consumption has rebounded after the holidays, while other sub sectors will hope for a similar rebound in fortunes. Newcastlemaxes continue to change hands this week with Berge Bulk acquiring the “HL FRONTIER” (Abt 207k dwt Universal 2010) at USD 32.5m. Bringing the tally, in what is usually a very illiquid segment, to a total of 4 units transacted so far this year.

Very good - slightly rephrased     The en bloc transaction of two scrubber fitted Enesel LR2s ELYITS/KAVAFIS (113K dwt SWS 2024/2023) to Centrofin for USD 143M grabbed the attention of the market this week. The levels paid, despite being well above historical average, represent a sharp correction in value given the last done scrubber fitted LR2 STI LILY (109K dwt New Times 2019) was transacted at similar levels in October 2024. This does show however, that would be sellers are increasingly willing to transact  in light of growing uncertainty and increasing unpredictability across the tanker market. Older afras are too proving popular, with handsome returns available on loading Urals crude in the Baltic.     The much-anticipated post Lunar New Year bounce has yet to materialise on dry, as capesize spot rates hover close to two-year lows. This will not panic owners for now, who are busy assessing a daily changing environment as talk of tariffs dominate the political landscape. Transactions are for the most part limited to older tonnage, with ECO units still highly desirable across the market. In the largest sector by size, Berge Bulk bought scrubber fitted ore carrier NSU INSPIRE (250K DWT NAMURA 2011) for USD 37M.
Moderate

The tanker market finds itself in a strange position. There is bullish sentiment on large crude tonnage, however it is yet to manifest itself into values and S&P activity. It makes a good investment proposal at a time where confusion reigns across the market, however it is hard to see those with modern ECO tankers surrendering their positions to buyers. Non-ECO tonnage on the other hand, is plentiful in supply with many motivated sellers in the market. Across products it appears that the recent boom is very much over, something that will be crystallised should ongoing second-hand discussions materialise.    The Lunar New Year is a milestone many in the dry market have been waiting for. There is a lot riding on the next few months, which many feel will set the tone for the rest of the year. Despite the holidays, Chinese buyers were still active on Capes, buying CAPE HERON/HAWK (177K DWT MITSUI/NAMURA 2005/2006) en bloc for USD 30M. Earnings in general are still sluggish, even with the panamax market showing signs of life, but there is some way to go if it is to have a meaningful effect on values. For now, the dry story remains as it was with an overall bearish sentiment for 2025.

Uncertainty in the tanker market has made and lost fortunes over the years, and is generally welcomed, however at the moment there is a sense that you can have too much of a good thing. With the Far East celebrating Lunar New Year, the European market has been rife with rumour as a fresh wave of new buyers emerge to exploit potentially lucrative trades in the aframax sector. This has led to a sense of confusion over values, which had been correcting after a period of stubborn resistance in the wake of an illiquid 2024. Demand for older tankers too seems to be picking up, with demand focused from the Far East – seen in VLCC ALRAYA (300K DWT IHI 2005) being bought by Chinese buyers at USD 43M. Even market veterans will scarcely believe a 20-year-old VLCC can be worth over double its scrap value, it seems, this buoyant values period is far from over.   The dry market is slipping into an unprecedented scenario. Granted, seasonality can be blamed for uninspiring earnings right now, but the overall story remains the same in the sense owners are waiting for a supply/demand shock to change their fortunes for 2025. What gives this market its unprecedented nature, is the fact that despite a sustained low earnings environment, owners for the most part are financially sound and have less exposure to lenders than they would have done in recent low markets (2016 for example). This creates less opportunity for buyers to use the prevailing conditions to their advantage in playing hardball with sellers. Chronos offloading their fleet this week dominates the sales this week, but also shows there is still demand for non eco tonnage and not just the highly sought after eco units. Elsewhere, CAPE FRIENDSHIP (185K DWT KAWASAKI 2005) sold for USD 16M, a correction of almost 25% on what the ship was marketed for in Q3 24.

Aside from the unusually busy vintage Panamax sector, likely due to falling rates and abundance of older tonnage still operating, the story of this week is the benchmark set for modern Ultramax tonnage going forward. NORD MAGELLAN (63K DWT IWAGI 2020)*SS/DD due April 25, was sold to Bangladeshi buyers Megha for USD 29.2M, a correction from last done 2020 built ERIN MANX (63K DWT TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN 2020) at USD 32.5M late last year. There will be a number of prospective investors watching this sector closely, particularly with a high number of deliveries expected this year.   The tanker market has thrown investors and owners into an interesting and unpredictable scenario, following the further sanctions introduced as one of outgoing president Biden’s final acts. It lit the touch paper for TC demand, as owners rushed to secure ships but much of this excitement seems to be short lived. The reality of the situation is that non eco tonnage will still be at the mercy of buyers, despite a flurry of transactions this week riding the positive sentiment. Euronav offloaded a quartet of suezmaxes, a shrewd move given ships of this age traditionally do not have much trading life left. Interesting to note all transactions this week are non eco tonnage. In the languishing product sector, NORD HIMALAYA (49K DWT ONOMICHI 2011) sold for USD 25.5M, a ship that would have been worth comfortably over USD 30M 6 months ago.

Sweeping sanctions on tanker tonnage has drastically altered the prospects of the fleet for 2025. Where in the first weeks of the year there was little TC interest, charterers are now rushing to secure ships on long period. Before the sanctions were introduced, it seemed that the overdue correction in values would have completely shifted the valuation story across the sector however, now the landing looks a lot softer than it did just a week ago. Values are still correcting for the time being, though it is now looking likely that they will settle higher than previously expected. That said, some key size and age ranges are still awaiting the benchmark transaction. One such benchmark has been set in the aframax sector, with AMAX AVENUE/ANTHEM (115K DWT SAMSUNG 2010/11) being sold en bloc at USD 79M, pricing the ships below USD 40M, with last done NISSOS DELOS (115K DWT SAMSUNG 2012) at USD 45.3M late last year. Things could quickly change however with the incoming presidential turnover in the USA next week.    Lower activity in the dry market is typical for this time of year, and as we quicky approach Lunar New Year it is likely we will need to wait a further few weeks before we see this market come alive. Speaking of China, it is the most probably destination for older bulk carriers, with Chinese buyers account for at least half of the sales this week. Mirroring the tanker sector, we are still awaiting new benchmarks for 2025 across key ages. Eco tonnage will be of particular interest, with modern bulkers at the top of most shipowners’ wish lists. SALT LAKE CITY (171K DWT Daewoo 2005) selling at USD 16.2M to Chinese buyers has reset ideas on older Capesize, as not long ago a ship of this age/size would have bene asking in excess of USD 20M.

It feels too soon to make sweeping statements on the fate of the 2025 tanker second hand market, but the sale of the LR2 SUVRETTA (109k DWT STX 2008) for USD 31.5M is certainly a sign of things to come for non eco tanker tonnage. This age of Aframax for example would have been asking in excess of USD 40M at its peak in 2024. Non eco ships however are still in a historically good position, and there remains plenty of money on the table for those who invested shrewdly over the past cycle. What will be interesting to watch is how eco tonnage holds up against potentially volatile price swings across non eco ships.   Usual seasonality dictates a somewhat subdued start to the year in the dry market, and 2025 is no different. Enquiry remains healthy, though buyers are adjusting their budgets to reflect the quieter times. This should help pricing fall into line with the earnings environment, an issue that caused significant disillusionment with the second-hand market last year. Eco tonnage will remain highly sought after, especially that of Japanese build, and buyers will be monitoring the markets closely for any fresh candidates. Handy IYO SEA (37k DWT IMABARI 2015) was sold for USD 17.5M to Greek buyers, a pattern which is likely to repeat itself over the course of the year.

What goes up must come down’ has been the feel in the tanker market this year, resulting in a struggle for liquidity throughout 2024. Correcting values are keeping prospective investors on their toes, and it is likely we will see increased activity once the market returns from winter breaks. CHIBA (45K DWT Shin Kurushima 2007) sold for USD 17M, representing a new benchmark for Japanese blt pumproom MRs.   The Dry market has been the avenue for the majority of second hand investment this year, this is despite an underwhelming Q4 and a mixed outlook on 2025. 15 year old capesize units are still proving popular with Far Eastern buyers as Korea Line acquired scrubber fitted FEG SUCCESS (182K DWT Kawasaki 2010)*ss/dd due for USD 28M. In a rare eco Newcastlemax transaction, Oldendorff sold scrubber fitted LINDA OLDENDORFF (207K DWT HHI 2014) for USD 48.3M to Bohai.

Scrubber fitted DHT SCANDINAVIA (317K DWT HHI Samho 2006) was sold in line with last done despite the dreary VLCC market. It is a winter of discontent so far, and most buyers on large crude tonnage are likely to wait for pricing to fall further before considering this segment.   Likely a result of busy social calendars across the market, and the inbound winter holidays, but the dry market has not provided its usual high liquidity this week. Capesizes though, are still proving popular. OTSL ARTEMIS (177K DWT Shanghai Jiangnan Changxing 2008) & OTSL ATHENA (174K DWT SWS 2007)*scrubber fitted, sold for USD 24.5M each, firm pricing considering recent sale of younger scrubber fitted CAPE DREAM (179K DWT HHI Ulsan 2011) at USD 28M. Elsewhere, Premuda sold FOUR NABUCCO (34K DWT SPP 2010) at USD 11.8M.

Another muted, yet unpredictable, week in the tanker second hand market as reported sales vary in subsector from week to week and seemingly no longer follow any pattern. There remains a healthy level of enquiry behind closed doors, and owners are keen to take money off the table, however buyers are in the driving seat when it comes to discussing price. Saying that, more specialised sectors are holding firm with scrubber fitted J19 SONGA BREEZE (19K DWT FUKUOKA 2009) selling at USD 24M and WINTER (13K DWT 21st CENTURY 2009) at 13.5M.  Sharply dropping earnings in the dry market could be the reason for lower volumes, but certain sectors are still proving attractive to buyers. Capesize particularly is falling under that banner with Far Eastern buyers securing 3 candidates this week. Now could be a smart time to move, so long as you are willing to ride out the slightly gloomy sentiment and likely slowdown over Chinese New Year, as competition could be fierce market units come Q1/Q2 25. As in any market correction, older ships are feeling the pinch with STRATTON (74K DWT HUDONG ZHONGHUA 2004) sold at USD 7.1M to Chinese buyers, a noticeable downtick on the USD 12M sellers were seeking earlier in the year for the vessel.

Slow week again for second hand tankers, though there is increased appetite being shown from Far Eastern buyers, particularly on larger tonnage. Whether or not this translates into increased liquidity is yet to be seen, however, with the winter market noticeably absent, it is not expected that these buyers will rush to transact. On smaller sizes, handy tanker MAERSK BERING (29K DWT GSI 2005)*ice 1C was bought by Chinese buyers for USD 15.55M.   A clear direction for Dry cargo markets with consensus among most market players that there is still some way to go for this ongoing correction. Sentiment which is keeping liquidity high with some Sellers deciding to catch the falling knife at what remain historically attractive levels, while Buyers seeing increasing value in these correcting benchmarks. This week has seen flurry of capesize activity with scrubber fitted capesize sisters K.CONFIDENCE/K. VICTORY (181K SASEBO 2012-13) inviting offers this week and being traded around USD 32-33M each, while the scrubber fitted CAPE DREAM (179K DWT HHI ULSAN 2011) was sold at USD 28M to Chinese buyers.

Although spot rates have improved somewhat this week, the tanker winter market continues to be elusive. Enquiry on larger crude tonnage remains tentative as a result, but despite this, any discussion will be taken very seriously by owners who are keen to exit positions at these elevated levels. What is uncertain is the extent to which values will correct following this ongoing slump. As expected, values for non-eco aframaxes, around the 15-year age bracket, are the first to feel the heat as uncertainty takes hold. Tellingly, the sale of SOFIA II (105k DWT Sumitomo 2008) at USD 32.2M is a rude awakening for owners still stuck with yesterday’s price expectations. History has shown however, that bids accepted in a falling market may prove to be a smart move once the dust settles.  It can be argued that the reason for the well documented disconnect between values and rates has been driven by sentiment, rather than by genuine market fundamentals in this year’s dry market. Despite this somewhat lacklustre earnings environment, investors are still keen to pursue opportunities in this sector. Sellers, for the same reason, are willing to service this enquiry even as values are correcting. This is demonstrated in the sales of scrubber fitted capesize sisters NORD ENERGY/POWER (178k DWT HHIC Phil 2012) to Hayfin at USD 31.8M each, 6 months after the same owners sold a year older ship scrubber fitted unit NORD FERRUM (179k DWT HHIC Phil 2011) for USD 34.3M (in May).

Bahri week provided a welcome distraction for the tanker market this week as owners find themselves waiting for what would be a very welcome seasonal boost. The second-hand market has struggled for liquidity throughout this year, and it looks like the final six weeks of 2024 will be no different. The list of sales candidates is growing as owners look to capture historical highs, but investors are uneasy given a lull in rates and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. The incoming Trump administration could shake up the market with a combination of increased exports and stringent tariffs, however, it is too early to tell and is difficult to predict. In the small chem tanker space, KIISLA/SUULA (14k DWT 2004/5 VIANA DO CASTELO)*Ice 1A sold en bloc for USD 12M.   On dry, rallying Capesize spot rates are providing a ray of positivity against the overall softening sentiment. Liquidity remains consistent, and pricing continues to slide, although there will be no rapid correction until rates fall further. While this is not headline news, the reality is that the majority of dry owners are sitting on debt free units which are comfortably clearing opex and returning a healthy profit, this means that while there are buyers, these owners will not allow themselves to be lowballed. In a segment where the value correction has been more pronounced, CL RIZHAO/SINGAPORE/TANJIN (81k DWT JIANGSU JINLING 2015-16) sold via auction en bloc at USD 68M.

Activity remains subdued in the tanker SnP markets with a resilient bid/offer spread still too wide to bridge. Some movement must be noted however, with a number of potential sellers gradually breaking rank and recalibrating their price expectations. It remains to be seen how much of a correction will be enough to entice the number of buyers patiently sitting on the sidelines. One sale to report, with VLCC TAIGA 311K DWT MITSUI 2007 sold to Chinese Buyers at USD 44.5m.  In the Dry segment, Capesize rates have some tailwind at the end of this week, with average spot rates moving up approx 25%. This should give some breathing space to owners speculating on their next move. CAPE LAUREL 180K DWT IMABARI 2010 has been sold after a number of parties showed interest and in the end fetching mid USD 28m from Chinese buyers. For vintage tonnage, owners continue to cash in on healthy levels such as for sisters CAPTAIN MIKE & IOANNIS M 87K DWT IHI 2005 which were sold at USD 25m en-bloc to ever-present Chinese buyers.

Tanker sales have stuttered throughout the year and continue to do so despite the ever-growing list of candidates. A slight spike though was seen this week courtesy of George Procopiou’s Dynacom selling 3x ice 1A Panamax Tankets ICE ENERGY/FIGHTER/VICTORY (70K dwt Onomichi 2006) to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 72M. Sellers of J19 JAL SIDDHI (19K dwt Kitanihon 2006) managed to catch a buyer in a market space where interest is shrinking rapidly against falling TC rates, selling the unit for USD 20.1M.   The dry market was less active than usual this week as values begin to noticeably slide, in what could be seen as the first move in levelling out the well documented imbalance between asset values and charter rates. That said, rates for the most part aren’t yet in a position where they are causing hurt to owners, sitting comfortably above opex. Ultramax ERIN MANX (63k dwt Tess Zhoushan 2020) sold at USD 32.5M, helping price other eco Chinese candidates of similar age. The dry sector is likely to be the first avenue for investors should asset values continue to correct, with many buyers watching this space intently.

The tanker market this week continues to slide in unfamiliar fashion as firm buyers are finding themselves inundated with possible candidates, particularly in the 10YO+ age range. These buyers though, will likely be rewarded for showing patience while sellers begin considering interest at well below last done levels. Modern units however, continue to show resilience to this story. C.15yo MR tankers are under pressure in terms of value due to the persisting flat sentiment, however it is worth remembering that most owners of these units have enjoyed buoyant earnings and will be exiting positions well in the money. Helping price this part of the age curve AHINOS (53k DWT GSI 2007) which was sold for USD 22M.   The disconnect between values and rates persists across the dry sector, with many buyers waiting in the wings at tomorrow’s prices. Owners for the most part are resilient and are not so inclined to drop their price ideas despite a lacklustre earnings environment. That said, there is still a fairly healthy amount of liquidity within the market, particularly when those price ideas are reduced. For example, scrubber fitted Ultramax pair ALWINE/AUGUST OLDENDORFF (63k DWT JMU 2014/2015) were sold SS/DD due en bloc at USD 51.5M to Greek Buyers, having failed at c.USD 30M per vessel during the summer. In the modern Ultramax sector GREENWICH PIONEER (63k DWT Nantong Xiangyu 2020) was sold for USD 32.5M with TC attached until March 2026.

There is a feeling in the tanker market that beating last done is no longer the expectation for sellers, as buying interest wanes given a calming charter market and potentially impactive events to come in the near future (i.e. the US Election). That said, levels slightly below the last done will still provide owners with extremely healthy returns on their initial investments.   A flurry of new candidates on the market coupled with a sharp correction on spot rates has dampened sentiment in the dry market. Buyers are being encouraged to either wait or are testing owners on levels very much at tomorrow’s pricing rather than yesterday’s. It remains to be seen whether owners will embrace this new pricing sentiment or endure the uncertain charter market and rely on the vessel supply story to support elevated values. There was healthy activity in the Capesize sector, particularly focused around the 15 year old mark, which will help price the increasing list of units in the market.

While the story on modern tanker tonnage remains steady, older units are once again in the spotlight as geopolitical turmoil continues to pose questions to investors. There is a real sense of unpredictability over escalating conflict in the Middle East, and the US elections getting ever closer. Record prices on modern MRs are being crystalised in the form of scrubber fitted MARITIME VERITY/INSPIRATION (49K DWT GSI 2021), where not long ago, NB prices were in line with these levels now seen on almost 4 year old ships.    A quieter week in terms of reported transactions in the usually busy dry sector has been interestingly coupled with what has felt like an avalanche of new candidates on the market. The 10-15 y.o. Capesize sector seems particularly active, where confidence in the iron ore demand story is waning in the wake of a strong period for owners and charterers. Values and rates on the smaller sizes however, seem fairly consistent for the time being, despite a recent slight softening on the increasingly liquid Ultramax market where OCEAN AMBITIOUS (63K DWT China Shipbuilding 2016) was sold for USD 25.5M.

With much of Asia taking holiday this week, one would have predicted a more subdued few days, however the increasingly volatile geopolitical landscape jolted the tanker market into life. The questions on the longevity of record asset prices have been put to one side, at least for now, as spot rates and tanker stocks both received sizeable boosts this week. Sentiment had been, that price ideas on second hand tanker tonnage would begin to soften, however owners and investors alike will be closely monitoring the earnings market as the situation in the Middle East unfolds. Appetite for older MRs remains firm as MR HAFNIA ANDROMEDA (50K DWT GSI 2011) was sold for USD 31M.   A combination of extreme weather and Golden Week in China has not disrupted the liquidity in the bulk market, as demand for units remains strong. What continues to challenge investors though, is the disconnect between asset values and charter rates. Granted, there is cause for optimism on news of the incoming China stimulus, but overall demand and consumer confidence is still an issue in this major global market driver. Ultramax demand is high, and liquidity appears to be increasing, particularly on more modern units where BEECHGATE (63K DWT IWAGI ZOSWEN 2019) was sold at USD 35.6M.

In the standout transaction of the week, Evalend took 2x Hengli scrubber fitted VLCC resales due for delivery in 2026 for USD 127M each. While modern ship values are holding fairly steady, there is much debate on the fate of older units and whether buyers are still there to pay yesterday’s prices.  That said, undercutting the last done on c.10-year-old tanker could provide owners with a straightforward way to take some money off the table at extremely healthy historical levels. This is just what Advantage tankers did, with VLCC ADVANTAGE VIRTUE (296K DWT BOHAI 2009) being sold to Chinese buyers at USD 51M.   There are a number of stories to contend with on dry bulk this week. Extreme weather has spurred the capesize market onward, where a single day jump of 8% was registered on Thursday this week. This is while supramax values hinted that there may be an imminent correction. ZEN-NOH GRAIN PEGASUS (55K DWT OSHIMA 2010) sold for USD 15M, this is at a sizeable discount to last done similar VISAYA (56K DWT MITSUI 2010) at USD 16.8M. Levels that will excite buyers in what is a very liquid sector. Elsewhere, Newcastlemax MINERAL CLOUDBREAK (205K DWT HHIC-Phil 2012) was sold to Chinese buyers for USD 38.5M.

Despite the buoyant levels seen in transactions this week, there is an emerging sense of caution among second hand participants in the tanker market. Rates have been lacklustre in recent weeks, but given the winter markets are just around the corner, perhaps this caution will be short lived. In the J19 market, TC rates dipping below $20K/Day have done little to discourage investors. Woojin bought HORIN TRADER (19K DWT USUKI 2015) at USD 32.5M, a premium to last done 1 year younger and scrubber fitted TRF J19s which sold at the same price.  CHEM STREAM (19K DWT SHITANOE SHIPBUILDING 2010) also sold at a firm USD 25.3M to Chinese buyers, showing the unrelenting appetite of Far Eastern buyers for this vessel type. VLCC SAKE (300K DWT IHI KURE 2005) selling at USD 40M will likely entice more owners of older tankers to consider exiting those positions, however it is worth adding that VLCCs have been of more interest to buyers over suez-afra sizes.   While modern bulkers remain atop the shopping lists of most owners, older ships are cause for discussion among brokers and investors. A correction in value in the panamax/kamsarmax sector is potentially acting as a cautionary tale for those thinking these record asset values are here to stay. Tellingly, several Japanese owned Kansarmaxes in the 10 yr bracket have been withdrawn for sale as offers received were deemed too low. Kamsarmax sisters AM QUEBEC/HAMBURG (81K DWT NEW TIMES 2013) were bought by Chinese buyers at USD 18M each, a level that will correct similarly aged units by at least 10%. It is as yet unseen whether similar corrections will take place in other sub sectors, with most sellers not willing to be the first to reduce price ideas. What is sure though, is that asset players will be watching this sector very closely.

Ice 1B JAG LALIT (158K DWT Hyundai Samho HI 2005) is the first suezmax tanker to be sold since June 24 as it was transacted this week at USD 33M. Not only suezmax, but tanker sales in general have stuttered this year, with historical high pricing giving potential investors much to consider. This sale will catch the attention of those owners who are placing the increasing number of ageing tanker candidates in the market. MR tankers continue to provide consistent liquidity to the market, with this week TENACITY (50K DWT GSI 2014) selling in line with other market candidates at USD 40M to Greek buyers.   Dry liquidity is somewhat bolstered this week by a 7 ship en bloc transaction of the entire Dasin Holdings supramax fleet for USD 80M to Hai Tong of China. There continues to be a healthy amount of activity on second hand capesize units, as rates remain firm. ALPHA PRUDENCE (178K DWT SWS 2008) was bought for USD 24.75M, a slight increase on last done OCEAN COURTESY (178K DWT SWS 2008) which sold in July 24 for USD 24M.  Overall, attitude on dry remains bullish, with a rapidly ageing fleet, despite some reported economic uncertainty in China.

There is a ‘back to school’ feel in the market this week, with most players returning from their seasonal holidays. In the tanker space, MRs are continuing to hold value against last done deals in the market, with Scorpio selling the scrubber fitted sisterships STI SAN ANTONIO / TEXAS CITY (50K DWT SPP 2014) at an enbloc price of USD 85M. Levels that are becoming increasingly attractive for owners that so far have resisted the temptation of these historical highs. A sentiment particularly well illustrated by the increase in availability on older large tankers, with some owners looking to exit positions they likely fought aggressively for 18 months ago.    The dry space continues to dominate in terms of S&P activity, with the sector being the preferred avenue second only to newbuildings, for profit reinvestment for owners. While COSCO made the headlines revealing a 42-ship newbuilding order, there appears to be an increase in Japanese controlled bulkers, which will help set pricing benchmarks going forward for the rest of the year. Much of the liquidity remains in the older units, particularly this week on the capesize front. Surveys due AZURE OCEAN (180K DWT IMABARI 2007) was sold to Chinese buyers for USD 25M.

An unsurprisingly slow week in terms of SnP transactions as markets are slowly finding their post-holiday rhythm. Subdued summer freight markets are consolidating a relatively cautious sentiment with a number of players anticipating a possible value correction on the short term especially on older tonnage. A dynamic that would see owners exploring potential sales in hope to capture last done levels that remain historically attractive. A consensus that however remains far from negative with a widely shared positive long-term sentiment. On the Tanker front only one sale to report this week with the 20 year old Aframax “SILVERA” (Abt 115k dwt Hyundai 2004 ) being sold at Usd 27m. Levels that remain in line with recently concluded business.

After some optimism last week tanker rates again face some overall pressure. That is, however, not out of the ordinary for this time of the year, and everything looks set for normal seasonality to the upside in coming weeks and months. TC rates have not been immune to these summer doldrums but hold at overall solid levels – especially for longer durations. This bodes well for values in the near to medium term, however any disappointment in earnings will put values for the older ones firmly at risk.  Values for modern tankers are, and will remain resilient but we see rather limited upside potential from present levels. Tangible deals for the very modern ones are few and far between but following its acquisition of three modern VLCC’s from Korean owners in May, Bahri made another swoop this week for nine modern, scrubber-fitted units from Capital Group reportedly for abt Usd 1 bn en-bloc. Prices agreed are in line with our value estimates.  Earnings in the Capesize and Ultramax segments are at solid levels, whereas Kamsarmax earnings continues to slide. However, the imminent US and Canadian grain season could reverse this trend. Coal demand in Asia will eventually improve in Q4, so earnings in the Ultramax and Kamsarmax segments will likely average in the mid or even high teens through the remainder of this year. In the Capesize segment, the weakening fundamentals in China could result in a near-term correction in earnings. However, seasonal factors like Indian coal demand and increased Guinean bauxite shipments should support the market in Q4.  We have seen a bumper dry SNP actitivity YTD and with this expected back-drop on earnings, the briskness should continue once the holiday season has passed.

A slump in activity is being felt across chartering and S&P in the tanker space this week as the summer market takes hold. This is likely not distracting owners from their holidays while they enjoy the historically strong position the market is in. In the only sale this week VLCC APOLLO HARMONY 301K DWT IHI KURE 2010 was bought by Smart Tankers for USD 58M, with an end of year delivery.   The dry market too is suffering symptoms of the summer, with a fall in activity this week. This is likely only temporary while owners take a breather before the typically hectic Q4. Despite the lower activity, values have remained steady, with Capesize SEA TRIUMPH 181K DWT KOYO 2012 sold in line with last done at USD 36M.

Despite the usual seasonal slump and lacklustre earnings environment, there remains a healthy amount of activity on the dry S&P front. This only amplifies questions on the disconnect between asset values and earnings, particularly on modern ships. It hasn’t however, deterred Alpha Bulkers acquiring DD due capesize HERUN GLOBAL SWS 2016 at USD 49.5M, in line with recently done COURAGEOUS (181K DWT SWS 2016). Kamsarmax trio THERESA HEBEI/JINLIN/GUANGDONG (81K DWT SAINTY YANGHZHOU / JIANGSU EASTERN HI 2012) were sold en bloc at USD 19M each to a Chinese buyer, a premium versus the USD 17.5M paid for YU QIANG (81K DWT PLA4807 2012) by a Greek buyer.   MRs continue to dominate activity within tanker S&P market as GREEN SEA (50K DWT DAE SUN 2014) was sold this week at just under USD 39M, with SS/DD passed.  A price that when compared with recent transactions is Illustrating particularly well the premium that HMD built units still command over their Korean counterparts.  Liquidity for large mid aged tankers remains resilient as EMERALD I (104K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2007) sold for USD 38M, this is in contrast to older c.20yo afra and suezmax tankers where the number of available candidates is growing steadily.

MRs, particularly older MRs this week, continue to be a popular investment despite the well documented rise in asset prices over the last 18 months. This is likely due to the low barrier to entry and the healthy returns on offer. The rise in pricing shows no sign in stopping as BAHRI sold DD Due NCC TABUK 45K DWT HMD 2006 for USD 20.7M, a slight rise on their last done DD Due NCC TIHAMA 45K DWT HMD 2006 at USD 20.5M. Several other sales have been or are close to being concluded, with Navios rumored having sold their NAVE EQUATOR 50k DWT, SPP 2009 at USD 26M to Soechi with slightly forward delivery and prompt dock due. A handful of similar aged MRs we understand being discussed with owners now aiming in the high 20s for both DD passed and due.  Elsewhere, China continues to be a destination for older Afras, with Thenamaris’ DD Due SEAQUEEN 115K DWT SAMSUNG HI GEOJE 2004 sold to Victory Global Navigation at USD 30M.   South Korean buyers continued their run on modern dry tonnage with two notable transactions this week. Scrubber fitted Newcastlemax FOMENTO TWO 206K DWT DAEHAN HAENAM 2017 was bought for USD 60M by Pan Ocean, while HMM provided Densay the opportunity for a rare modern asset flip, purchasing SSI DARING 36K DWT SHIKOKU 2017 for USD 2.7M more than they paid for it in March 2024, at USD 26.7M. We also observe this week the progress in pricing on the Kamsarmax front, XING DE HAI 82K DWT OSHIMA 2017 being bought by Tolani at USD 37M, versus the last notable comparable sale in August 2023 of ALAM KEKAL 82K DWT OSHIMA 2018 at USD 31.8M.

Despite the market entering the usual summer lull, capesize bulkers remain an attractive investment as 2 further units were reported sold this week. Pricing remains firm, with CAPE MATHILDE 178K DWT MITSUI 2010 achieving close to USD 30M and scrubber fitted GENCO HADRIAN 169K DWT SUNGDONG 2008 being sold for USD 25M. This price environment seems for good reason too, with Vale reporting this week they increased iron ore production in Q2 and expect to reach the upper end of their 2024 guidance. Scrubber fitted kamsarmax KRISTIAN OLDENDORFF 82K DWT JIANGSU NEW HANTONG 2024 saw the first transaction of a Chinese kamsarmax in xs of USD 40M, sold at USD 40.85M, showing the value of a new ship on the water.   Scrubber fitted sisters PACIFIC JEWELS/TREASURES 115K DWT DAEHAN 2016 were reported sold to Vietnamese buyers in the high USD 60Ms, this represents a strong firming in the market following from two sales in February of scrubber fitted 2018 built sisters POLAR BRIGHT/ACE 109K DWT DAEHAN 2018 for 65.5M USD. NAVE EQUATOR 49K DWT SPP 2009 was bought by Soechi at USD 26M, riding the high of the increasingly strong market with a near 20% rise in values since last year. Clearly buyers are backing this market, with TORM further establishing market position in a cash plus shares deal for 8x 2014-2015 MRs valued at USD 340M.

Capital is capturing the headlines this week with the purchase of Scrubberfitted Newcastlemax BERGE BOBOTOV (207K DWT BOHAI 2021) at $75m which marks an appreciation in values since last done “TRUST SHANGHAI/QINGDAO (209K DWT SWS 2021) at $73m - a price highlighting the continued strong appetite for larger tonnage. Elsewhere in the dry market, a flurry of Handysize transactions across all ages, most notably the MAESTRO EMERALD (39K DWT SAIKI 2020) fetching $30m from Turkish buyers, as well as Nisshin Shipping, who is rumoured to have offloaded 4 x handies, WESTERN DURBAN/LIMA/MIAMI/PARIS (39K DWT JIANGMEN 2015) at $19.75m each to Precious shipping. To no surprise, the activity in the tanker market continues to be subdued. Prices for older tankers remain resilient as the PGC COMPANION (72K DWT HUDONG-ZHONGUA 2005) fetched $18m. Buying enquiry remains high for product tankers with three transactions to report this week, most notably the ZEZE START (50K DWT HMD 2009), which is sold basis surveys due to Indonesian buyers for $27m.

Ice 1c ARISTOFANIS 115K DWT DAEHAN 2020 was the latest modern afra/LR2 to be reported this week, sold to Azerbaijan Caspian Shipping Co for USD 78.8M, this represents a significant rise in the last done STIRLING 112K DWT COSCO 2021 which sold at USD 70M back in May of this year. Rumour still surrounds Japanese controlled PUSAKA JAVA 108K DWT TSUNEISHI 2018, with uncertainty related to both price and direction.    Transactions this week in the dry market are typical of the current environment; modern ships hard to come by resulting in an increased focus on 10-15yo units. Despite a somewhat lull in earnings, supramax values remain firm with NORDIC STAVANGER 56K DWT MITSUI 2011 selling for USD 18M. Elsewhere, Jinhui Shipping, a strong believer in the capesize market as they make another purchase, OCEAN CONFIDENCE 178K DWT SWS 2008 for USD 24M.

Softer sentiment across the tanker charter market won’t be of too much concern to owners as the overall picture remains strong. Tanker SNP has lagged behind dry this year in terms of liquidity, and it seems unlikely to change anytime soon particularly as we enter the summer months. The Japanese controlled scrubber fitted Aframax PUSAKA JAVA 108K DWT TSUNEISHI 2018 invited offers on 25.06.24 and is now understood to have been committed at rgn USD 68M to EPS. Elsewhere, Kyklades Maritime bought the scrubber fitted C. PROSPERITY 313K DWT HHI ULSAN 2009 at USD 53M, a slight discount against last done given the ship has her special surveys due.   Despite a slower week on the spot market, dry values continue to push upwards. Belships announced this week that along with declaring a purchase option on BELMAR 63K DWT SHOEI KISEN 2021, they have agreed to also purchase an unnamed Japanese built 2024 64K DWT Ultramax at USD 41M, setting the pace for the rest of the market and showing that there are genuine buyers at levels only previously speculated. In other news, Pioneer have followed up their recent supramax purchase with the acquisition of two Newcastlemax sisters MINERAL CHARLIE/MAUREEN 205K DWT HHIC PHIL INC 2012 at USD 81.6M en bloc.

The dry market continues to benefit from increased levels of interest as shipowners look for ways to deploy their capital. Once again, anything ECO is deemed to be extremely desirable, and this is reflected in the price. In the standout transactions this week, 2x 2016 Chinese blt Capesizes sold either side of USD 50M. We would have to look back November 2023 for the sale of the last 2016 Chinese capes with scrubber fitted CHOW/COMANCHE 180K DWT SWS 2016, which sold to Genco for 43.1M each. Considering the premium applied to scrubber fitted units, this would mean the market has pushed ~20% in value in the last 8 months. Greek buyers in these transactions would indicate there is room for these values to increase further.   A lacklustre week all round in the tanker market with stuttering spot rates and only one sale to report. Away from the second-hand market however, investment is still being poured into tanker newbuildings, with owners backing the legs of this bull run. In the only transaction this week, Greek Buyers bought LR1 AVRA PATROS 75K DWT Sungdong Shipbuilding 2008.

Headlines about the tanker second hand market have provided little in terms of variance in the past few months (slowing activity amid high prices), however, the reported sales this week confirm there are still those willing to buy and sell at these levels. Prices in general have continued to firm despite few transactions to prove it, shown here with scrubber fitted FRONT THOR 159K DWT JIANGSU RONGSHENG 2010 selling in the low USD 48Ms. Suezmax transactions around this age bracket have been hard to come by, however, Frontline’s ability to dispose of their 2010 blt Rongsheng series at better than last done on each occasion is a prime example of the underlying positivity in the tanker space. MRs also continue to gain in value, with ALHENA 52K DWT GSI 2012 selling to Greek buyers at USD 32.2M.  Quite an unremarkable week in the dry market with the usual activity of players jostling for position on older units. Capes remain strong, with scrubber fitted NYMPHE 180K DWT DSME 2009 sold to Hayfin at USD 29.3M, just slightly up on last done 2009 CORINTHIAN PHOENIX 179 K DWT HHI 2009 at USD 29M. Otherwise, it is tough to see where the potential asset play is in the dry bulk space. Modern eco ships are scarcely available and priced to represent that, and older bulkers are often priced in excess of any justifiable calculation from an investment standpoint.

A predictably quiet week, with the majority of the market gathered in Athens for the latest instalment of Posidonia. Despite the slow week, the good times in the tanker market continue to roll on. MRs GUNMETAL JACK/PARADISE CITY 50K DWT SPP 2009 were both sold to Greek buyers at USD 28M, as this market continues to rise in terms of asset values.   A more subdued, yet surprisingly active week in the dry market. In the standout deal, the Stefanou brothers (Sea Gate Navigation/Bright Navigation) took 3 Laskaridis Panamax units THISSEAS/ICARUS/ATLAS 75K DWT PENGLAI 2012 en bloc for USD 52.5M. Elsewhere, the Far East remains a likely place for older capes to end up as China’s Pioneer paid USD 32.5M for CAPE KEYSTONE 179K DWT HHI ULSAN 2011.

No tanker sales to report this week, further reinforcing our previous comments on lower liquidity being the new norm in the sector. Despite this lower liquidity environment, there are sure to be smiles across the faces on all stakeholders throughout get-togethers at Posidonia next week.   A more eventful week across the dry SNP market before an inevitable slowdown as the industry unites in Athens. We are still seeing limited modern sales, with the majority of transactions happening around the 15-year-old mark. Pricing remains at a disconnect with earnings, despite overall general bullish feeling towards the charter market, thus proving the overall vessel supply story is the dominant factor in the current run on asset values. Large handysize YASA VIOLET 40K DWT JIANGMEN NANYANG 2024 was sold to Pan Ocean for USD 34M, showing the premium buyers are willing to pay for a brand-new ship on the water. There looks to be a sizeable uptick in 15-year-old capesize values as EASTERN WINDFLOWER 175K DWT NEW TIMES 2010 sold to Chinese Buyers for USD 28M, eclipsing the last done on a New Times cape with 1-year younger ex MINERAL BRUGGE 175K DWT NEW TIMES 2011 selling in March for USD 26M, representing a near 10% increase in merely three months.

A low volume environment seems to be the new norm on tanker SNP, despite healthy levels of buying enquiry within the market. The comfort for owners joying the sustained high returns,  means they are not in a rush to dispose of tonnage and will certainly not accept anything below last done. This is shown with EPS offloading pumproom MR PACIFIC DIAMOND 47K DWT IWAGI ZOSEN 2010 for a healthy $26.7m. The same vessel was acquired for $18m back in 2022, an eye-watering 48% increase.   The dry market continues to steal headlines in the second-hand markets, despite a growing disconnect between earnings and values. A rise in pricing particularly well illustrated by the sale of the Kamsarmax GIA AMBITION 84K DWT CSSC TIANJIN 2022 which was picked up this week for USD 38.5M by Egyptian buyers, roughly 17% more than the last 2022 Chinese sold in October 2023 KUNO OLDENDORFF 82K DWT JIANGSU 2022.

Another quiet week in terms of volume on second hand tanker sales, rather in keeping with recent trends. In the standout transaction, Dee4 sold MR DEE4 LARCH 49K DWT HYUNDAI VINASHIN 2016 at USD 41M, comfortably eclipsing the last comparable Vinahsin MR transaction of scrubber fitted TRF BERGEN 49K DWT HYUNDAI VINASHIN 2015 which sold for USD 36M back in October 2023. This shows yet again how far MR prices have firmed in the recent run. Elsewhere, NIPPON PRINCESS 105K DWT SUMITOMO 2008 was sold at USD 41M, this transaction likely will be a comparable for the numerous units on the market in this age/size range. It will also be interesting to see whether prices continue to firm over the summer, usually a quiet time for tanker SNP.   Modern ultramax units continue to be in high demand and are priced accordingly. HMM bought SSI PRIVILEGE 63K DWT JINLING SHIPYARD 2019 from Densay for USD 32.5M, with SS/DD due, the Turkish outfit flipping the unit they bought earlier this year for USD 30.3M, an unusually quick turnaround on such a modern unit. Elsewhere Agricore paid USD 35.75M for EL GRASSO 181K DWT IMABARI 2012, priced in line with recent Japanese capesize sales of this age.

Further holidays this week could be blamed for the lack of output on the tanker second hand sales front however, the story very much remains in keeping with recent market trends. Overall lack of supply of modern sales candidates, and fair liquidity on the older tonnage. Those who are genuine sellers of modern ships in this market are in no rush and can continue to enjoy the bumper earnings while their suitors fight it out. New York listed Scorpio announced they sold STI MANHATTAN 50K DWT SPP 2015 for USD 40.8M to KSS Line, only a tick higher than the sister units they sold to International Seaways back in February of this year, showing that despite the sharp gains in MR values over the recent run, pricing has remined consistent in the last 6 months.   A subdued week by recent standards in the dry market, but not one without notable headlines. Asset values, for anything younger than 10 years, continue to strengthen. Sellers of modern units are few and far between, and this scarcity is contributing to an emerging disconnect between asset prices and charter rates. Pangaea bought Belships supra sisters BELFRIEND/BELTIDE 58K DWT TSUNEISHI CEBU 2016 at USD 28.3M each, comfortably eclipsing the last sale of a 2016 Tess Cebu 58 (EMMANOUELA 57K DWT Tess Cebu 2016) sold at USD 22M back in November 2022. Elsewhere in a rare modern ultramax transaction, FLORENTINE OETKER 63K DWT IMABARI 2017 was bought by Ince of Turkey for USD 32.85M.

A somewhat interrupted week due to holidays across the market saw a handful of transactions reported. Chinese buyers continue to dominate mid aged Aframax tonnage, as scrubber fitted CLARET PRINCE 109K DWT HUDONG ZHONGHUA 2010 was picked up for USD 43.5M – in line with recent sales. With the Canadian Trans Mountain pipeline soon to be opened, one could speculate these recent Chinese acquisitions are to service this new increased export capacity to Asian markets. China was also the destination for ageing VLCC PHOEBE 311K DWT MITSUI 2005, as she was sold for USD 40M. In the clean market, LR1 ALPINE PERSEFONE 74K DWT SUNGDONG 2008 was bought by Spring Marine for USD 29M.   Modern tonnage is still proving hard to come by in the dry market, and any candidates that do emerge are hotly contested. As a result, we continue to see an abundance of mid aged and older ships being traded. Pricing emerged on the Newcastlemax sisters CAPE KALLIA/NEWMAX 203K DWT BOHAI 2012, which were bought for USD 38M each by Pioneer. Owners of capesize HENG SHAN 174K DWT SWS 2007, took advantage of the recent run on values with a healthy USD 21.75M achieved to undisclosed buyers.

The situation across the tanker second hand market has remained largely the same over the past months, despite the usual volatility in the charter space. The climb in asset values show no sign of respite with very strong level of buying enquiry for modern eco tonnage being met by an ever-thinning list of available candidates. Newbuildings become therefore the avenue of choice where despite the continuous headlines of placed orders, the relative percentage of fleet renewal is still historically low. A flurry of 2009 blt Aframax tanker sales this week, showing the high demand from the Far East for ships of this type and vintage. GSTAAD GRACE II/AFRAGOLD 115K DWT New Times 2009, sold for USD 42M and 41M respectively with the formed freshly surveys passed, this will help price other units in the market.  Despite a fall in earnings on Capes this week, it seems buyers are not being discouraged by the resilient price targets from owners, with the overall vessel supply story trumping doubts of the longevity of this run. This is shown in scrubber fitted FRONTIER UNITY 181K DWT Koyo Dockyard 2012, selling to Greek buyers at USD 35M . A particularly busy week on the Supramax front, where Navios sold two Tess 58s NAVIOS CELESTIAL/CHRISTINE B 58K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2009 for USD 30M en bloc.

The tanker story remains unchanged from recent trends, with relatively modern (younger than 15 yo) sales candidates hard to come by, resulting in low liquidity. Money continues to flood the newbuilding yards giving an idea of the future make up of the global fleet, where we are seeing advancements in designs and fuelling, this week seen in the first ammonia dual-fuel aframax tankers being ordered by MISC (through shipping arm AET). In the second-hand market, Tsakos sold IZUMO PRINCESS (105K DWT SUMITOMO 2007) for USD 37.1M.   The bulk market continues to see fairly strong liquidity despite prices making many buyers in the market feel uneasy, even with the general positive market sentiment. Modern tonnage is still very popular with YMK QUARTET (82K DWT Jiangsu Yangzi-Mitsui 2021) being sold at USD 35M to Greek buyers. FEDERAL ISLAND (63K DWT TADOTSU SHIPYARD 2017) was sold for USD 32M, a firming against the last done 2017 blt unit SANTA JOHANNA (61K DWT SHIN KURUSHIMA 2017) at USD 30.5M back in February.

A jolt of life in the tanker second hand market this week with a handful of transactions to report amongst the smaller sizes, otherwise, a fairly subdued week as Ramadan came to an end. In the standout transaction, D’Amico bought AMFITRION (50K DWT SAMSUNG HI NINGBO 2017) for USD 43.5M, compare that to the last sale of a similar Chinese MR SUNNY APATITE (50K DWT GSI 2016) at USD 34M, one can see just how much the market has shifted in the last two quarters. In the high value and tight STST market where levels continue to rise, Delos Shipping bought CHEM BULLDOG (21K DWT ASAKAWA 2010) at USD 23M.  We are entering a critical period in this most recent dry market rally. Levels and buying interest have been ever increasing over the last quarter, however, as a consequence some buyers are now being priced out and others are perhaps pulling back to observe whether prices will remain high, or will correct in the short term. Scrubber fitted Kamsarmax SAMMY (82K DWT Tsuneishi 2012) sold at USD 24.6M, surprisingly softer than the initial market rumours pricing the deal closer to USD 26M. Capes continue to be in demand with the sale of scrubber fitted HL HARMONY (179K DWT DALIAN 2015) to Hong Kong based buyers at USD 43M.

The start to Q2 has been somewhat disrupted with various holidays, however, it is not expected that it will mirror the explosive Q1 in the dry market. Asset prices rose sharply as buyers looked to acquire prompt market ships to take advantage of increasing rates, even enticing non-traditional dry players into the space. This sentiment appears to have shifted as those buyers who missed out on the rush have either been priced out, or indeed have turned to sellers themselves to try and capitalise on the inflated values. One could fall back on the underlying overall vessel supply argument, but it just feels that buyers are not comfortable at the current market levels, hence the downtick in sales. In the modern Ultramax space WORLD ROYAL (61K DWT DACKS 2022) sold for USD 35M, while NEW CHAMP (66K DWT MITSUI TAMANO 2018) was bought by Meghna for USD 33.85M.   The reinvestment focus of the tanker market continues to be in Newbuildings, as the number of second-hand transactions stutters. In a rare modern tanker transaction, scrubber fitted Aframax AURVIKEN (112K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2019) was auctioned off and eventually sold to Greek buyers for USD 73M, this auction was a result of part of the ownership structure making the unit subject to sanctions against Russia. Elsewhere, Minerva offloaded Ice 1c MINERVA HELEN (103K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2004) for USD 30.35M.

After the furore of the last few weeks, it seems as though the dry market has taken somewhat of a breather. Small and medium sized buyers are looking at the market more tentatively than before, having seen price expectations on units increase rapidly over the last quarter. Earnings stuttered this week, reminding buyers that everything can change quickly. Capes are still receiving healthy premiums, with ORANGE TIARA 181K DWT KOYO 2012 selling at USD 35M, exceeding what was paid for 1-year younger KINOKAWA MARU 181K DWT IMABARI 2013 (USD 34M) back in February. Supramax STRAITS BAY 55K DWT KAWASAKI 2007 sold for a very sizeable USD 14.75M, showing the premium buyers would pay for a very prompt ship. Elsewhere Lauritzen sold scrubber fitted handy bc ASIAN BULKER 36K DWT SHIKOKU DOCKYARD 2017 for USD 24M.   It was a fairly lacklustre week in the tanker market, despite a jump in earnings. Modern second hand tonnage is still hard to come by, with the majority of activity happening on the newbuilding front. In the notable transaction for the week, Scorpio sold MR pair STI LE ROCHER/STI LARVOTTO 49K DWT HMD 2013 for USD 36.2M each.

There is a feeling of the second-hand S&P market resembling a runaway train, particularly on dry, where we see huge activity at rapidly firming levels. Modern tonnage is still hard to come by, however, over the next few months owners may find the surging prices too much to resist provided the market is willing to pay up. Scrubber fitted Newcastlemax sisters ATLANTIC TIGER/DRAGON 209K DWT SWS 2020 fetched a notable USD 71M per vessel to Pan Ocean. A rally  in values that becomes particularly apparent when compared to the USD 63.5M per vessel paid for scrubber fitted BULK SHANGHAI/SEOUL 208K DWT NEW TIMES 2019 in February of this year. Otherwise, players have been jostling for older units where competition is quickly driving up prices and expectations. There were 10 buyers on supramax QUEEN BUSAN 55K DWT KAWASAKI HI 2010, which eventually sold at USD 17.15M, setting a new benchmark in this competitive size and age bracket.  The tanker market of late has been somewhat flying under the radar, rates have remained firm with a high level of purchase enquiry that is met short by an ever-thinning list of available candidates . In the immediate term, appetite is slightly lower on older units, perhaps due to some scepticism over sanctions and longevity of this run. That said, Turkish buyers are reported to have picked up suezmax KARVOUNIS 156K DWT SUMITOMO 2013 at 67.5M. Elsewhere, older units have softened, seen in scrubber fitted VLCC ACHELOUS 299K DWT IHI 2004 at USD 30M (SS due 09/24).

Lack of liquidity is a distant memory for dry market players as the run on second hand bulkers continues this week. Perhaps a cause for all this excitement is that despite the seemingly buoyant market, there is still some way to go before historical highs are reached, at least from a TC point of view. There is work to be done even to eclipse the 2022 TC market, though judging by the ever-increasing competition on any new market candidate, there is no shortage of confidence that this will not be achieved. Modern Scrubber fitted Tess 82 Kamasarmax SANKO HAWKING 82K DWT TSUNEISH 2021 sold this week at a notable USD 41.5M. At the other end of the age curve where values are likely to fluctuate significantly as players look to take advantage of the spot market, Capesize CASTILLO DE VALVERDE 173K DWT BOHAI 2005 sold at USD 15M.   The second hand wet market is happy to stay out of the headlines this week, with more ink being devoted to the strong demand for Newbuilidng tanker slots. There is still demand for older tankers, albeit softer than we’ve seen in recent times, shown in aframax SEA HAZEL 106K DWT TSUNEISHI TADOTSU 2004 being sold at USD 29M.

The dry market rally continues to gather momentum this week, with capesize values in particular going from strength to strength. Scrubber fitted SEALINK 180K DWT DAEHAN 2010 was bought by Kisamos for USD 31 M, while scrubber fitted MOUNT CARAMEL 177K DWT NAMURA 2007 was sold for USD 25M despite having surveys due in June. This is seeing values in older market units jump over 10% in the last week or two. It is conceivable that there is some way to go in this rally, so we expect to see asset players cashing in over the course of the year. In modern tonnage, ultramax BULK MONACO 63K DWT SHIN KASADO 2023 priced the market, having been transacted for a considerable USD 40.5M.   It may look that the tanker market has taken a breather, but the attendance of London’s IE Week and the ongoing transactions behind closed doors say otherwise. In the only reported transaction this week Ice 1A STST MIRELLA S 20K DWT QINGSHAN 2006 was bought by Vietnamese and then subsequently fixed on a 2-year TC at $18k/d.

The week’s most impactive news story is not one of a tanker transaction, but that of fresh sanctions from the UK government “targeting individuals and businesses sustaining Putin’s illegal war in Ukraine” (from statement released yesterday 22.02.24), which could have deep implications for tanker owners involved in the trade of Russian oil. This has coincided with a typically volatile week on the charter front, seeing the gains from last week duly erased. Only a handful of transactions reported, with surveys due scrubber fitted VLCC NAVE SPHERICAL (297K DWT SHANGHAI JIANGNAN CHANGXING 2009) being bought for USD 53.9M. STST tankers continue to prove popular with BEATRICE (25K DWT ASAKAWA 2013) purchased by DM Shipping for a healthy USD 29M.  The dry market looks as though it is gearing up for its moment in the sun, as the Actual Cape Index registers the best rate for this time of year since 2010 at USD 26,079/day. This will surely empower sellers to hold out for premium levels as buyers jostle for market position. There has been particular demand for Capesize units in the last few weeks, particular eco tonnage, with JPM attracting over 10 buyers on their scrubber fitted TRUE CARTIER (181K DWT IMABARI 2014), eventually selling for a shade under USD 41M. Bulker prices in general will surely benefit from tonnage hungry and cash rich market players who would rather have steel on the water than cash in the bank. Liquidity appears to be improving in the ultra sector, DARYA PADMA (60K DWT JMU 2015) showing exactly what is needed (USD 29M) for those looking to secure an early eco Japanese built unit. Those looking at a similarly aged Chinese unit will note SYROS/ANDROS (ISLAND 63K DWT ZHEJIANG SHIPBUILDING 2015/2016) selling for USD 52.5M en bloc.

The Tanker market moved on in relentless fashion this week with a flurry of transactions in the product space, against an ever-tightening crude sector. Scrubber fitted Suezmax RAPTOR (159K DWT Universal 2007) was sold to Chinese buyers at USD 46.5M. Worth noting that she is surveys freshly passed but nevertheless this transaction shows just where the market has reached, given this is a 17-year-old ship. Across the product sector, an abundance of buyers are giving owners of ageing ships the option to cash out at a very healthy level, such as in the case for TORM selling TORM PLATTE (46K DWT HMD 2006) for USD 22M.  No such thing as a quiet week it seems, as an abundance of transactions were registered this week in the Dry market. Scrubber fitted Newcastlemaxes BULK SHANGHAI/SEOUL (207K DWT New Times 2019) were bought by Neda Maritime, a deal which will have others looking upon it in envy as modern dry tonnage seems increasingly tough to come by. Lunar New Year has not impacted the market quite as it used to, with Chinese buyers still active and an overall bullish feel to the market, giving impetus to those still in the office.

Tanker rates remained firm this week, with little disruption to be expected as we enter into Lunar New Year celebrations which according to the South China Morning Post will see “a record high of over 9 billion trips” being made within China. The second-hand S&P market though failed to ignite any real excitement, with only a handful of transactions reported this week. Intermediate tanker PENINSULA XI 17K DWT HMD 2023 is the most notable of those deals, being bought by Union Maritime for USD 32.5M.   A healthy amount of liquidity in the Dry sector this week, perhaps as players rush to complete deals before much of Asia celebrates, at the very least, a long weekend out of the office. Bullish sentiment at the largest end of the size curve sees 6 Newcs/Capes traded with market players seeking opportunity for the asset plays in the 10-15yo field. Scrubber fitted Newcastlemaxes QING MAY/LAN MAY 206K DWT SWS 2012/2011 were bought by Winning at USD 73M enbloc, exceeding previous price expectations. Elsewhere ArcelorMittal offloaded 3 post panamax bulkers.

Shipping stocks were topic of discussion this week as Al Jazeera reported, and then retracted, that a ceasefire had been brokered between Israel and Hamas. This sent a number of stocks spiralling down over investor fears that this latest period of disruption to shipping would be over. Otherwise, it was a generally uneventful week, with 3 tanker sales reported. Scrubber fitted MILTIADIS JUNIOR 320K DWT SWS 2014 was sold for USD 80M, setting a new benchmark for 10 year old VLCCs, while Ardmore has kickstarted their fleet renewal with the acquisition of MR tanker ST. PAULI 49K DWT HMD 2017, the unit now the most modern of their fleet.   Impending Lunar New Year could be the reason for the healthy liquidity this week, with participants rushing to complete deals before the market with inevitably takes a breather during the holidays. The Supramax subsector demonstrated why it is such a competitive space, with a total of 7 ships changing hands this week. SOLAR AFRICA 58K DWT TESS CEBU 2011 was the standout transaction in the surpas as it sold for a healthy USD 17.8M. Elsewhere, Agricore have purchased their first Capesize unit, buying scrubber fitted SEAMATE 177K DWT SWS 2010 for USD 26M.

Tanker transactions dominate the wires this week with sturdier prices further emphasizing the latest trend. Although products have seen most of this action, the sale of the EUROCHAMPION 2004 (164K DWT 2005 HHI) for $40m shows that the trend is very much apparent for crude as well. Product tanker tonnage has seen stronger spot and term rates which has encouraged buyers and resulted in several transactions. One of which is the MT LR2 MARE ORIENS (110K DWT 2008 MITSUI CHIBA) sold to Chinese buyers for $42m.  Even though tankers dominated the S&P market this week, dry has seen it’s fair bit of action as we are slowly approaching Chinese New Year. Asset pricing is mostly flat with a positive pricing bias for modern tonnage. This positive bias is prevalent in this week’s sale of the MV SSI PRIVILEGE and MV SSI SPLENDID (63K DWT 2019 JINLING) which sold en bloc for $30m each.

This week has seen a pickup in tanker activity with vintage tonnage leading the charge by capturing the bulk of the action. Geopolitical uncertainty along with ever increasing tensions in the Red Sea continue to apply upward pressure on rates which would suggest appreciating values in the near term that could trigger increased liquidity in the modern front. Noteworthy sales are the LR2 FAIR SEAS 155k DWT 2008 STX sold to Chinese buyers for a firm $43.5m. LR1 VOLANS 99K DWT 2009 HHI has also changed hands at reported price of $33m illustrating particularly well rallying values for units of that vintage considering she was bought by Sellers in July 2022 at a price of $26m. On the modern side, Scorpio taking current levels to their advantage by cashing in on the scrubber fitted MR2 STI TRIBECA 49K DWT 2015 SPP, which sold for $39.1m.   Busy week on the Dry cargo front which Compared to last week has seen more modern units changing hands. NGM acquiring its third Capesize from Unisea with the purchase of CORONET 182K DWT 2011 Kawasaki at $27m. In the Ultramax segment Parakou Shipping sold their CP GUANGZHOU 63K DWT 2015 CHENGXI and CP TIANJIN 63K DWT 2016 CHENGXI en bloc for $47.6m. Another en bloc deal was reached on the Handysize EURUS VENTURE and NOTOS VENTURE 43K DWT 2017 QINGSHAN S. which sold at $46m.

A subdued week for the tanker S&P market with a number of deals on hold behind the scenes. The unfolding situation in the Red Sea raises the question whether Sellers of large Crude tonnage could hold out and receive premium rates/price levels. This is coupled with the fact that without a very prompt delivery, Buyers would miss out on the best of the winter returns and would be unwilling to pay a premium to do so – resulting in a standoff. Smaller product carriers were the movers this week with ice 1A Handy Tankers DINAH/PLUTO 37K DWT HMD 2008 being sold by Tufton for USD 41.75M en bloc, booking them a sizeable profit on the units. Elsewhere, MR SOCHRINA 46K DWT SUNGDONG 2008 was bought by Besiktas for USD 24M.  A busy week in the Dry sector but in general the story remains the same, which is one of a significant lack of liquidity on modern tonnage. Rates are experiencing a seasonal dip, however, this does not translate to lower values. Quite the contrary for those available modern market units, with some owners taking advantage of the scarcity of candidates and indeed increasing their price expectations. With that in mind, in the one standout modern transaction of the week, scrubber fitted Newcastlemax MINERAL QINGDAO 206K DWT Qingdao Yangfan 2020 was bought by Winning for USD 54.25M. Otherwise Kamsarmax SUPER LUNA 81K DWT JINHAI HI 2016 sold to Modion at USD 22.6M, part of a very active week for ships of this size. Further down the size curve activity thrived with a number of Supramax units blt 07-12 transacted, helping price other candidates in which is a very competitive corner of the market.
Moderate

The unfolding situation in the Red Sea, coupled with the upcoming festive break, meant the S&P market had a rather quiet week. Sellers can be forgiven, as the ramifications of the Red Sea disruption could yet dramatically change price expectations when the market returns to full capacity in the New Year. In a sub-sector that has largely struggled for liquidity in the latter half of the year, scrubber fitted Suezmax SERENEA (158K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2009) sold this week for USD 45.5M. Elsewhere, a trio of 2008-2009 blt MRs sold, helping price other units circulating in the market.  Modern tonnage in the dry market has been hard to come by for most, and this week’s transactions are symptomatic of this. That said, there remains much optimism in the sector going into the New Year, with Capesize rates ticking along around USD 20k/day. The hope will be that momentum can be maintained despite the upcoming Chinese New Year celebrations in early February.

Much of the tanker story this week was to do with an attack on Norwegian owned STST tanker STRINDA 20K DWT FUKUOKA 2006, which was struck by a missile in the Red Sea. Fortunately, there were no injuries sustained but the narrative here is one of increased disruption to a very busy shipping lane, and further unpredictability in an already mercurial market. Aframax AEGEAN POWER 115K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2007 was privately sold at a very firm price of USD 41M, which will fuel speculation over whether this is a new benchmark, or whether there were other factors at play. Elsewhere ice 1B handy tanker BLUE TRADER 37K DWT HMD 2005 sold to Turkish Buyers at USD 17.4M.  Eagle Bulk shares were the big winner this week in the dry market following the announcement of an all-stock acquisition by Star Bulk. The combined company will boast a total fleet of 169 bulkers and over USD 2BN in market cap. On the vessel side, 7 sales kept the market ticking over with the most significant being 3x Capesize units MINERAL TEMSE/DESTELBERGEN/BRUGGE 175K DWT NEW TIMES 2010/2011 bought by EGPN for total of USD 63.5M. With seasonal slowdown expected over Christmas/New Year and then Chinese New Year, market players will be keen to tie up as many deals as possible in the next week.

The Dry market, despite the recent uptick in earnings, still lacks liquidity. Market players will need to see this earnings surge sustained for at least a few months before we see any significant changes in buying impetus, and with Chinese New Year swiftly following the Christmas holidays, this seems unlikely. The few sales that are reported this week are useful in the sense they help benchmark a number of candidates on the market, such as Supramax ERMIONE (56K DWT IHI 2008) sold by Byzantine for USD 14M, and handy VULLY (35K DWT Shinan 2011) selling for USD 13.2M.   VLCCs are making the most noise on the tanker front, with three sales reported this week. Scrubber fitted VLCC ATHENIAN FREEDOM (299K DWT HHI 2013) was bought by Greek interests at USD 73.5M, however it is the behind the scenes candidates that have been igniting conversations at festive industry get togethers. One thing is for sure, should the modern candidates being discussed transact at their rumoured levels, the modern VLCC market will witness a significant jump in values. At the other end of the age curve, HARAD (303K DWT Samsung 2001) sold for USD 30M to Chinese buyers, still well above scrap levels and a staggering delta of USD c.100M to current newbuild price ideas. Elsewhere, Greek interests picked up LR1 LEON APOLLON (75K DWT HMD 2009) for USD 28.5M.
