The dry market rally continued this week as Capesize earnings saw their biggest daily jump since 2010, this was particularly prevalent in the North Atlantic market where tonnage is most scarcely available. Scrubber fitted Capesize duo CHOW/COMANCHE 181K DWT SWS 2016 are primed to take advantage of this rally, being bought by Genco for USD 41.3M each. Smaller sizes are also seeing a welcomed push in rates as a result, after a fairly uneventful Q3. This bump in rates, if sustained, will begin to justify the comparatively firm price expectations across the bulk market. This could also entice more cash rich owners looking to diversify, such as Pyxis, who bought scrubber fitted Kamsarmax PEDHOULAS CHERRY 82K DWT JIANGSU NEWYANGZI 2015 at USD 26.5M.    News of OPEC+ production cuts rather dampened the festive sprit in the Tanker market as rates will likely see a dip in the short term, but in the medium to longer term result in higher ton miles. In reality, these cuts won’t drastically change the overwhelmingly positive overall tanker story. MR tankers have been making headlines this week as some units have reported TCE earnings in excess of USD 100K/day, no wonder there is a swell of interest here with a number of ongoing discussions behind the scenes, surely to set new price benchmarks once completed.

Whether it was celebrated or not, tanker market players would have been giving thanks this week for the fortuitous position they find themselves in as the sector remains hot. Although a relatively quiet week, behind the scenes there are rumours of a 2019 eco VLCC seeing interest in the region of USD 110m levels that would recalibrate valuation models across the sector. Older Aframax tankers have received a boost this week with AEGEAN MYTH (115K DWT 2006 SAMSUNG) being transacted at USD 37.5M to Chinese buyers, showing that current freight rates are proving hard to resist. Elsewhere, Chinese interests secured J19 ALBATROSS TRADER (19K DWT 2015 USUKI) for USD 29.3M.    Rallying chartering markets on the Capesize front is building up anticipation for an ever-increasing level of enquiry. NGM securing in time the Capesize sisters GLORY/HONOR (179K DWT 2011 HHI) for USD 26.5M per unit from compatriots Unisea - levels that most would consider a relative bottom in light of ever bettering earnings. Final price on Ultramax ZEYNO (63K DWT 2014 DAYANG) was revealed to be USD 22M, rather in line with market expectations. With most players cautiously heading into 2024, the busy nature of the S&P market in this year-end suggests sentiment is mending across segments with hope that these invigorated earnings are here to stay.

Tankers have taken a breather this week as the Dry bulk segment dominates the S&P market. Headlines were stolen by Transmed sale of their AGIS (182k dwt Namura 2023) to Arcelor Mittal, what is considered a very firm $67m. Among other Capesize transactions was the sale of the FRONTIER BRILLIANCE (181k dwt Imabari 2013), which was sold for $30.6m with SS/DD due. Elsewhere, benchmarks are also being set on modern Kamsarmax front with the resale of the AP LOVRIJENAC (82k dwt Hantong 2024) to NNC for $37.62m. In the Ultramax segment, the GLORY HARVEST (63k dwt Hantong 2014) was sold for $21.5m. This sale includes a 1-year time charter to Pan Ocean, explaining the slightly higher than expected price. There have been several Handysize sales, with the most noteworthy being the sale of the APRILIA (36k dwt Jiangdong 2017) to Greek buyers for $20.2m.  In the wake of last week’s numerous tanker transactions, we have recorded 3 Aframax sales supporting last week's activity. One of these was the IRIDESCENT (112k dwt New Times 2009) which was sold for $40m. Following last week's purchase of 8 LR2’s, Torm has this week sold 2xLR1’s, the TORM ESTRID and scrubberfitted TORM ISMINI (74k dwt HHI 2004) en bloc for $40m. Lastly some activity in the MR segment with the sale of the SEAWAYS LORAIN (51k dwt STX 2008) for $24.5m and the FALCON SEXTANT (50k dwt STX 2009) for $25.5m.

A busy week again across S&P dominated by Tanker sales, despite a significant proportion of the market occupied in Dubai for Bahri week. On the larger crude tonnage, New Shipping took C. CHALLENGER (313K DWT DALIAN 2013) & C. SPIRIT (313K DWT HHI 2013) for USD 65M and USD 67M respectively, these were sold with tc attached hence the slightly lower than expected price. In the Afra/LR2 sector TORM were extremely busy this week, taking in 8 LR2 tankers built between 2010 – 2012 built at Hyundai Samho for a combination of USD 239M and 5.5M shares (roughly equating to USD 399M), and selling scrubber fitted LR2 TORM MARINA (109K DWT DALIAN 2007) for USD 36.2M to Chinese buyers. This sector is very busy behind the scenes, with more deals likely to emerge before the end of year. Activity continued further down the size curve, with CHEMTRANS URANUS/MERCURY/LEO (37K DWT HMD 2006) selling for USD 18M each to Middle East buyers.  A fairly uneventful week on the Dry front as asset values remain relatively high compared to the available earnings in the market. Buyers are therefore encouraged to go bargain hunting in order to have a more attractive investment case, but this of course relies on a motivated seller. Liquidity is still there however, with NIPPON MARU (55K DWT MITSUI 2011) selling for USD 17.3M, and MARLIN V (61K DWT IWAGI ZOSEN 2013) for USD 21.3M. Elsewhere, Genco are rumoured to be the buyers of scrubber fitted Capesize CHOW (181K DWT SWS 2016), which sold in October for USD 41.3M, after releasing an announcement they are due to take delivery of a scrubber fitted SWS 2016 Cape this month.

Quite simply, the S&P world at the moment is a very busy one. Conflict, adverse weather, and humanitarian crises dominate the headlines, impacting long and short-term strategy, all while market players rush to conclude deals before the end of the calendar year. In the only large crude transaction, VLCC JIU YUE (305K DWT DSME 2007) sold for USD 48M. Behind the scenes on the large crude tonnage there is swell of activity, which will dominate reports to come over the next few weeks. Elsewhere, Scorpio sold scrubber fitted MR STI AMBER (49K DWT HMD 2012) for USD 33.9M, which will help price other units in the market.  The Dry market is proving tough to measure as the BDI hit a seven-week low, but appetite on the asset side remains high. There is a steady flow of Japanese built units hitting the market, but mostly on the older end of the size curve, with buyers being forced to either wait for younger Japanese units or shift their attention to modern Chinese built bulkers. An example of this is Ultramax FJM GLORY (61K DWT COSCO Dalian 2019) selling for USD 29.6M. In the largest sub size, Capesize OCEAN CORONA (180K DWT Koyo 2009) was sold for USD 20.8M and SATORI (177K DWT Mitsui 2007 ) sold for USD 18.5M, these were to Chinese and Turkish buyers, respectively.

A fairly volatile week in the Tanker market takes nothing away from the overall picture that good times are here to stay in this sector. Aframax spot rates are driving increased interest in this size, with some routes paying a mouth-watering USD 100k/day+. Little coincidence then, that the headline transaction this week comes in the form of ice 1A LR2 HIBERNIAN TIDE (108K DWT 2019 SWS), to Minerva at USD 65.5M. VLCC TIMMUS (318K DWT 2002 HHI), sold at USD 32M, a softening on last done, GOOD NEWS (319K 2002 HSHI) at USD 34.75M.  A softer week in the Dry market and a subsequent correction in the recent strong rates hasn’t discouraged buyers, as liquidity remains strong. Otherwise, a rather unremarkable week in the sector as the reported sales do little to raise eyebrows. Japanese tonnage is at the top of most buyers’ shopping lists, with modern tonnage still tricky to acquire, hence the older sales as below. In the most modern of the transactions, Ultramax ATLANTIC ISLAND (61K DWT 2014 IWAGI ZOSEN) sold for USD 24M to Greek buyers while Capesize FRONTIER BRILLIANCE (180K DWT 2013 IMABARI) sold at USD 30M.

Much of the market has been left scratching their heads as LR1s AESOP/SIENA (74K DWT 2012 HMD) were purchased by Naftomar for a very firm price of USD 41.5M each. Details are yet to emerge on the transaction, so pricing on existing market candidates of that age remain unchanged for now. With the ongoing situation in the Middle East on a knife edge, it would appear that tanker sentiment will remain firm for some time. NAT purchased Suezmax CHEROKEE (158K DWT 2016 HYUNDAI SAMHO) for USD 72M from CM Lemos, the firm price highlighting the relative lack of available candidates in the market.   Liquidity continues to be a feature of the dry market, as market players jostle for position. Despite a recent uptick, the market is still relatively low in terms of asset values, so there is much opportunity for those looking to divest into Dry. In the rather traditional pattern for this stage of the dry cycle, a number of Japanese ships went into Greek buyers – ROYAL FUKUYAMA (82K DWT 2013 TSUNEISHI) was sold for USD 23M, and Ultramax SANTA FRANCESCA (61K DWT 2016 SHIN KASADO) sold for USD 26.8M. Elsewhere, scrubber-fitted Capesize CYMONA IRON (176K DWT 2011 SWS) was sold for USD 26M.

The unfolding geopolitical turmoil in the Middle East is generating headlines and stirring concerns about contagion risks in the region. Although the events haven't yet impacted commodity pricing or shipping rates, the concerns are evident. This week’s Tanker transactions seem like an echo from last week, but this week focused on 15 year old tonnage. We’ve seen the sale of the LR1 CHEMTRANS AEGEAN (76k dwt DALIAN 2007) for $22m and the sale of the MR2 ELIZABETH M (50k dwt SLS 2007) for $22m and MR2 CONSTANCE (50k dwt SPP 2008) for $23.5m.   Although the dry spot market appears to have taken a breather, the secondhand market appears to persist with the volume of transactions. We have recorded the sale of 5 Capesize units built between 2007 and 2010 with pricing pretty much flat from last week demonstrated by the sale of the Capesize AQUA BONANZA (180k dwt IMABARI 2010) sold for $23m. Other noteworthy dry sales are the Ultramax CP SHANGHAI (63k dwt CHENGXI 2015) sold for $23.5m and the Supramax XING HONG DA 8 (58k dwt YANGZHOU DAYANG 2012) sold for $12.7m.

Headlines at the end of this week are dominated by Frontline & Euronav, and the proposed end to a very public battle for control of the Belgian Tanker giant. John Fredriksen’s Frontline, if approved by regulatory bodies and relevant shareholders, will walk away with 24 Euronav VLCCs in exchange for their 26.12% stake in the company. Transactions this week were concentrated in the MR sector, with five units changing hands. The 22 tanks, fully IMO2 capable TRF BERGEN (49K DWT HYUNDAI VINASHIN 2015) was sold for USD 37M, while EVINOS (49K DWT STX 2013) and SANDPIPER PACIFIC (51K DWT SUNGDONG 2013) both received around USD 34M. Finally, Turkish buyers paying a strong USD 40.5M each for the two 2016 SPP built MR's LACERTA and BORA BORA.   Despite the Golden Week holiday in China, liquidity in the dry sector remains strong. The Capesize market has bounced this week as manufacturing has rebounded. This has filtered down across the dry market where price expectations are firming across the board, meaning those waiting out the bottom of the market might well have missed their chance for now. The standout transaction is Sinokor selling scrubber fitted pair COMANCHE/CHOW (180K DWT SWS 2016) for USD 43.5M each en bloc to buyers Arcelor Mittal, and CONTAMINES (180K DWT SWS 2016) for USD 41.5M to Neda Maritime. Elsewhere, scrubber-fitted Kamsarmax LORD STAR (82K DWT SANOYAS 2013) sold for USD 23.8M.

The standout transaction in the Tanker market is CRUDESUN/CRUDEMED (115K DWT DAEHAN 2018) sold for USD 70M each. We understand the vessels are fixed to Unipec for 3 years at USD 40K/day. A further transaction in the Aframax/LR2 sector is PS VENEZIA (108K DWT HUDONG ZHONGHUA 2010) at USD 37.5M (DD Due) to Vietnamese buyers Fgas, notably fetching a lower-than-expected price in what is quite an in-demand part of the Afra/LR2 age curve, even with surveys due. Elsewhere SHANDONG ZIHE (40K DWT SHINA 2004) sold via online bidding platform at USD 14.45M.  Volume in the dry sector remains high, with sales across the size curve this week. This comes despite murmurs in the market of a possible slight further softening in the space before the anticipated recovery, only time will tell when we hit the bottom of this dry cycle. JP Morgan acquired 3x large handysize vessels FENGNING/FUNING/FOOCHOW (39K DWT CHENGXI 2015) for USD 19.5M each, around the same levels as last done on a 2015 unit (CIELO DI VALPARAISO) at USD 20M in March 2023. Offers were due this week on Capesize SUIGO (174K DWT NAMURA 2011), and she was eventually sold at USD 23.5M to Greek buyers.

A relatively quiet week in the second-hand tanker market with much of the industry’s attention focused on the newbuilding story. 11% of the existing Suezmax fleet is now on order, this subsector seeing the highest number of orders in a single year in the past decade. Behind the scenes however, Aframax tanker interest is swelling, and owners are seemingly happy to part with tonnage, often at hugely attractive levels to what they initially purchased their ships for. Particularly FULMAR (115K DWT 2009 HANJIN HI), sold to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 39.5M, almost double what Union Maritime paid for the unit in 2019 at auction. Older large tankers seem to have cooled with the sale of VLCC GOOD NEWS (319K DWT 2002 HHI) at just under USD 35M, a unit that was asking over USD 40M before the summer. Pyxis has sold its eco MR tanker PYXIS EPSILON (50K DWT 2015 SPP) for a whopping USD 40.7M to US buyers. At this stage we can only speculate if the deal is linked to the US Tanker Security Program aimed at boosting access to commercial product tankers to safeguard oil shipping for its armed forces.   Liquidity in the Dry sector continues to grow as it feels ‘now is the time’ to make a move. All sizes of modern Japanese built tonnage appear on most prospective buyers’ wish lists, thus making available units highly competitive. Those willing to look at slightly older units are seeing an increased availability of candidates, something which will excite potential asset players. In the Kamsarmax sector, WESTERN MONACO (81K DWT 2016 HANTONG) was sold for a firm USD 26M while NORD SUN (82K DWT 2013 TSUNEISHI CEBU) was bought by Greek buyers at USD 21.8M. Elsewhere, Capesize GRACIOUS ETERNITY (180K DWT 2009 IMABARI) was sold to Chinese buyers at USD 21.9M.

No action on the larger Tanker front this week as spot rates continue to give a lethargic feel to what is fundamentally, a strong market. Interest, however, seems to be swirling around the Aframax space with a number of candidates entering the market. CENTENNIAL SAPPORO (110K DWT Mitsui 2008) bought by Beks for USD 35.5M with delivery SS due, and FULMAR (115K DWT Hanjin HI 2009) at USD 39.5M to Middle Eastern buyers will certainly help guide the growing list of enquiries. In the MR space, SUNNY APATITE (49K DWT GSI 2016) sold for USD 34M, while GRAND ACE8 (46K DWT HMD 2008) at USD 23.8M with SS passed, showing that despite a cooling since highs of earlier this year there remains robust interest in this sector.  Activity across Dry remains strong as prices stabilise. The most notable of the recent deals is 4 x Crown 63 Dayang Ultramax units GIANTS CAUSEWAY/SADLERS WELLS/GALILEO/CAPE CROSS (63K DWT 2014-2015) being bought en bloc at USD 86M by Greek buyers. This provides an interesting benchmark for what is clearly a high level of buying interest of modern Ultramaxes. Two transactions in the Kamsarmax sector as GENEVA STAR (81K DWT Tsuneishi Cebu 2015) received numerous offers, eventually going to Chinese buyers at USD 26.5M, and CUMA (83K DWT Tsuneishi 2006) acquired by Bulkseas for USD 13.2M.

ATHENIAN FREEDOM (299K DWT 2013 HHI) to Chinese buyers (scrubber to be installed prior delivery) at USD 78M, and Tsakos fixing a VLCC on 3yr charter for USD 55k/day signals the underlying strength of the tanker story, despite the limp spot market and talk of lagging Chinese demand. Older large tankers still hold their value, with Chinese buyers paying USD 37.8M for LILA ORLANDO (158K DWT 2005 DSME). Elsewhere, Bahri offloaded 2x Zinc-coated MRs in the form of NCC NAJD/HIJAZ (45K DWT 2005 HMD) at USD 17.2M each.    Across the bulk market, buyers are jostling for tonnage as some market participants speculate that we have either reached, or are about to reach, the bottom of the market. There will be a healthy flow of sales from now until the end of the year, not because owners are suffering, but because they will want to position themselves and structure their fleets to profit from improving conditions next year. Ultramax SANTA MARIA (61K DWT 2014 IMABARI) sold to Greek buyers at USD 23.5M, reinforcing the ongoing value correction. Enquiry has picked up dramatically in recent weeks in the handy sector, where we have seen 4 sales this week, most modern of which NORD SAVANNAH (37K DWT 2013 SAIKI) sold for USD 16.8M.

A slow week across the sale and purchase market sees only one sale reported in the tanker sector with CAPT THANASIS 40K DWT HMD 2004 selling at just under USD 18M. Across the larger units, despite much of the market returning from holidays, S&P discussions are yet to regain momentum given a limp sentiment in the spot market.   The dry market is similarly quiet with only three sales to report. The most notable being NORD PACIFIC 61K DWT SHIN KURUSHIMA 2018 selling for USD 27.15M. The last transaction of a 2018 blt Japanese unit was in July when KK PROGRESSION 64K TSUNEISHI 2018 achieved USD 28.5M which reaffirms the gradual softening in values for these younger Japanese built units.

Asset players are driving a surge in genuine buying interest across the Dry market. Where perhaps purchase enquiries over the last few months seemed like more of an information gathering exercise, buyers are now ready to capitalise on the recent market price correction. Despite this surge in buying interest, many subsectors are still facing weakened returns at least in the short term, thus justifying lower price levels. Capesize continues to dominate in terms of liquidity with 5 sales reported this week. Of those, IANTHE (180K DWT DSME 2009) sold for USD 21M while YUAN FU STAR (176K RONGSHENG 2011) sold to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 22.3M. Elsewhere lower down the size curve, ongoing deals are the talk of the market, likely to have significant impact on prices once completed.   Discussions on Tankers at the upper end of the size curve appear to be resuming after the summer hiatus, however, at levels lower than initially proposed. That said, general outlook across the sector remains bullish especially as the winter months approach. Activity was restricted to the smaller sizes this week with Union selling MR BRUNSWICK (45K DWT SHIN KURUSHIMA 2010) to PV TRANS for USD 24M, and Maritime Asset Partners selling Handy Tanker ACAMAR (37K DWT HMD 2011) for USD 23.4M.

In what has otherwise been an uneventful week in the tanker S&P markets, UK buyers are reported to have acquired scrubber fitted Suezmax NAMSEN 157K DWT NEW TIMES 2016 for USD 67M. The last comparable sale was in June when EPS paid USD 75M for scrubber fitted ELANDRA OSPREY 157K HHI 2018.  The downwards correction of dry values is gathering pace as the transaction liquidity begins to pick up . Capesize ARIADNE 180K DWT DSME 2009 was hotly contested, and eventually sold at USD 21.25M to UK buyers. Demand is growing in the 2008-2014 built range of Capesize as opportunistic owners look to find a bargain asset play. Capesize MOUNT APO 176K DWT RONGSHENG 2012 was bought by Peter Doehle for just under USD 25M, helping price similar assets in this sector. Elsewhere, MBA GIOVANNI/ROSARIA 93K DWT JIANGSU NEWYANGZI 2010/11 sold to Samudera for 33.5M en bloc.

With the summer in full swing, many Tanker S&P discussions have found themselves on hold. Buying interest has more or less dried up, which has forced sellers of the decidedly thin number of candidates circulated in the market to reevaluate their price expectations. This has coincided with rates slipping across the larger end of the size curve, putting buyers back in the driving seat. It seems, for now at least, the next transactions will not eclipse last done but instead will provide the wet market with a much-needed correction in values. This week’s sales are dominated by smaller tankers with Celsius continuing to offload their older units, this time in the form of MR2 CELSIUS ROSKILDE (46K DWT 2009 HMD) for USD 25M. Elsewhere, scrubber fitted Suezmax MONTE TOLEDO (150K DWT 2004 UNIVERSAL) sold for USD 35M.  The Dry sector price correction, something which has been discussed in the market since Q4 2022, is finally taking hold with market candidates attracting interest at c.10-15% lower than original asking price. That said, there hasn’t been a rush of sales candidates to meet the ever-increasing enquiry. Japanese built eco units are still at the top of buyers’ shopping lists but the lack of replacement ships being delivered from yards are stifling those looking for a potential bargain. In a rare example of a modern Japanese ship changing hands, Meadway Shipping picked up scrubber fitted Ultramax NORD AMAZON (64K DWT 2020 OSHIMA) for USD 32M. Furthermore, in the Ultramax sector, SSI FORMIDABLE (63K DWT 2017 JINLING) sold for USD 27M.

The roaring tanker S&P market has turned to a whisper as buyers take a backseat amid feelings of toppy pricing, and a general lull in activity. That said, there is still a trickle of transactions to report this week, concentrated in the MR sector. DONG-A TRITON 50K DWT HMD 2015 sold for USD 38.5M, levels which will not excite other sellers of similarly aged tonnage, who have been marketing their units with expectations of xs USD 40M in mind. Of course, owners will not be too phased, with earnings still healthy in this part of the size curve.   Sellers in the dry market will not be hurried by the increased level of enquiry, despite the dwindling earnings environment. A shared positive outlook for end Q3/Q4 by owners means that lowball offers are being duly ignored. Mostly older ships changing hands this week with NYK shedding capesize OCEAN COBALT 180K DWT IMABARI 2008 for USD 19.4M, and Lomar picking up JOY 79K DWT JINHAI HI 2011 for USD 14M.

One reported sale in the Tanker market this week rather speaks for itself. Tanker S&P activity has shuddered to a halt with summer looming, along with a feeling that prices particularly on larger crude assets are peaking, at least for now. The longer-term outlook remains bullish, shown in the interest for Oman Shipping 2010/2011 blt VLCC trio FIDA/SIFA/SAHAM inviting offers this week, rumoured to have c.15 parties registered with opening offers around USD 62-64M per unit.   Interest in Dry bulk is higher behind the scenes than what the deal flow suggests. Buyers are jostling for position on assets across the size curve, as they look for their next play. Of course, this relies on Sellers readjusting their price expectations, despite the overall optimism in the sector. Ultramax KAMBOS 63K DWT COSCO ZHOUSHAN 2015 has been sold to Greek Buyers at USD 24.5M, representing a softening since last done of BCH BRAMBERG (ex DIOMIDIS) 63K DWT JIANGSU JINLING 2015 at USD 25.5M back in April.

Older crude tankers are still achieving record premiums, but one cannot ignore a slight toppy feeling as prices stabilize, rather than continue to rise as they have done over the last 12 months. Of course, the USD 42.5M achieved for VLCC LULU 316K DWT HHI 2003 is still extremely healthy, but it feels as though a ceiling has been reached at the older end of the age curve. Elsewhere long-time sales candidate Aframax MINERVA ZOE 105K DWT HHI 2004 was sold for USD 31M, a good price for sellers given many buyers are now pricing these older Afras at sub USD 30M.   A flurry of Kamsarmax transactions dominated the dry sector this week. JY HONGKONG 81K DWT CHENGXI 2019 was sold via commercial auction at USD 30M, showing a softening in values from last done AQUAVITA SUN 81K DWT JIANGSU HANTONG 2019 at USD 32M in March. The optimistic argument in the dry sector is that sluggishness seen in the China recovery story is behind us, and the outlook is positive for the rest of the year. However, in reality, question marks remain over the immediate summer period, and how the market will react. Some sellers are open to adjusting their expectations as underlying values soften, which opens the door for potential asset players, seen in Thenamaris’ purchase of Kamsarmax LORD STAR 82K DWT SANOYAS 2013 at USD 23.2M. Capesize values continue to soften, seen in the sale of AQUAENNA 175K DWT JINHAI 2011 for USD 22M to Costamare.

The tanker charter market has a ‘summery’ feel to it this week, with looming production cuts and public holidays in China casting doubt over earnings. Differing strategies were making headlines in the S&P space, with Ridgebury confirming their exit from shipping, while Tor Olav Troim announcing Magni Partners’ intention to order two LNG dual-fuel VLCCs for 2026/2027 delivery at region $130m per ship – thus legitimising the much-speculated top end of the VLCC value curve. In the modern Suezmax sector, scrubber-fitted ELANDRA OSPREY (157K DWT HYUNDAI SAMHO 2018) was bought by EPS from Vitol for $75m, with sellers showing that shrewd asset plays can be actioned even for modern ships, having bought the unit for $62.5m back in 2019. Elsewhere, Ridgebury’s selling spree is over, as RIDGEBURY GALILEO (47K DWT HMD 2006) is sold for xs $19m.  There were some unusual premiums being paid in the dry sector this week, despite the general bearish feeling in the market. Supramax CORINTHIAN EMERALD (57K DWT STX JINHAE 2012) was sold to Middle Eastern buyers for an eyebrow raising $19.25m, leaving many market participants scratching their heads. Vega Bulk exercised a purchase option on Ultramax HANTON TRADER III (63K DWT HANTONG 2014) at $23.6m, which helps price other Chinese built Ultramax units at similar ages on the market. Deltas between Chinese and Japanese tonnage are widening in this current slump which has encouraged more of a ‘wait and see’ approach, while some buyers are opting to change their requirements to solely focus on Japanese built units, despite the evident lack of available market tonnage. Either way, deal flow seems it will be an issue across dry for some time to come.

An increasing level of uncertainty is getting hold of the dry SnP markets with a subdued sentiment leading potential buyers to take a wait and see position unless a discount to last done can be secured. A number of vessels have however changed hands this week, notably in the Kamsarmax space where two units have been sold, setting much needed benchmarks in a segment that has seen limited activity in recent past. The Chinese controlled JY BULK (82k dwt, Chengxi , 2018) has been sold at Usd 28.5m while the Korean built DANHIL (82kdwt, Sugdong, 2012) was sold with her balance of TC attached at Usd 23.5m. Clearer signs of softening values can be seen in the Supramax sector with some Sellers of circa 10-year-old units deciding to go meet an ever-softening bid. More resistance is of course witnessed on more modern Ultramax designs with Owners reluctant to entertain the lower levels currently indicated in the market.  Very little to report on the secondhand tanker front which continues to see a thin list of available modern tonnage unless a substantial premium is offered. A subdued activity which is however not reflective of the bullish sentiment shared by most tanker players, a positive outlook which becomes more apparent on the newbuilding front with an ever increasing number of contracts being placed in China.

With much of the market convening in Oslo for Norshipping, the tanker market is excused for having a quieter week on the SNP front, that said, outlook and values remain firm. MR2 CELSIUS RIGA (46K DWT HMD 2010) affirmed the strength of this sub sector, achieving $28.5M to US based buyers.   The dry market appeared to somewhat stabilise this week after recent volatility, however general sentiment remains uncertain as we approach the summer period. This could provide an opportunity for buyers to pick up some discounted tonnage in the short term, with price ideas generally softening across the sector. Elsewhere, Capesize HERUN ZHOUSHAN (181K DWT SWS 2017) sold at $42M, the first sale of a modern Capesize since March.

In what looks like a good deal for DHT, its purchase of five-year-old scrubber fitted VLCC MARIA P. LEMOS (319K DWT HHI 2018) at USD 94.5M stands out. The price is well below market consensus on values which arguably have been inflated by Barhi's purchase in November 2022 of ELANDRA DENALI/ELBRUS (299K DWT HHI 2020) at USD 112M each. That said, despite the big numbers, there is very little liquidity in VLCCs aged 5 and younger. In what has become a very competitive space in the market, 10-15 yo Suezmaxes, Frontline sold non scrubber fitted FRONT NJORD (156K DWT RONGSHENG 2010) at USD 44.5M. This, in comparison to the sale of its scrubber fitted sister EVERBRIGHT in March at USD 42M, shows the trajectory of this market. Rounding off the larger tanker sales, Aframax duo STAR PROSPERITY (115K DWT SASEBO 2009 ) and DAKOTA STRENGTH (115K DWT SAMSUNG 2007) both sold to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 43M and USD 40M respectively.   Alarm bells are sounding in the dry market with both the BDI and average spot rates languishing. To put it into context, this week the Capesize Atlantic Index registered its third largest daily decline on record. Time will tell whether, or how soon, concerns over the Chinese demand story will impact the second-hand market. It is worth remembering that despite the speculation over the performance of the dry market in what has been a rollercoaster 1H 2023, prices have generally remained firm, with sellers unwilling to take a haircut despite volatile rates. In the only headline transaction, Ultramax GREAT VENTURE (61K DWT COSCO DALIAN 2019) was bought by Greek buyers for USD 30.3M.

Vintage tanker plays are still making headlines with New Shipping doubling their investment on the VLCC GOOD NEWS (319K DWT SAMHO HI 2002) at USD 43M to undisclosed buyers. It is too soon to tell whether the flagging and insurance issues plaguing vintage tanker operator Gatik will impact the level of buying enquiry for older tanker tonnage, but it is worth monitoring, as registries and P&I clubs begin to scrutinize trading patterns of these older units.    Sentiment in the dry sector is waning at least in the short term, as global worries over Chinese demand increase. Nevertheless, despite more market players adopting a wait and see approach to second hand vessel acquisitions, there has been a steady stream of transactions reported this week. In the modern Ultramax sector TAURUS/ARIES CONFIDENCE  (63K DWT NEW DAYANG 2018) were sold to Spar Shipping for USD 28.5M per unit. With Chinese units generally much more available than their Japanese equivalents, it will be interesting to see whether this transaction sparks a run on the available Chinese built units in the market. Capesize BAO MAY (178K DWT SWS 2010) was sold for USD 25.5M, perhaps showing that slightly younger units are being considered by market players, following the recent spike in demand for vintage Capesize units.

Scrubber-fitted Aframax SOUTHERN GLORY (108K DWT TSUNEISHI 2019) is the standout transaction in the wet market, purchased by Eastern Pacific for USD 66M, thus affirming value for Aframax units of this age following the recent sales of SPERCHIOS and ARISTOKLIS. Otherwise, it was the familiar tale of older tonnage achieving firm prices, often at huge premiums to the previous purchase price. No transaction represents this better than WONDER POLARIS/BELLATRIX (115K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2005/2006) selling en bloc for USD 72M, compared to their respective purchase prices of USD 13.6M (06/22) and USD 18.15 w/TC attached (12/21). In the only VLCC transaction of the week, having failed previously at USD 53M, BALITC SUNRISE (309K DWT HHI ULSAN 2005) sold to Chinese buyers at USD 51.5M.    Units at the top end of the size curve are the flavour of the week in the Dry market, making up the majority of transactions. There appears to be a run on vintage Capesize units, with levels on 2004 built vessels exceeding last done on a 2006 built. VICTORIUS/OLYMPIUS (171K DWT HYUNDAI SAMHO 2004) sold en bloc for USD 17M per vessel to Dubai based buyers, which surpasses the USD 16.3M spent earlier in May on the younger C H S SPENDOR (170K DWT IHI 2006). TASIK MELATI (180K DWT KOYO 2004) sold for USD 15.5M, perhaps a slightly lower price than the VICTORIUS/OLYMPIUS due to the manner of sales process (sealed bids/outright offers). Elsewhere in the dry sector owners around the market are reporting disappointing results largely due to the lower earnings environment for the first half of 2023, adding to a widely softening sentiment.

Recent sluggishness seen in the tanker charter market seems to have spilled into the S&P space, as the sector registered an unremarkable week. Asset values remain strong however, with Suezmax CLASSIC (159K DWT HHI 2005) transacting for USD 36.8M, more than double what Seven Islands paid for the unit back in December 2020. Aframax PS PISA (108K DWT Hudong Zhonghua 2010) was sold for USD 36.5M, issues with the vessel condition explaining the lower than market price on the unit. With an enticing rates environment, vintage MRs continue to be in high demand, MR SYMPHONY (46K DWT STX 2004) fetching just under USD 18M. Tanker owners across the size curve are likely asking themselves the same question; how far can this market go?   The dry market remains a target for most market players, seen in the competitiveness for the Capesize DENSA COBRA (180K DWT STX 2011) which had a rumoured 6-7 buyers. This, however, did not prevent the sale from failing, with the unit being circulated around the market once again. There seems to be a run on older Capesize units, seen in TASIK MELATI (180K DWT KOYO 2004) taking offers this week and attracting levels of xs USD 16M, which is well over the last done for a ship of this vintage (C H S Splendor). In the even more competitive Ultramax space, scrubber fitted VOKARIA (63K DWT COSCO YANGZHOU 2020) sold for USD 32M.

Tanker values showing no signs of abating. Another week with pricey Aframax sales; WONDER AVIOR (108K DWT 2004 HHI) achieved USD 30.1m and the one year younger and scrubber-fitted SONGA CORAL (107k 2005 KOYO) is reported sold for USD 35m. To put this into perspective, WONDER AVIOR was purchased by the Sellers in May 2021 for just below USD 10m. Expecting further activity in the sector with the modern scrubber fitted Aframax SOUTHERN GLORY 2019 Tsuneishi seeing a number of buyers getting outright in view of the upcoming offers which are invited on 10th May.  Dry values are moving sideways as seen by the sale of Capesize DENSA COBRA 2011 STX at USD 27.7 which, adjusted for yard, falls is line with the sale in mid-April of STELLA ADA 2011 Dalian at USD 25.6 mill. Japanese owners remain notably absent from the sales lists.

Predictable unpredictability in the tanker charter market did not phase the S&P space as headlines continued to be written by high value transactions. Capital Maritime’s Ice class 1C Aframax ARISTOKLIS (113K DWT DAEHAN 2017) sold for a reported USD 68M, thus reaffirming the demand for modern second hand tankers. Ridgebury continued their tanker selloff with Suezmax RIDGEBURY LESSLEY B (158K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2013) being snapped up by Indonesian buyers for USD 54.5M. Elsewhere it was busy week on the MR front with a number of sales across the age curve. UK based buyers picked up MR KIRIBORA (50K DWT SPP 2013) for USD 33.5M and CELSIUS RANDERS (46K DWT HMD 2010) was sold for USD 26M, helping price units around the 10-year age range.   A busy week for Supramaxes dominates the story in the dry market with 9 out of the 11 sales reported. Tess 58 AMIS LEADER (58K DWT TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN 2010) sold for a firm USD 18M, once again showing the value in good designs. 2010/11 blt Chinese units fetched considerably less, in the form of DAXIA (57K DWT COSCO DALIAN 2010), SANIA (57K DWT QINGSHAN 2010) and HAUT BRION (57K DWT TAIZHOU SANFU 2010) each being sold for region USD 14M. Elsehwere, Ultramax DIOMIDIS (63K DWT JIANGSU JINLING 2015) sold for USD 25.5M.

With much of the market enjoying a few days holiday, activity in the S&P sector ticked along without incident. No sales of larger tankers mean the headlines this week were taken by Advantage Tankers' purchase of three LR1s NAUTICAL DEBORAH/JANINE/SARAH (75K DWT 2018/19 JIANGSU HANTONG) from TRF, for USD 153M. Elsewhere, MRs DI MATTEO (46K DWT 2009 NAIKAI ZOSEN) and SW SOUTHPORT I (47K DWT 2004 STX) were sold for USD 24M and USD 18M respectively, which will help price the units on the market at this end of the age curve. Handytankers VOGE TRUST/DIGNITY (38K DWT 2009 GSI) were sold to Greek buyers at USD 19M per unit.   The dry S&P space has been busy this week despite the holidays, with sales reported across the age and size curve. The highest value deal of the week came in the form of Eagle Bulk selling Supramax trio SANKATY/MONTAUK/NEWPORT EAGLE (58K DWT 2011 YANGZHOU DAYANG) in an en-bloc transaction rumoured to be xs USD 16M per ship. This shows the strengthening bulk market, particularly the swelling demand for Supramaxes of around this vintage. Further up the size curve, Capesize MARAN PIONEER (171K DWT 2004 DAEWOO) sold for USD 18.5M and STELLA ADA (180K DWT 2011 DALIAN) changed hands for USD 25.5M. In the only transaction of a modern ship, Ultramax GLOBAL ROYAL (61K DWT 2022 DACKS) was committed for a rumoured USD 34.7M.

With sentiment in the tanker charter market looking flat, the S&P sector, despite the overall strong market, did little to provide a significant headline. Surprisingly, a 1999 blt Suezmax made the most noise, as WHITE TRADER (150K DWT 1999 NKK) was sold for USD 27M, representing almost double the price the unit would fetch at demolition. Elsewhere, in the very popular MR sector, Parakou sold MR PTI DANUBE (50K DWT 2017 SPP) at USD 41M, a price that initially seemed elevated when the ship reached the market but has quickly been realised as value. Viken sold the last of their HMD Handytankers, with NORVIKEN (37K DWT 2010 HMD) changing hands for USD 23M.  Activity continues to increase in the dry sector with a total of 18 ships having been reported sold this week. JP Morgan purchased Handy trio of ERISORT/ERRADALE/WULIN (39K DWT 2014 CHENGXI) from Swire at USD 20.5M per unit, with MUR to manage the vessels going forward. In the Capesize sector, ROSEBANK (177K DWT 2010 NEW TIMES) was sold for USD 23M and MULAN (176K DWT 2005 TSUNEISHI) transacted for USD 16.25M, sales which will help price the spread of older units at this end of the size curve. Wisdom Marine sold Tess 58 Supramax AMIS ORCHID (58K DWT 2012 TSUNEISHI CEBU) for 18.7M, as Supramax values continue to be squeezed upwards.

Tanker Snp markets were relatively subdued with only a handful of transactions to report this week. Older tonnage is still fetching significant premiums with the Suezmax EUROVOYAGER (159K DWT DAEWOO 2005) reported sold at USD 38M and LR2 STAR PROSPERITY (115K DWT SASEBO 2009) was sold for USD 41M. While interest remains high in the MR space, only one transaction was registered this week as OCEAN III (45K DWT BOHAI 2007) was sold for USD 21.5M.  A busy week in the dry sector sees transactions taking place all across the size and age curve. Tomini splashed out on 2x scrubberfitted Newcastlemax units MP THE BRUSCHI/MP THE VRABEL (208K DWT JIANGSU NEWYANGZI 2020/2021) for a total of USD 121M. They weren’t the only ones to pick up large tonnage as Norden affirmed their commitment to Capesizes with the acquisition of AQUAHAHA/AQUATONKA (179K DWT HHIC 2012) for USD 28M each. Scrubber fitted Capesize MOUNT FABER (176K DWT NAMURA 2008) was sold at USD 22.7M, providing valuable insight to those after a potential asset play at the higher end of the age curve. Despite soaring demand in the Supramax sector, only one transaction was regsitered this week with GF ORIENT (57K DWT STX DALIAN 2011) bought by Chinese buyers for USD 13.5M.

Following last weeks momentum the tanker charter markets levelled as global financial and oil markets were shaken on news of potential banking crisis. In the S&P space, older units continue to receive healthy premiums with VLCCs KASSOS I (319K DWT 2007 HYUNDAI SAMHO) commanding USD 61M and VLCC YUFUSAN (311K DWT 2005 MITSUI) selling for USD 52.3M. Offers were invited on SUEZMAX LILA HONG KONG (159K DWT 2003 BOHAI), eventually seeing Chinese buyers secure the unit for USD 31M. Interest remains high in the MR sector, with rates displaying significant volatility particularly in the Atlantic. Only one transaction though was registered in this sector this week, with MRK Shipmanagement picking up SAFESEA NEHA III (46K DWT 2003 SHIN KURUSHIMA) for USD 13.75M.  Increased activity in the dry S&P market is providing is providing little relief for the ever-swelling number of purchase enquiries in the sector. Seen as the next potential asset play, and an outlet for tanker owners’ increased cash supplies, the demand for dry ships is beginning to push asset values perhaps north of where recent market returns would usually denote. In the headline size category, CAPESIZE pair GOLDEN FENG/SHUI (169K DWT 2009 DAEHAN) were snapped up for USD 23M each by Greek buyers. Elsewhere, another Chinese Ultra sale in the form of ULTRAMAX SOHO PRINCIPAL (63K DWT 2016 YANGZHOU DAYANG), going for USD 26.5M.

The tanker charter market roared back into life this week with the biggest intraday rate jump in recent memory seen yesterday. In the S&P space, healthy MR TC returns are proving too alluring to resist, with market players flocking to snap up units all along the age curve. MTM shed 3 units, MTM MANILA/YANGON/MUMBAI (46K DWT 2003 HMD) to Chinese buyers, while Norden and Ridgebury both offloaded one unit respectively in the form of scrubber fitted NORD SKATE (51K DWT 2009 STX) for USD 24.25M and RIDGEBURY MERCURY (46K DWT 2008 HMD) for USD 21M. Price ideas, particularly for late 2000s units are on the rise, with some prospective buyers beginning to rethink their intentions. In the larger sizes, all over the age curve, prices continue to rise with USD 35M now needed to purchase a 2004 blt Suezmax, seen in the form of KRITI DIAMOND (166K DWT 2004 BRODOSPLIT) to undisclosed buyers.  Elevated activity levels in the dry market have seemingly put the recent market misfortunes firmly in the rear-view mirror, as sentiment and momentum build. Quality designs and yards are in demand with Supramax IVS Pinehurst (58K DWT 2015 TSUNEISHI CEBU) being sold for USD 23.5M by Grindrod to Greek buyers, and Supramax IGNAZIO (58K DWT 2010 TSUNEISHI CEBU) being sold for USD 15M. Last week’s reported sale of Supramax SUPRA ONIKI (57K DWT 2010 QINGSHAN), has since failed at USD 13M, with increased levels likely to be required to develop a new transaction. Oldendorff made headlines on the sales of 4 modern Chinese built scrubber-fitted Ultramax units JAN/JONAS/JENS/JACOB OLDENDORFF (61K DWT 2019 NACKS/DACKS) at USD 32M per unit, market players are sure to be taking note of this in what is a very popular sub sector.

GNMTC stole the tanker headlines this week with the resale acquisition of scrubber fitted Aframax pair DELAWARE/GALVESTON STAR (115K DWT 2023 DAEHAN) at USD 76M per unit, with sellers Atlas making a healthy profit on the original contract price of USD 45M. Elsewhere, the hot ticket in the tanker market appears to be in the MR sector, as players look to cash in on buoyant TC rates. MSEA sold MR MARLIN AMETHYST (51K DWT 2015 COMEC) to Union Maritime for USD 33M, a price that is unlikely to be repeated for foreseeable future as interest surges in modern units. There is also a lot of activity on older MR units, with JOHNNY TRADER (46K DWT 2004 STX JINHAE), SPRUCE EXPRESS (51K DWT 2006 STX JINHAE) and LILA RHINE (51K DWT 2007 STX JINHAE) all being sold this week.  In the dry space, deal flow seems to be the only thing holding the market back as interest remains incredibly high across the size curve (provided the presence of an ECO engine). Supramax pair PACIFIC VISION/DREAM (56K DWT 2013 JIANGSU HANTONG) fetched USD 15.5M per unit, a transaction that should help price a number of similar units in the market. Further to these sales, SUPRA ONIKI (57K DWT 2010 QINGSHAN) sold for USD 13M to undisclosed buyers.

Activity in the Bulker segment was muted this week in comparison to the recent acquisition of a sextet of H Line Newcastlemaxes by Golden Ocean for USD 291M. The vessels will be chartered back to H Line for 36 months at USD 21kpd. Elsewhere in the market, Winning bought Capesize OCEAN CAESAR (180K DWT IMABARI 2008) for USD 20.2M, and Supramax SUN GLOBE (58K DWT TSUNEISHI HI CEBU 2007) sold for USD 14.2M, once again showing that values in the dry sector have managed to hold despite recent negative sentiment. This will be welcome news to those dry sellers who have fended off opportunistic bids in hope for better prices.    The Tanker market continues to read from the same script with premiums being paid for Ice Class units and vessels that would have been scrap candidates only a short while ago. Ridgebury Tankers, who have been proven sellers in this market, sold scrubber-fitted Suezmax RIDGEBURY JUDITH (150K DWT UNIVERSAL 2008) for USD 39.5M. They also sold MR RIDGEBURY KATHERINE Z (50K DWT SPP 2009) at USD 24.8M, into an MR market which seems to be bubbling as players eye healthy returns. Elsewhere, Euronav offloaded ice class 1C Suezmax CAP CHARLES (158K DWT SAMSUNG 2006) for USD 41.5M to Gardsea.

The ageing tanker selloff continued this week with MARAN AQUARIUS (320K DWT 2005 DSME) and SEAHERO (306K DWT 2006 DSME) each fetching over USD 50M. It is easy to see why, when ships of this size and age have almost doubled in value over the last eighteen months. Clear premiums for Ice class units are still very visible in the market with the sale of scrubber-fitted Ice 1A LORELEI (73K DWT 2007 STX JINHAE) for USD 33.5M, compared to both HAFNIA COLUMBIA/KRONBORG (76K/74K DWT 2007 DALIAN/NEW CENTURY) each selling for USD 22M.    Meanwhile in the dry market, timing appears to be key as market players look to position themselves as values seem to be bottoming out. China’s post CNY recovery has been slower than usual, in part to people enjoying their first in person CNY since the pandemic began, but also due to decreased liquidity. This will likely be remedied by additional stimulus in March, which could lead buyers into action. In the highly competitive Japanese Ultramax space, scrubber-fitted NORD POTOMAC (63K DWT I-S SHIPYARD 2016) sold for USD 27.75M setting well needed benchmark in the segment with the most buying enquiries. Over in the Supramax sector, MILOS (56K DWT 2010 COSCO Zhoushan) sold in the high 13s, and Navios unloaded the SERENITAS N (56K DWT 2011 YANGZHOU GUOYU) for USD 12.5m.

Despite a lack of headline grabbing transactions this week, the tanker market fundamentals remain consistent. Spot market players would likely disagree, as sentiment wobbled on the back of Chinese New Year festivities. Ice class 1C Aframax MARATHON (105K DWT 2005 HHI) sold for USD 32M, with premiums for ice class tonnage still being realised by sellers. In keeping with the norm of the last few months, Aframax LILA FUJAIRAH (113K DWT 2007 DSME) was bought by Middle Eastern buyers for USD 37M.  Navios made for the bulk of the story in the dry market, shedding three of their older units; Panamax NAVIOS LIBERTAS/PROSPERITY I (75K DWT 2007 STX JINHAE) and Supramax NAVIOS AMARYLLIS (58K DWT 2008 TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN). The sale of Tess 58 BONITA (58K DWT 2008 TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN) at USD 15.8M shows that despite widely reported hammering of values, there is still money in well regarded yards and designs. As the Dry purchase enquiries continue to mount up, some owners are revaluating their selling positions and putting previously circulated candidates on the backburner, holding out for brighter days ahead.

Another SnP week dominated by tanker activity with headlines stolen by Torm’s acquisition of a total of seven LR1s. The transaction confirmed on Thursday doubles Torm LR1 fleet with 4 vessels bought from Jo Invest AS and a further 3 units from ST Shipping & Transport. Total price tag for the tally stands at Usd 233m marking the substantial appreciation in values we continue to see in the broader tanker space but more particularly on the product front.  Elsewhere in the tanker space the theme of the last few quarters remains unchanged with ice class units and older large tankers finding buyers at hefty premiums.   The limited number of reported sales in the Dry market is not necessarily reflective of the activity brewing under the surface. Buying enquiries are increasing week after week with a number of market players calling the bottom with bids in line with last done. A level of enquiry that up until now has not yet been met with expected flow of market candidates with potential sellers still deliberating their timing. Saying that, this heighten competition and lack of available tonnage is driving certain buyers to offer premiums in order to dig out the right candidate which should lead to more transactions in the near future.

The beginning of Chinese New Year looks to prolong the Tanker charter market’s subdued sentiment, while activity on S&P remains high. No changes from the theme of the last few quarters as ice class units and older large tankers remain the darlings of the S&P market, seen in Ice class 1A Aframax SEAMAGIC (116K DWT 2007 HHI) sold for a hearty USD 47M, and scrubber fitted VLCC FPMC C HONOR (298K DWT 2008 UNIVERSAL) changing hands for USD 55M. In further Aframax activity, KYTHIRA WARRIOR (115K DWT 2006 SANOYAS) and KRITI GALAXY (110K DWT 2006 MITSUI) sold for USD 38M each, showing that even non-Ice class tonnage can benefit from this rising tide.  The Dry market too will be impacted by CNY festivities, but this did not stop Pacific Basin from dominating the headlines this week as they spent USD 125M on 6x Ultrabulk units (4x Japanese blt Ultramaxes, 1x Tsuneishi Cebu Supramax and 1x Imabari blt Handysize). Taking advantage of the recent value correction in c.10 yo Ultra/Supramax units, they have taken position at a time where others are still sat debating whether the bottom of the market has been reached or not. Elsewhere, Greek buyers have seen opportunity in PPMAX AM LIBERIA (  98K DWT 2013 TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN), swooping in at USD 20.50M.

A flurry of activity in the Dry market this week, as players tie up loose ends from the winter break and execute before the inevitable slowdown in S&P activity over the Chinese New Year period. The market will be paying keen attention to the fallout from the first CNY under China’s more relaxed COVID stance, hopeful there is no U turn in policy after the festivities which pre covid represented the biggest migration of people on earth. Transactions of note include Capes AQUANAVIGATOR & AQUASALWADOR (ABT 180K DWT 2011/12 DAEHAN) at USD 25m and USD 27m respectively, widely reported to have been snapped up by Greek interests, a transaction that could indicate a floor has been reached on dry bringing additional comfort to market players that have been patiently timing their next move in the space. Elsewhere the tier II Supramax SUNRISE RAINBOW (ABT 56K DWT 2012 JIANGSU HANTONG) sold for USD 15.25m, piling pressure on the many Supramax sellers in the market.   A lacklustre Tanker charter market hasn’t discouraged the S&P space, as asset values continue to rise. Those with an Ice class notation remain the key beneficiaries, shown in the USD 47.5m received for Suezmax ICE TRANSPORTER (ABT 146K DWT 2006 UNIVERSAL). VLCC COSGREAT LAKE (ABT 298K DWT 2002 NACKS) sold to Middle Eastern buyers for an eyewatering USD 39m, showing the run for older large tankers is not yet done. In the MR space TEN unloaded 6 Ice class 1A units APOLLON/ARIS/AJAX/AFRODITE/ARTEMIS/ARIADNE (ABT 53K DWT 2005 HYUNDAI MIPO) for a price in the region of  USD 21m each.

Despite a slight cooling in the tanker charter space, appetite for second hand units continues to grow as players fight to take up position in a historically strong market. In the standout transaction of the week, Latsco sold their seven year old Aframax FOS ATHENS (105K DWT 2015 HHI) to Turkish buyers for USD 50m. Singapore based Stamford Shipping cashed out of their Aframax exposure, with the sale of GULLIT (108K DWT 2008 SWS) for USD 34m.   In the dry market, the Ultramax sector took centre-stage with the sale of two units - DELSA (63K DWT 2015 ZHEJIANG) and STONY STREAM (64K DWT 2015 CHENGXI), with both vessels fetching USD 24m each. Market players will certainly take note as interest in this size and vintage will only increase further, with many pondering an opportunistic entry into this space over the next few months. Elsewhere, Navios picked up Kamsarmax RICH RAINFOREST (82K DWT 2022 JIANGSU YANGZI-MITSUI) for USD 34.5m.

As the tanker charter market adjusts to new Russian crude regulations, the S&P space remains strong. VLCC SEAKING (318K DWT 2005 HHI) was sold by Thenamaris for USD 51.5m, proving there is still no shortage of suitors for ageing large tankers. Modern scrubber fitted Aframax SOUTHERN ROUSE (108K DWT 2018 TSUNEISHI) sold for USD 62m, having invited offers at the end of November, which should help price the number of Aframax units in the market.   Timing will be crucial in the dry market as players expect a run in Q1/Q2, but also debate on the impact of new regulations, and the reliability of China easing their COVID restrictions. This week’s S&P activity shows that owners must be busy pondering their options as only a handful of sales were seen. Open Hatch Supramax RIO CHOAPA (50K DWT 2012 OSHIMA) sold for USD 16.5m which is basis SS due. Kamsarmax NORD POLLUX (81K DWT 2016 TSUNEISHI CEBU) sold for USD 25.2m which we understand reflects delivery in the Sellers' option until May 2023.

Tanker market players must be running out of superlatives to describe the market, as another bullish week comes to a close. Ice class 1A Aframaxes SAMRAA ALKHALEEJ & ALHANI (114K DWT 2006/07 SAMSUNG HI) sold for USD 86m enbloc, representing an over 30% jump in price compared to the last done back in October (PAROSEA/BLUESEA 113K DWT 2006 SAMSUNG HI FOR USD 62.5m enbloc). Market players seem to be recognising the inflated price environment, as Marinakis’ Capital ship management penned orders at New Times for 2x 115K DWT LR2 Tankers at USD 60m each. Elsewhere, MR GWN2 (50K DWT 2020 SAMSUNG HI) sold for USD 38.5m to Japanese buyers in an internal sale.   The dry market will be buoyed by the news China are soon to be easing their long standing COVID restrictions, however, such effects from this easing will take time before reflecting in rates and values. More market jostling this week saw 2 transactions in the Kamsarmax sector LOWLANDS COMFORT (81K DWT 2016 TSUNEISHI CEBU) and DL CARNATION (81K DWT 2014 JIANGSU EASTERN HI), sold for USD 26.4m and USD 18.8m respectively.  In the modern Ultramax space, ITALIAN BULKER (63K DWT 2017 SHIN KASADO) was sold for USD 26m.

A slight cooling in the charter market was duly ignored this week as S&P activity ramped up in the tanker market. The first VLCC transaction of a 10 year old unit since Q1 was registered in the form of the C. PASSION blt 2013 HHI which was sold for USD 66m to European buyers. If viewed in regard to the old valuation adage that a 10 year old ship is worth roughly half a newbuild, this transaction will put a smile on the faces owners of modern VLCC tonnage – not that they need any excuse. MR owners should be advised not to get carried away by the sale of ATHLOS blt 2016 Samsung HI Ningbo for USD 41m, which was bought at a significant premium for US Naval purposes. Elsewhere, Pareto purchased LR1 Sisters CAPE TEMPEST/TAMPA blt 2007/08 New Times en bloc for USD 34m.   Uncertainty continues to govern sentiment in the dry space, with market players watching the worsening COVID-19 situation in China with trepidation. A transaction of note was the sale of Newcastlemax sisters CHINA STEEL TEAM/ENTREPRENEUR blt 2006/07 China Shipbld en bloc for USD 35m to Greek buyers. Elsewhere down the size curve, there were a number of handy transactions including SEASTAR HARRIER blt 2022 Hakodate for USD 30.9m and TS Bravo blt 2015 Shanhaiguan for USD 16.75m.

Compared to recent activity, the tanker market had a rather subdued week on the S&P front. However, this is not to be mistaken for a cooling market, quite the opposite. There seems to be no foreseeable end to the tanker bull run with charter markets and asset values remaining red hot, often leaving last done in the rear-view mirror. This is shown in Performance Shipping paying USD 44m for DPP trading LR2 FOS HAMILTON blt 2013 HHI, compared to recent comparable transaction RAFFLES HARMONY blt 2013 HHI which sold for USD 41.80m in October.   Values in the dry space continue to feel downward pressure, following a notable squeeze in earning sentiment. Scrubber fitted Capesize HL SHINBORYEONG blt 2010 SAMHO HI was bought by Stealth Maritime for USD 23.8m, having invited offers across the market and following a number of recent Capesize transactions. In the Supra/Ultra sector, some rates are being reported at below OPEX levels in places indicating it could be a tough winter to come for market players. In an area of the size curve which will be carefully watched as the values correct, Ultramax ACHILLEAS blt 2012 Yangzhou Dayang sold for USD 22.30m to Eastern buyers basis ss/dd freshly passed and BWTS installed.

A ground-breaking week for tanker asset values, with Bahri paying USD 112m each for 2 x 2020 built VLCC’s from Vitol which in our book translates to about USD 120m for a brand-new Korean built vessel with scrubber. This is up about 16% from mid this year.  Vitol also reported to be selling a resale LR2 delivering 2023 which we understand comes with a three-year TC back.  Another flurry of transactions across the dry cargo segments which are illustrating the underlying market correction experienced over the recent weeks. Notably the Japanese controlled Capesize NAVIOS OBELIKS built 2012 Koyo which has been sold to Synergy at USD 29m, this follows the two vessels sold by JP Morgan last week. The Supramax segment continues to feel the downwards pressure with a number of sellers in the market looking to catch an ever sharper falling knife. Tess-58 BULK CARINA 2016 Cebu was reported sold at USD 22m, while lower down the age curve the AZZURA built 2004 IHI sold at USD 13m. There is an ever-increasing number of vessels for sale within the Supramax sector, with owners and opportunists making plans to take advantage of the potential bargains to be had.

Charter market volatility has not deterred dry market S&P players, with a number of transactions being registered this week. JP Morgan invited offers on its Capesize TRUE PATRIOT built 2016 Imabari which was sold for USD 38m, and AQUAFORTUNE built 2011 Namura which sold for USD 26.5m. In the Ultramax space, a segment which will be sure to garner a lot of attention over the looming market correction, CARO PADRE built 2012 Yangzhou Dayang sold for USD 21.0m, levels that are still showing relative degree of resilience despite an increased downward pressure coming from chartering front.  Although older tankers continue to attract most of the attention with CITY OF TOKYO built 2004 Universal selling for USD 49m, a more significant transaction is the brand new, scrubber fitted LR2 ALTHEA built 2022 Daehan which was sold for USD 72.5m, showing that regardless of the rising values, market players see sense in positioning themselves for the long term. Tonnage is available for those looking to enter the market, but buyers will need to take a leap of faith and match the bullish sentiment.

Another busy week in the tanker SnP market with vessels across the age curve transacted. Sentek Marine offloaded NEPTUNE M & PACIFIC M, 2019 HHI for Usd 90m each to HMM. The price reflects a below-market charter attached. Older VLCC tonnage continues to make strong gains as demonstrated by the sale of BRILLIANT JEWEL, 2002 DSME for a whopping Usd 40m to Chinese buyers. Two interesting Suezmax sales as well, both at prices slightly above our reference values.    The dry market is beginning to feel the widely anticipated downward pressure in earnings, with some chartering managers seeing rates as low as Usd 6k/day for Supramax tonnage in the Far East. This has resulted in a somewhat quieter week on the sale and purchase front. There is no sense of urgency to move for sales candidates and buyers are as such increasingly adopting a wait and see attitude. In a notable transaction GREAT GLEN and GREAT AMBITION, 93K DWT 2010/2011 JIANGSU JINLING were sold en bloc for Usd 37m by Sinotrans.

With the tanker market taking the majority of recent headlines, dry market players enacted a flurry of transactions this week. Within the much sought after modern Japanese ultramax tonnage space, scrubber fitted NORD BISCAY (62K DWT 2019 OSHIMA) sold for USD 32.5m. Another sale to note from this sector was Pacific Basin picking up ULTRA WOLLONGONG (61K DWT 2011 OSHIMA) for USD 22m. A total of 15 sales were concluded across the board. This increased activity is dividing opinions with one hand believing a relative bottom has been been reached while the other see it as a signal that a broader sell off is around the corner.  Extensive demand and firm prices in older tonnage such as the EUROGLORY  (166 DWT 2005 BRODOSPLIT) USD 26m reassures market players that the tanker market ascent shows no signs of letting off. Ice class Suezmax vessels are commanding a particular premium seen in the CAP PHILIPPE (158 DWT 2006 SAMSUNG HI) changing hands for USD 32 m. In what is regarded by some as a significant, sentiment assuring transaction, AQUAVIRTUE (156 DWT 2022 SAMSUNG HI) was bought by Thenamaris at USD 76m.

A busy week in the dry market saw a rare sale of a modern asset, in the form of Ultramax BERGE TRONADOR 2020 DACKS built sold for USD 32.8m. Elsewhere, Post-Panamax D SKALKEAS 2011 Newyangzi sold for USD 19.0m to Hong Kong interests. Panamaxes AGRI KINSALE / AGRI QUEEN 2009 Oshima built were sold at auction for USD 16.0m each. Many units remain in the market across the size curve, and players are braced for an interesting Q4 as they jostle for market position.   The tanker market shows no signs of cooling off as VLCC PRINCESS MARY 2004 Mitsubishi built sold for a huge USD 48.0m, granted she is SS freshly passed and BWTS fitted, but this total is well over previous market estimates. In the smaller sizes however, the S&P market is beginning to look crowded with a rumoured 50 plus MRs currently seeking new ownership. This is likely to apply pressure to values across in this sector, which saw 5 transactions this week. The pick of the sales were ENERGY PUMA / ENERGY PROGRESS 2008 Sungdong built, sold to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 20.0m each.

The dry market had a bumper week in transactions, despite the overall uncertain sentiment that has been shared by most market players over the past few weeks. On the Supramax front, sisters GENCO BOURGOGNE & TERESE OETKER 2010 YANGZHOU DAYANG were sold at USD 15.75m and USD 16.1m respectively. Benchmarks which will be most welcome in a market that is seeing an increasing amount of similar tonnage been placed for sale. Capesize SHINYO GUARDIAN 2005 NAMURA was bought by Turkish buyers for USD 17.25m which also marks a new, lower benchmark for this vintage Capesize.  The tanker markets were relatively subdued in terms of completed transactions with product tankers capturing most of the activity this week. The standout deal in this space was UOG picking up the DEE4 FIG 2011 ONOMICHI for USD 26.5m. To put this in perspective, the vessel was purchased by DEE4 in August 2020 for USD 16m. Performance Shipping added another Aframax unit to its fleet with the purchase of PHOENIX BEACON 2011 HHI for USD 35.0m.

As widely anticipated, the dry cargo markets have witnessed a number of corrective sales this week. Navios have sold the Supramax NAVIOS ULYSSES 2007 Oshima at a price of USD 14.5m providing a much needed benchmark for a market that is seeing a number of similar candidates being placed for sale. What remains to be seen is whether this will spur on the number of transactions or encourage scepticism as we head into a potentially challenging Q4. More modern tonnage is proving desirable, with scrubber-fitted Ultramax NORD BARENTS 2019 Oshima selling at USD 33.3m.  The tanker market is alive with excitement and rumour, leaving market players wondering whether this buoyant sentiment can translate into previously unthinkable asset prices. Sales of older ships at firm levels such as VLCC VIKI 2000 Samsung HI at USD 29.5m are causing a conundrum as assets further up the age curve fail to entice buyers into chasing owner’s price ideas. Ridgebury Tankers though, have cashed in with 3 sales concluding this week MRs RIDGEBURY BIRCH & ACACIA 2006 Shin Kurushima at USD 17.5m each, and RIDGEBURY VOYAGER 2008 HMD at USD 19.5m.

A relatively quiet week in the dry market as sentiment remains largely unchanged, even with the sale of Capesize FRONTIER TRIUMPH 2012 Imabari at USD 30.0m to Chinese interests. Players in smaller segments are patiently waiting for a corrective sale, which would help price the increasing number of candidates being placed in the market. That said, owners are still enjoying a bump in earnings, so are in no rush to sell themselves short. The sale of Kamsarmax NORD CORONA 2019 Hantong for USD 29.0m will not go unnoticed, setting a renewed benchmark in the sector.  Tanker owners are still very much enjoying the upward momentum, particularly by those who perhaps took a position a few years ago at what is now considered a very attractive entry point on the price curve. More modern tonnage is attracting attention too with some owners entertaining the idea of a potential sale at substantially higher targets. A revision that is not yet met by buyers who are yet to feel comfortable with these fast-moving levels.

The dry market remains delicately poised as players align themselves with lowering asset values, despite a brief jolt in earnings. Capesize FRONTIER TRIUMPH 2012 Imabari is rumoured to have had over 10 suitors, showing that the appetite is very much present on the buying side despite variable market conditions. A notable sale this week is HANTON TRADER I (2014/Jiangsu/63k dwt) to Jinhui for USD 25.4m. With many ships being considered in the market, we predict a flurry of transactions once market players are at ease with the ongoing value correction. There is clearly plenty of potential equity following the dry space these days in anticipation of lower asset values in the short to medium term.  Appetite in the wet market shows no signs of letting off as asset values continue to rise in line with a buoyant earnings environment.  The VLCC TSURUSAKI blt 2002 being sold to Greek interests at USD 33m is an example, demonstrating that there is still money to be made from old rope. However, with strengthening freight rates, the bid/ask spread is widening across the board. Modern tanker sales remain few and far between.

Dry asset values are gradually aligning to the lower earnings across the board with sellers willing to take a 10-15% reduction in price compared to recent highs. Notable sale this week is the scrubber-fitted 2015 Japan built Ultramax ULTRA TRUST at Usd 27.8m to Eagle Bulk. This compares with the sale end July of the non-scrubber fitted GOLDEN CECILIE and GOLDEN CATHRINE also 2015 built Japan at USD 31.5m each. In the near future, non-eco Chinese built vessels will take the biggest hit in values. The next benchmark deal for Capesize will be FRONTIER TRIUMPH (2012/Imabari/181k dwt), which is inviting inspections in Singapore on 12th September. Last comparable sale was the two year older MINERAL HAIKU (2010/Koyo/180k dwt) reported sold for Usd 34m in May.   Tankers with ice class 1A remain in hot demand as seen by the sale of Aframaxes ALBA and ARISTODIMOS built 2005 and 2006 respectively at a firm Usd 65m en-bloc. Both vessels are scrubber-fiited.

Product tanker values are continuing their gradual climb with each reported sale exceeding their relative last done. Celsius Shipping has disposed of its older BWTS fitted LR2 tankers -  “CELSIUS ESBERG” & “CELSIUS EVERETT”  built 2009 and 2008 at New Times – respectively achieving Usd 33m and Usd 31m. The sale is marking yet another substantial jump considering that the last comparable sale of a Chinese built unit was that of the 2006 Dalian built “JAG LYALL” which was sold at Usd 26.2m end of July this year. This momentum is partly shared by crude segments, where the overall trend in values remains positive with DHT Tankers selling their 2008 built VLCC “DHT EDELWEISS” at Usd 37m, despite some fragility seen in earnings. The vessel was sold basis survey due with BWTS to be fitted at next docking. Despite having no sales to report on the MR front this week, activity remains high with signs of a number of negotiations suggesting further sales in the near future.   Following a relative show of resistance from Dry cargo sellers we are definitely witnessing a number of owners caving to the ever lower bids shown by buyers who are looking to capitalise on the most recent correction. With every new deal reaffirming this downward trend, we expect an increased amount of sellers opting to pull the trigger sooner rather than later in hope to achieve what is still broadly considered as a high price point on the curve. A sentiment well illustrated by the sale of the 2010 Hyundai Vinashin built “CLARKE QUAY” which achieved Usd 17m.

Tanker markets continue to occupy centre-stage with a flurry of sales to report this week. The Aframax segment is continuing its upward rally supported by strong levels of buying enquiry. Performance Shipping has confirmed its purchase of the “ALPINE AMALIA” (Abt 105k dwt built 2010 HHI). The scrubber fitted LR2 achieved a price of Usd 36.5m falling in line with the most recent appreciation in values in the sector. Similarly the sistership  “ARGO” (Abt 105k dwt built 2009 HHI) was sold at Usd 33.75m. Ridgebury Tankers has taken its tally of vessel disposals this summer to eight with “RIDGEBURY CAPTAIN DROGIN”  (Abt 166k dwt built 2007 HHI) sold at Usd 29m to Greek interests.    Similar dynamics also witnessed in the CPP segments with MR leading the charge. Notable transaction this week being the sale of the sisterships “ALAKIOS” & “ARCHON” (Abt 50k dwt built 2016 Sasmung Ningbo). They achieved a price of Usd 36.5m each reinforcing the positive trend witnessed in the segment. A trend that becomes particularly apparent when compared to the sale of 2016 SPP built LARGO SUN which only last month was sold at Usd 35m.  Also strong prices indeed for the older ones with EGD Shipholding achieving a firm Usd 16.8m for its eighteen year old "AGNES VICTORY" which recently completed DD including installation of BWTS.

Tankers in all asset classes remain in hot pursuit and sellers are clearly gaining the upper hand. SFL Corp swooped for four modern Suezmax tankers from Ciner. The vessels were on TC to Kock with one year left which have been cancelled in exchange for new 6 years TC contracts to Koch, adding approximately Usd 250 million to SFL’s fixed-rate backlog. The 2019 DSME built VLCC “C.GUARDIAN” invited offers this week with 7 buyers understood to having shown their cards and the vessel is now reported sold for Usd 98 mill. Last comparable sale was Hunter’s 2020 DSME built VLCC’s at Usd 96 mill. This week’s sale represents as such about 6% increase and the implied value for resale/2022 VLCC is now Usd 110 mill. Aframax/LR2 built 2009-2011 is a sweet-spot for many buyers with several deals expected to materialize soon. The same goes for MR where UOG this week added another two 2011 built units to its fleet. Suezmax tankers with ice class 1A are few and far between which, together with the vessels having open loop scrubbers, goes a long way in explaining the firm price Ridgebury achieved for its 2006 and 2007 built vessels.  Dry asset values are under pressure. SNP volumes are low with buyers increasingly applying a wait-and-see attitude. Sellers will have to readjust price expectations or take cover for a while. Latter being the case for two 2015 JMU built Kamsarmaxes which have been withdrawn from the market as best on offer was region Usd 31.5 mill. In May, two 2015 sister vessels were sold for Usd 35.5 mill.

All eyes on a tanker market that seems to be going from strength to strength as demonstrated by this week’s reported transactions. The product markets as expected have drawn most of the interest, leading to substantial drive in values with new benchmarks being set across several vintages. The Japanese controlled “CHALLENGE PHOENIX” invited offers on Tuesday after having up to a dozen buyers registering interest; the vessel is now sold at a price in the region of USD 18m to Greek buyers. A jump in pricing which becomes particularly apparent when compared to last months sale of the “ENERGY PANTHER” (47k dwt 2008 Sungdong) which achieved Usd 16.1m.  Similar dynamics on the more modern front with JP Morgan achieving Usd 35m for their 2016 SPP built unit “LARGO SUN”.  A comparatively subdued Dry SnP market with the most recent market slow down gradually taking hold on the SnP front. We are indeed witnessing a weakening bid with buyers now looking to secure tonnage at levels below last done. We therefore expect a relative correction in values despite the resilience shown by potential sellers who would rather wait over these summer months rather than pulling the trigger at these lower levels.

The positive momentum experienced over the past couple of weeks in the tanker snp markets continue to drive activity in most sectors with a number of sales to report this week. As expected, the product markets are leading the charge with values reflecting the healthy earning which has gradually been taking hold over the past couple of months.  A trend in pricing particularly apparent on the MR front which has seen a higher volume of transactions setting improved benchmarks across most vintages. Elsewhere we continue to see a drive on Aframax values with a strong buying enquiry competing over a limited supply of sale candidates. Saying that we expect a number of potential sellers to come meet this renewed interest in hope to capture the value offered by the most recent appreciation in values. A jump well illustrated by the sale of the “ELANDRA ANGEL” (115k dwt 2009 Samsung) which was sold by Vitol at Usd 32m. Important to note that the vessel is scrubber fitted which would condone a notable premium against a comparable non scrubber fitted vessel.  With most headlines stolen by Tanker activity dry SnP markets remain relatively uneventful with values still showing resilience against a certain degree of uncertainty that seems to be settling in. A flat pricing curve that is as usual well supported in the Supramax market with units such as the “NEUTRINO” (58k dwt 2012 Kawasaki) still achieving levels in line with their relative last done.

Steady activity in the Dry Cargo sectors with healthy amount of transactions despite a relative weakening in sentiment. The Kamsarmax sector has seen a handful of vessels changing hands with values continuing to show resilience against an increasingly challenging environment. As mentioned in last week's wrap up, pressure on values seems to be most felt on the Supramax front. A correction partly due to the heighten liquidity usually seen in the sector which makes this specific asset class more reactive to price volatility. Notable pick up in buying enquiry on the Capesize front where we expect further activity in the near future.  Despite the limited amount of sales to report on the Tanker front, this week continue to see positive momentum driven by increased levels of buying enquiry. We are indeed witnessing a strong buying appetite with signs of a number of ongoing negotiations; an appetite however that is met with a fast-moving target by sellers who have been long awaiting for market rebound and who are now revising their ideas upwards in light of what seems to be an unanimous consensus of even better days to come.

As anticipated, this week has seen a number of vessels changing hands on the tanker front with new benchmarks being set across most sectors. Transactions that are indeed validating the positive trend witnessed over the past couple of weeks with values gradually catching up with this shared positive sentiment. An appreciation particularly felt on the product front with 8 units being sold this week. The 2005 built MT “EXPLORER II” (47k dwt built Onomichi) achieved Usd 13.3m basis surveys and BWTS due. To put levels in perspective the MT “ANGEL NO. 6" (45k dwt, 2005, Shin Kurushima) was sold earlier this month at Usd 9.4m representing an approximate 40% jump in values between these two comparable sales. Other notable increase on the Aframax front with the sisters “TARTAN” & “FORTIES” (113k dwt, 2005, Samsung – Ice 1A) being sold at Usd 22.5m each. Similarly the last comparable sale is this of the “SOPHIE SCHULTE” (115k dwt, 2005, Sanoyas) which was sold at Usd 19.5m beginning of June this year. Worth noting that the Tartan and sister are both holding an Ice class notification 1A which is understood to have had a positive impact on the levels achieved.  Dry SnP markets have seemingly rebounded from last weeks relative dip in activity with about 15 vessels being sold this week. While most values remain relatively flat, there are signs of weakening on certain fronts which have seen a relative loss of momentum. The SDARI 64 ultramax  “WESTERN SANTOS” (64k dwt, 2014, Hantong) was sold at Usd 26.3m which could be construed as a slight correction against last month’s sale of the one-year younger sister “BELPAREIL” (64k dwt, 2015, Hantong) which achieved Usd 29.5m. Saying that, levels continue to be well supported by high levels of liquidity in most sectors which is expected to continue to keep values in line with most recent concluded business.

A relatively quieter week for Dry cargo SnP markets that have got us used to exceptional volumes of weekly transactions throughout the year. The four vessels changing hands this week are all Supramax, which continues to draw most of the buying enquiry; saying that there has been a relative shift in sentiment with the number of potential buyers thinning down and adopting a standby approach to a market that appears to show signs of weakening. Nevertheless values remain flat for the time being with the 2009 built Tess 58 MV “SAGARJEET” achieving USD 18.4m.   Slightly opposite momentum on the tanker front despite the limited amount of reported sales this week.
