We are witnessing a strong Buying appetite with signs of a number of ongoing negotiations; an appetite however that is met with a fast-moving target by Sellers who have been long awaiting for a market rebound and who are now revising their ideas upwards in light of what seems to be an unanimous consensus of even better days to come.

Dry cargo markets continue to capture most of the SnP activity with vessels changing hands across all segments. The sisterships “DARYA JYOTI & DARYA MOTI (2010/STX/80k dwt)”, have been sold to Greek buyers at USD 24m each representing a tick up in values for 1st generation Kamsarmax units of Korean design. Notable pick up in activity in the Panamax front with four mid 2000 built units changing hands; prices achieved continue to fall in line with most recent transactions. Buying enquiry remains particularly strong in the Ultramax segment where a number of vessels are being placed on the market for sale suggesting further activity in the near future.   It has been a subdued week in terms of concluded business for Tanker markets which is however not particularly reflective of the buying appetite witnessed in most segments. A momentum in values seems to be getting hold with signs of ongoing negotiations suggesting a tick up in levels put on the table by potential buyers. Increased levels that should soon be supported by a higher volume of vessels changing hands providing consolidated benchmarks for future transactions.

Crude asset values are stabilizing at newfound higher levels, except for modern Aframax where the sale of RUMFORD (107k 2012 Tsuneishi) at Usd 32.8 mill represents another uptick. The vessel has SS passed and BWTS fitted. Certainly more buyers than sellers around with the sweet spot being Aframax/LR2 and MR built 2007-2012. A steady trickle of VLCC transactions and MOL's sale of DUQM (310k 2008 Imabari) at Usd 39 mill is broadly in line with recent transactions.  Dry asset values are moving sideways except for Supramax where values continue to gain. Handysize are still a favorite with buyers whereas Capesize deals are few and far between.

A flurry of activity in the dry cargo markets with up to 20 vessels changing hands this week. From handysize to capesize the dry SnP space is joying of sustained liquidity providing great transparency on values which in turn facilitate further transactions. A dynamic that becomes particularly well illustrated by the ultramax/supramax sector which sees a consistent amount of units changing hands over the weeks, keeping levels in line with relative last done. This week the “FORTUNE BELL” (Abt 61k dwt built 2020 Shin Kurushima) has been sold at Usd 39m in line with last months sale of the “ULTRA INITIATOR” (abt 62k built 2019 Oshima) at Usd 37.5m while the “OSIOS DAVID” (Abt 55k dwt built 2012 IHI) achieved a price of Usd 22.5m paving the way for the several sisterships that are currently in the market solicitating interest. A pickup in activity in the handysize segment this with 7 vessels being sold this week.    On the tanker front Sinokor continues this year’s shopping spree with the acquisition of the two VLCCs  “NUCLEUS” & “NEPTUN” (Abt 300k dwt built 2007 Dalian) at a price of Usd 30.8m each. Notable activity continuing to take place in the Aframax sector with a number of region 10 year old units being under discussions – as previously reported the long standing bid/ask spread seems to be slowly closing up spurring potential buyers into action. A dynamic that we expect to hold in the near future translating into heightened liquidity and an appreciation in asset values. Similar activity witnessed in the product markets where the strong rate environment continues to drive interest upwards.

Sentiment in the tanker sectors continue to show encouraging signs with a strengthening buying enquiry leading to increased SnP liquidity in most segments. Product sectors draw strong levels of interest however this week has seen a greater number of crude carriers changing hands with 5 units sold. Notable transactions in the VLCC sector where MT “LEONIDAS” (Abt 320k dwt built 2009 HHI) was sold at Usd 42m while the Chinese built “NEW TALISMAN” (Abt 300k dwt built 2009 Bohai) achieved Usd 38.2m from UAE based Buyers. Levels that remain surprisingly in line with most recently concluded business but which however are not necessarily reflective of the current buying appetite which should apply upward pressure on values going forward. Elsewhere the 2007 built Aframax “ALMI SPIRIT “ was sold at USd 20m basis surveys due providing clear direction for the several other similar candidates that are currently in the market for sale. Candidates that were struggling to transact due to a rather stubborn bid/offer spread that seems to finally tighten.  Steady activity in the dry cargo sectors with healthy amount of transactions and ongoing negotiation in most segments; notable pick up for Capesize which are seeing  an increasing number of  buyers entering the market. Elsewhere the Chinese built Ultramax “YANGZHOU CONFIDENCE” (Abt 63k dwt built 2017 Dayang) has now been sold basis SS Passed and BWTS fitted. Indicative of the current appetite, it is understood that the vessel drew up to 10 potential buyers with SUMEC inviting offers on the 17th of May which saw the vessel being sold at price of Usd 31.3m

Dry cargo markets continue to see a flurry of transactions with north of twenty vessels changing hands across all segments. With strong level of enquiries being met by steady stream of sale candidates, values remain relatively flat and pricings fall in line with last done. Notable activity in the Capesize sector where Synergy has bought the 2010 Koyo built MINERAL HAIKU at Usd 34m providing further benchmarks for Japanese designed vessels of similar vintage. Panamax and Kamsarmax segments have also joyed of a pick up of activity with 6 units being sold this week, mostly driven by Chinese built vessels with pricing at relative highs for sellers but at levels that remain attractive for buyers weighing Chinese designs against their Japanese counterparts.  Tanker sale and purchase markets seem to have lost steam again off the back of a relative softening on the chartering front. A freight volatility that continues to feed into a widening bid offer spread on the snp front with most potential sellers holding off for levels reflecting a largely expected recovery. As a result only four sales to report this week with most buying enquiries falling in the Aframax space where a number of discussions taking place which may translate into further sales in the near future.

Deal of the week being Delta Tankers’ purchase of Suezmax STENA SUPREME built 2012 Samsung at Usd 37.5 mill basis prompt delivery FE with SS and BWTS due by the end of June. Last comparable sale was in March when DENSA ORCA also built 2012 Samsung was sold for Usd 32.5 mill with her SS imminently due as well. Even allowing for the fact that the Stena vessel has electronic main engine, this represents a hike of 12-14% in a short time. Aframax, Suezmax and MR are all hot commodity and VLCC values will also be following suit. Last done prices are becoming less relevant with sellers gaining the upper hand.  Euronav has confirmed the acquisition of two VLCC's from Hartree, both scrubber fitted DSME units - GHILLIE built in 2019 and CHELSEA in 2020 and the en-bloc price is Usd 179 mill; a tick down compared to what has been speculated in advance. Euronav also confirmed the sale of four non eco VLCCs built 2011 and 2012 for an en-bloc price of Usd 198 mill. The confirmed price is in line with what we reported as being done to Sinokor in March.  Transactions in the 33k dwt stainless steel segment are rare indeed but Stolt Tankers is now reported have acquired three such vessels from K-Line built 2012 and 2013 at an en-bloc price of Usd 76 mill. The last deal in this segment was in early 2021 when EGD Shipholding bought two vessels built 2009.   Bulkers continue to change hands across all segments. Values are moving sideways with continued focus on the smaller sizes. However two Capesize sales to report this week. The limited supply of modern Capesize for sale and sellers unwilling to reduce asking levels, bode for new higher benchmark deals in the near future. To date, the last modern Capesize deal was in April for RED SAGE 2015 JMU built at Usd 47.5.

Values for tankers are moving north. Our take is that values are up by 5-10%. Unconfirmed reports that Euronav has purchased from Hartree 2 x 2019/2020 scrubber-fitted DSME built VLCCs at USD 182-184 mill en-bloc, possibly with an element of shares as payment but the trend is clear. Suezmax STENA SUPREME 2012 SHI invited offers yesterday. The vessel is expected to be sold next week and price to be north of USD 35 mill. Delivery will be basis SS due in June. Last comparable sale is DENSA ORCA also 2012 Korean built which was sold for USD 32.5mio with her SS/DD promptly due early March. Purchase interest for MRs and Aframax is picking up and ice classed older tonnage is seeing a premium.    Dry market is moving sideways with focus on Panamax and Supra/Ultramax, however Capesize is again back in fashion. Our expectations are for healthy rates until end of Q2, with a more gloomy 2H of this year. Notable sales are the 2 x 2016 Japanese built Ultramaxes “NAVIGARE BACCA” and “TOMINI INTEGRITY” at USD 32.5 m and USD 33 m respectively. Worth noting that TOMINI reportedly purchased the “TOMINI INTEGRITY” at USD 19 m July 2020. We expect the values of modern tonnage to retain steady, with a potential upside in the near future with lack of quality tonnage available for sale.

A week dominated by a tanker market that seem to have finally caught up with the long drawn expectations of a market upturn. We have witnessed rates going from strength to strength in all major sectors establishing a positive sentiment across the board. A sentiment supported by news of further consolidation with the announcement of the merger between Frontline and Euronav creating the largest tanker owning company in the market comprising of 69 VLCCs and 57 Suezmax. A move that seems to have been mostly welcome by most as a sign of great commitment by some of the market leaders. This week also comes to a close with a number of units changing hands, notable activity in the Aframax market that has seen GNTMC acquire the two sisterships from Atlas Maritime built at Daehan with delivery in 2022 at a price of Usd 61m each. A price reflective of current NB environment considering that these contracts were placed in the mid 40s in 2020. We expect further activity in the sector as exhibited by a growing buying enquiry with strengthening bids trying to go meet an offer that is now firmly into a sellers market.

With a market still trying to find its bearings in light of an ever-changing geopolitical situation and a week that is cut short by several national holidays, we close this Friday with a relatively subdued snp sentiment. Despite already closing one month into the conflict, the situation as expected remains highly volatile with sanctions and their impact on global trade representing a constant moving target for market players trying to identify alternative trading patterns. An uncertainty that is as usual felt the most in the SnP markets where potential buyers and sellers prefer to apply a wait and see approach before committing to any long-term decisions. This becomes particularly apparent in the tanker space where the gradual rate recovery should in essence provide enough support for buyers to start meeting the offers at hand but where we are still experiencing some reserve as to whether this gradual "recovery" has legs.  Dry markets continue to see very high levels of enquiry and as such liquidity remains relatively high in most sectors with Supramax and Ultramax leading the charge with a handful of vessels changing hands and signs of a number of ongoing negotiations. Levels are therefore well supported across the board with some segments seeing an appreciation in values, a trend that should be set for the foreseeable future.

Dry cargo markets continue to see a flurry of SnP activity with up to 15 vessels changing hands this week. Notable developments on the Kamsarmax front where new benchmarks are being set.  The 2007 built “OCEANIC” (Abt 82k Tsuneishi Fukuyama) was sold at Usd 21m while the 2010 built “MBA LIBERTY” (Abt 82k dwt built Tsuneishi Zhoushan) achieved Usd 22m.  A comparison highlighting the relative discount carried by the Tess 82 built at the Zhoushan facility against a straight Japanese built unit. A discount however that remains minor compared to straight Chinese designs with the  2 year younger “YANGTZE XING HUA” (Abt 82k  built Guangzhou Longxue 2012) also achieving Usd 22m. Elsewhere the Supramax market continues to joy high liquidity with strong levels of enquiry being met with a steady stream of sale candidates.   Following the most recent pick up in activity it has been a quieter week in the tanker sector with most of the activity captured by the product sector. With strengthening chartering markets we expect a number of Buyers to come out the wood work in an effort to secure additional tonnage. It will be no easy feat though, with sellers expecting this gradual rate recovery to translate into higher asset values in the near future.

Liquidity in the dry SnP markets is back at levels witnessed through most of last year with twenty-five units changing hands this week. The underlying macro environment is providing a relative degree of support on the freight side as mentioned last week. Rates that are driving buyers to increase their bids in order to secure additional tonnage. Most of that activity is captured by the Kamsarmax/Panamax and the Utramax/Supramax markets with seven and eight vessels being sold in those respective segments. Worth noting that sellers of Chinese built candidates are the ones more willing to transact with prices deemed to have reach relative heights while potential sellers of Japanese designed vessels are counting on the sharper drive in values usually experienced for quality designs in such rising markets.  Pick up in activity in the tanker space as well, with most market players expecting values to take turn off the back of the recent relative increase in rates. Although earnings remain limited in most sectors due to increased bunker costs, buyers are still willing to go meet the offer, expecting the current situation to have further positive impact on rates which will translate in higher second-hand values. The VLCC sector continues to see a number of units changing hands with a number of ongoing negotiations suggesting even further activity in the near future.

As we end another week of escalating conflicts in Eastern Europe and as sanctions on Russian interests unravel, we continue to feel its effect on all shipping markets. Confusion around which specific entities are being sanctioned has paved the way for a number of tanker owners to proceed with Baltic and BSea voyages offering substantial risk premiums for Russian liftings. The majority of players however are opting for a "self-sanctioning" approach with refiners and traders shying away from Russian product. Should the situation remain or worsen we expect these soaring regional rates to continue their climb and provide wider support for freight across all geographies. The sale and purchase markets have seen a pick-up in activity in the VLCC sector with 5 units changing hands this week, breaking an extensive stretch of inactivity in the segment. A strengthening buying interest that is driving buyers to re-evaluate their bids to go meet a thinning list of available candidates in hope to capture the gains that are currently witnessed in the chartering markets.  In a relative contrast to the volatility experienced by Tanker players, the Dry sectors are continuing to joy of steadily strengthening markets. A strength that can be felt through the most recent SnP transactions that have seen vessels achieve levels in excess of last dones. A dynamic that is particularly well illustrated by the sale of the 2012 Mitsui built MV "ORCHID" which achieved Usd 22.6m.

Following weeks of escalation - the growing fears shared by most over the past few weeks have unfortunately become a reality with Russia’s military operations currently underway in Ukraine. A volatile geopolitical environment with undeniable ramifications across all markets which have met Russia’s aggression with large scale economic sanctions. Measures that have yet to be fully announced and which implications remain to be seen; an uncertainty that has left the tanker markets with an already tighter list of available tonnage. Adding to an already skewed fleet positioning east of Suez leading to rate gains in the Atlantic. Baltic Aframax rates have also surged with most owners deciding to hold back unless they see a considerable premium from charterers. We expect these firming chartering markets to soon translate into a pick in SnP activity with potential buyers finding enough support from these improved rates to pull the trigger on future acquisitions.  Dry cargo players are of course also endeavouring to digest the effect that these recent events will have on their market; direct impact is as expected felt in the Black Sea where Ukraine has officially halted its operations in several of its ports including from Yuznhy where force majeure has been declared. A disruption in exports for several key commodities coming out of the Black Sea that will have to be substituted should the situation persists. The tonnage list in the region is of course following suit with owners shying away from Black Sea fixtures. Similarly, we expect this tension on rates to provided support to an already steady value environment which could be mean further gains for Dry cargo assets across all segments.

This week continues to see a climb in dry cargo snp activity with up to 20 vessels changing hands. As mentioned in our last report, potential buyers have re-entered the market supported by clear benchmarks being set by recent transactions taking place in all sectors. Levels that broadly remain in line with the relative highs achieved over the past quarter making it easier for sellers to trigger a sale. The Ultramax and Supramax sectors are once again capturing most of the activity with a steady stream of candidates being placed on the market to meet those increased levels of buying enquiry.  A rather more subdued sentiment in the Tanker space where values are continuing their corrections, lead by sellers who are gradually deciding to give in a market that is showing no signs of bouncing back. The mid 2000 crude carriers seem to be the first to take the hit with a number of units being sold. The Product sector is showing more resiliance with sellers keeping units out of the market or continuing to hold for levels in line with last done.

This week comes to a close with both sectors joying of an increased amount of sales; a liquidity however that reflects two very different underlying market sentiment. The long awaited tanker recovery seems to have become a long distant memory with a number of potential sellers now taking the decision to pull the trigger and dispose of assets that they have for so long resisted to sell at substantially corrected levels. A dynamic particularly well illustrated in the mid 2000 built Aframax front which has seen a great number of potential candidates being marketed over the past months, but by sellers hoping to capture the anticipation of a market rebound. Same sellers who have now decided to go meet the bid setting new benchmarks for other owners looking to catch the falling knife.   Dry cargo snp markets seem to also have set its direction seeing buying interest strengthening amongst all sectors with buyers willing to now pay levels in line with last done, in order to secure the right candidates. Values therefore remain particularly well supported both by a strong level of buying interest but also by a pool of sellers confident in the longevity of this market.

Increased sale and purchase activity on the dry cargo front where the supramax segment has been capturing most of the buying enquiry with 6 units changing hands this week. A pick up in liquidity pointing to a relative correction in values with new targets being set. A dynamic led by Chinese and Korean designed vessels which in typical fashion are the first to dip with sellers more willing to catch a falling knife by showing less resistance against a bid at less than last done. Elsewhere the Japanese controlled Kamsarmax “ENERGY TRITON” (82k built Tsuneishi 2012) achieved Usd 25m which similarly sets a well needed benchmark in a market that has started the year with a degree of hesitancy as to where the asset values are heading. Signs of ongoing negotiations and inspections suggest further sales in the near future.   The tanker market remains extremely subdued in terms of S&P with an underlying chartering market that offers no signs of respite. Noteworthy activity this week is the sale of the VLCC “ATHENIAN SUCCESS” which was sold to Sinokor at USd 42.5m. Levels that remain unsurprisingly flat with same owners having sold the exact sister “ ATHENIAN HARMONY” in December last year at Usd 42m.

Activity on the tanker front continues to be captured by the product sectors with several vessels changing hands. Further to last week's reported sale of Scorpio LR1 fleet, it has transcribed that owners have also disposed of two additional MR units - namely the 2013 HMD built “STI FONTVIEILLE“ and 2019 Vinashin built “STI MAJESTIC”, which were sold at USD 23.5m and USD 34.9m respectively. Amounting to a total of 14 vessels being sold for a total consideration of USD 472.2m. The Japanese controlled 2010 Shin Kurushima built Pumproom type unit “PRIME EXPRESS” has invited offers on Monday this week; after receiving up to 6 bids the vessel has now been committed at USD 16.2m to Greek buyers. Worth noting that the sale was basis BWTS due in August this year. Elsewhere, the 2007 Onomichi built LR1 “POLAR COD” was sold at USD 11.7m providing a well needed benchmark for LR1 units of such vintage.  Dry snp markets remain subdued in terms of concluded transactions with a widening bid offer spread between potential sellers who are holding back for last dones levels achieved end of last year and potential buyers hoping to secure tonnage from a thinning list of available candidates at a relative discount.

Despite it be a quiet week in the snp market with a shrinking number of sales to report, headlines were stolen by the reported ongoing discussions between Scorpio and Hafnia for the acquisition of Scorpios LR1 fleet. The deal would comprise of 12 LR1 product carriers built in 2016 and 2015 with all units being scrubber fitted. It would mark a continuous consolidation in the Product space which has been led by Hafnia over the years through a number of large scale transactions. A move that seem to be welcomed by most market players who see it as a stamp of confidence in a market that has been falling short of expectations.  In terms of concluded transactions this week, the dry markets have seen a handful of vessels changing hands notably in the Supramax segment which continues to capture the bulk of activity. Momentum seem to be subdued compared to last quarter’s frenzy, mainly due to market players finding their bearings in this new year and identifying the next investible sector.

While SnP markets are gradually finding their rhythm post the holiday season, this new year opens with no particular surprises with unchanged sentiment across both sectors. Dry cargo continues to draw healthy amounts of buying interest on the second hand front with freight continuing to provide support for potential buyers looking to take further positions in order to joy of these sustained returns. Supramax sector captures the bulk of activity with a handful of vessels changing hands at values which for now remain broadly in line with the end of year transactions. Saying that there have been signs of ongoing negotiations where bids have come at a discount to last done with potential buyers hoping to take advantage of the slight corrections in the chartering markets and this quieter seasonal period. Sellers however remain committed to their targets leading to a flat pricing curve.   With Tankers closing the year with a widely shared sense of disillusion about a market recovery that seems to become increasingly evasive; most market players have started the year with caution. This subdued sentiment can be felt in part in the thinning level of enquiry with buyers taking a wait and see approach rather than going to meet an ever-stagnating offer. This being particularly apparent on the modern front as opposed to older tonnage where pockets of activity can be seen with a number of region 10 year old product carriers changing hands.

The year comes to an end with a rather unexpected burst of activity in the Tanker space, with a number of sellers deciding to go meet the current bid instead of waiting for a market recovery that seems to become more evasive by the day.  Athenian has now sold the sisterships “ATHENIAN HARMONY" & "ATHENIAN SUCCESS” (300k dwt HHI 2010) to Greek buyers, Altomare, at a price of Usd 42m each. This follows an extensive period of inactivity for Korean built VLs of such vintage. Last comparable sale actually being the “ATHENIAN VICTORY” (300k dwt HHI 2009) which was sold by same owners in June at Usd 42.5m. The Aframax/LR2 sector has also seen increased liquidity for units around 10 years and younger with Socar committing their “SILVER” & “GOLD” (107k dwt Tsuneishi 2010) to Seaworld of Greece at a price of Usd 49.5m enboc while the coated Daehan 2018 built unit “PROSKY” was sold to Neda Maritime at Usd 52m basis the remainder of its TC to Shell attached.   Notable activity in the Dry front as well with Norden disposing of three modern Ultramax units. As mentioned throughout our past reports, values for more modern tonnage have showed increased resilience compared to vessels of older vintage. This being mainly explained by the high replacement cost in the sector with high Newbuilding pricing supporting values for modern second-hand units.

A relative busy week in the Dry snp markets in this end of year with about 15 vessels changing hands and a number of buyers re-entering the market in light of the most recent correction in values. Having taken a step back following a string of acquisitions, Costamare are back in the market having purchased the “EGYPTIAN MIKE” & “GEORGE P” (82k dwt built Guangzhou Longxue 2011 & 2012). The sister vessels were sold at an enbloc price of Usd 39m illustrating the abovementioned correction particularly well, especially when compared to last month’s sale of the “SM AURORA” (82k built Jiangsu Eastern 2012) which achieved Usd 21m. The same dynamic is witnessed across most dry segments with Supramax values also settling at levels which are about 15% lower than the recent peak. Notable transactions are those of Chinese design vessels which had greatly benefited of the recent rally with values soaring but which are similarly the most vulnerable to downward pressure.  A sense of delusion seems to have creeped in the Tanker markets off the back of the most recent spike in Covid cases pointing to yet another wave of restrictions across most western economies. As such most players seem be losing faith in the highly coveted market recovery resulting in very subdued activity. Therefore only four sales to report this week which once again took place in the product sector.

We continue to see the Dry snp markets gradually adjust to the corrected rates we have seen settle throughout these past weeks. A correction in values that becomes particularly apparent for tonnage that is 5 years and older where levels achieved are 10 to 15% lower than most recent transactions. Modern units are showing more resistance being supported by high newbuilding prices which allow sellers to maintain their targets which remain, in comparison to NB, a more enticing offer. A dynamic that is particularly well illustrated by the resale of a Japanese controlled  Capesize which was sold to Diana Shipping at Usd 60m. The vessel is being built at Namura Shipyard and is scheduled for delivery in April 2022. Similarly in the Ultramax front where a resale delivering in 2023 from Tsuneishi Zhoushan achieved USD 34.5m. With forward curves showing signs of levelling off we expect values to move sideways in this end of year with lower volumes of transactions.  Uneventful close of the week on the Tanker front with very little change from our last report. Most of the activity continues to be captured by the Product sector with a number of mid 2000 built MRs changing hands. Values remain flat in a market where this renewed buying interest is met with a steady flow of sales candidates. Worth noting that offers were invited on two 10 year old Aframax units; understand that up to 10 outright bids were collected which is tribute to the positive underlying sentiment witnessed in the Tanker space.

The positive sentiment witnessed in the tanker markets over the past couple of weeks is starting to translate into transactions with a number of buyers picking up tonnage. This dynamic is led by the product sector which has seen eight vessels changing hands across an array of vintages. This pick up in activity doesn’t however mean that buyers go meet higher price expectations but rather sellers taking advantage of an increased buying pool to dispose of vessels that have failed to attract any interest throughout these subdued markets. This is particularly apparent for vessels that are 10 years and older which are seeing a notable pick up in buying enquiry. We therefore expect values to continue to move sideways with a number of similar vessels being placed for sale.  Dry cargo continues to see a slowdown in activity with bids coming at levels below last done In hope to capture the value offered by the recent correction. Corrected values that also put pressure on transaction already in places with signs of a number of deals failing to materialize.

As expected, we are indeed experiencing a relative slowdown in terms of volumes of sale on the Dry cargo fronts. However, with the weekly liquidity that we have been accustomed to over the past months, this slight loss of momentum is far from a complete halt in SnP activity with north of a dozen vessels changing hands this week. Values as a whole are shifting sideways for the time being despite the adjusted bids seen from buyers looking to take advantage of the dip in rates, to secure tonnage at less than last done. Signs of which can be seen in the more liquid of segments such as Supramax units that are seeing levels which are on average 10% lower than the most recent completed sales.  Tanker markets continue to show growing signs of anticipation for a healthier rates environment. Buying enquiry is steadily rising along the recovering sentiment with product sector leading the charge showing a great number of enquiries for MRs and LR2. Well needed benchmark being set in the crude sector which has seen the Aframax “Antonis” (113k dwt, 2017 built Daehan) sold at Usd 45m. A sale that draws direction in a market that has strong levels of buying interest for units of such vintage, but which has seen no sales to provide some additional support for potential buyers to come forward with their bids.

Still a bumpy road in the tanker space and somewhat lack of clear direction. We see signs and growing interest, but the market is still in need for more steady guidance. Hafnia (BW) has again proved their strong belief in consolidation and enjoyed the headlines this week with their massive acquisition of the Oaktree controlled Chemical Tankers Inc (CTI) fleet. The transaction adds 32 modern, Eco, IMO II vessels and consist of 6 MRs, 18 Handies and 8 x 25k stainless steel tankers – all Korean/Japanese built. The equity portion was funded through issuance of new shares on a NAV-for-NAV basis and leaves Hafnia the largest operator in the segment and Oaktree as the 2nd largest shareholder at approx. 20% of Hafnia (Oaktree controlled ca 95% of CTI). Fearnley Securities is acting as financial advisors to CTI in the transaction as announced on 11th November 2021. On the crude side, we have seen a new sale in the Suezmax segment with M/T Densa Whale (158k dwt, blt 2012 Hyundai) sold for Usd 32-32.5 m to Greek buyers. There are limited references in this age, but we would say the price is somewhat lower than what we would expect. More in line with expectations was the sale of M/T Astro Perseus (159k dwt, blt 2004 Hyundai) at Usd 18.5 m. More interest also piling up on older Aframaxes and we expect transaction numbers to pick up.  Subdued Dry cargo rates and uncertainty stemming from falling forward freight agreements translate in a softening of buying interest. At least relative to the unhindered wave of buyers that the markets were so accustomed to. Sellers seem to have taken a standby approach rather than going to meet testing bids at levels lower than last done - saying that we do expect the odd correction that would traditionally come from Japanese sellers transacting at best.

We are witnessing a sentiment shift this week in the SnP markets with a loss of momentum in Dry cargo following a substantial correction in rates which resulted in an immediate weakening of buying interest. A loss of momentum which is particularly apparent in the volume of reported sales, but which has yet to transcribe into lower values. A resilience in pricing that can be attributed to sellers choosing to show composure in what many consider to be a temporary dip. Therefore, this week comes to a close with eight vessels changing hands at levels in line with their respective "last dones".  A stark contrast to the Tanker markets where the growing anticipation of a market upturn is leading an increase in buying enquiry. In terms of concluded business, the product sector is once again capturing most of the activity with five of the eight reported sales. Norden have committed their scrubber fitted  "NORD SKATE" and "NORD STINGRAY" (51K DWT 2009 STX) at Usd 17m each. A sale falling in line with Norden's effort to renew its MR fleet considering that earlier this month they acquired the two modern sisterships ECO LOS ANGELES and ECO CITY OF ANGELS (50K DWT HMD 2020) at Usd 36.5m each.

No major developments this week with unchanged sentiment across both sectors. The dry markets continue to see sustained liquidity with numerous deals to report each week and a steady stream of fresh sale candidates being placed in the market. This week has seen a particular pick up in activity on the modern front with a number of buyers now aiming for younger units. On the kamsarmax front, we have seen the Oshima built resale MV “RAMANA ROSE” being sold to Greek buyers at Usd 44m basis a prompt delivery from the yard while the Chinese built “SEACON SHANGHAI” (82k dwt 2019 Huangpu Wenchong) was sold at Usd 38m. A relative push in values for the modern units which becomes particularly apparent when compared against this weeks sale of the ten year old “KEY DISCOVERY” (82k dwt 2012 Tsuneishi Fukuyama) which achieved Usd 24m.  The product space has captured all of this weeks tanker activity with 5 MR units changing hands. Similarly we have seen notable movement on the modern front with two resales being sold at Usd 37.8m. The vessels are currently being built at the ex STX facilities now operating under the name K Shipbuilding – both units are due for delivery in 2022. A transaction that offers a well needed benchmark in a pricing environment that has been hostage to soaring NB prices. Values on the older vessels remain under pressure despite the relative pick up in liquidity – a sentiment well illustrated by the sale of the D'Amico controlled “High Venture” (51k dwt 2006 STX) which was sold at Usd 10.7m with DD freshly passed and BWTS installed.

Another week that has seen a series of dry cargo vessels being transacted at higher levels than their respective last done. Although this high weekly liquidity provides clear benchmarks for both parties to transact it can also become a moving target for buyers looking to meet the sellers’ fast changing expectations. The Supramax market has yet again seen a notable appreciation with the IKAN SELAYANG (56K DWT MITSUI 2013) being sold at Usd 26.5m. A comparable sale would be this of the sistership  “MEDI OKINAWA” (56K DWT MITSUI 2011) which was sold earlier this month at low Usd 23m. A notable dynamic remains the substantial ground gained by Japanese built vessels against alternative designs - this is particularly well illustrated by this weeks sale at Usd 21.75m of the WP BRAVE (58K DWT SPP 2012) which when compared to the sale of the Mitsui 56 highlight this growing rift.  Volume in the Tanker snp markets remains subdued with buyers remaining cautious by taking what seems to be a standby approach by waiting for a pick up in liquidity before considering meeting the current offer. Headline transaction this week is that of the 2 x LR2s sold by Navig8 to JP Morgan. The vessels were both built in 2018 at New Times, scrubberfitted and each achieved a price Usd 48m.

Following a series of headline announcements this week, the tanker space has for once joyed of most of the limelight and as such we thought we will give tankers the center stage of this weekly digest after being overshadowed by overwhelmingly active dry cargo markets. On Monday, Euronav publicly announced the acquisition of 5.5% of its stock by Fredriksen controlled entities. SEC filings have indeed confirmed that the Cyprus based Famatown Finance, a company beneficially owned by Mr. Fredriksen, has now increased its shareholding stake to 9.8% in the Belgian stock-listed owner Euronav. The move seems to be a welcomed sign for most tanker players as it firmly consolidates the current growing anticipation for a substantial market upturn. As mentioned throughout these previous weeks this growing sentiment was often made apparent by an ever increasing level of buying enquiry with owners struggling to acquire additional tonnage from a continuously thinning supply of sales candidates. In any case we expect this renewed momentum to spur several other parties into action which should see a strengthening of bids across the board in an effort to go meet the rising expectations of any potential seller. Other notable news in the product sector, is the sale of the two modern sisterships ECO LOS ANGELES & ECO CITY OF ANGELS (50K DWT HMD 2020) which were bought by Norden at Usd 36.5m each. The sale was made with the balance of the current charter to Trafigura attached, details of which remain undisclosed at this stage.  Volume of transactions in the dry snp markets remains unhindered with 20 reported sales this week. The larger segments have seen a rise in activity with two modern VLOC being sold to Eastern Pacific shipping, namely the STELLA BELLA & STELLA IVY (250k dwt, Qingdao Beihai, 2016 & 2015) which have respectively achieved Usd 60m and Usd 58m basis a 5 years charter attached to BHP. Another three Capesizes built from early to late 2000s have changed hands providing additional support and benchmark for future transactions in the space.

This week comes to a close with a number of fresh sales candidates being placed in the market continuing to drive liquidity across all dry segments. In terms of concluded business, the JP Morgan controlled capesize “TRUE ENDURANCE” (180K DWT HHI 2012) has now been sold to Turkish buyers at Usd 32.5m. The levels achieved fall in line with expectation as the last done in the sector is the “PROSPEROUS” (180K DWT SUNGDONG 2011) which was sold at Usd 31m last month. As expected from last week's negotiations, new supramax benchmarks have now been set with Japanese sellers committing the “MEDI OKINAWA” (56K DWT MITSUI 2011) at Usd 22.5m while the 2014 built Dolphin 57 “HTC CHARLIE” was sold at Usd 20.5m. The sale is pointing at a relative narrowing of the spread in value between Japanese and Chinese design which has recently been accentuated by the high volume of Japanese vessels changing hands.  Growing anticipation is definitely the name of the game in the Tanker segments where a strengthening buying enquiry is becoming ever so apparent. Signs of increased bids suggest that buyers are gradually moving upwards in an effort to drive potential sellers to transact and secure tonnage from a very thin supply of sales candidates. The product sector has seen the sale of the “IVY EXPRESS” (50K DWT STX 2009) which was sold to Greek buyers at Usd 15m setting a well needed target for potential MR players looking to transact units of similar vintage. Elsewhere, Xihe holdings finalised the sale of the VLCC “E MEI SAN” (317K DWT SWS 2010) which achieved Usd 39m by Far Eastern buyers.

This week comes to a close with yet again a number of transactions to add onto the dry snp tally - with markets not only showing no sign of respite but a momentum that seems to actually be picking up. New benchmarks are being set at a faster pace with heightened competition driving buyers to strike decisively in an effort to secure tonnage. Vessels able to give prompter deliveries will joy of the stronger bids with buyers scouting for any candidate able to offer them the yield offered by the chartering markets. This dynamic is particularly well illustrated in the Supramax/Ultramax sectors where the high liquidity of transactions highlights the more dramatic jump in values. The 2011 built Mitsui 56 “Medi Okinawa" is understood to be trading in the region of Usd 21.5m whereas only last week the 2011 IHI built “Ivy Delta” changed hands for a million less in what was already considered to be very strong price against last done. Similarly on the younger end of the spectrum we witness signs of ongoing negotiations on the modern ultramax front suggesting yet another upward correction in the near future.  Against this backdrop of activity the Tanker space is eerily silent with only three sales to report. Xihe Holdings is entering its final stages of proceedings with the sale of the OCEAN VELA (2009 SWS 109kdwt LR2) which invited offers end of last week and has now been committed at Usd 18.5m after attracting about 10 buyers outright - a number of potential buyers which highlights the now settled disparity between a strong buying enquiry and an ever thinning number of available candidates.

The dry market continues on the same pace and we note another week with stronger prices paid. The kamsarmax M/V Lowlands Nello (82k dwt, blt 2015 Sanoyas) has seen USD 32,2 mill in a deal with Chronos – this compares to the M/V Peak Liberty (82k dwt, blt 2015 Tsuneishi) which was reported last week at USD 30 mill. Suitably named M/V Million Bell and M/V Glad Mark (both 58k dwt, blt 2012 Kawasaki) are concluded at USD 22 mill each – half a million below Trans Oceanic (58k dwt, blt 2012 Tsuneishi) that was reported last week, but with deliveries in Q1 2022 there should be a good few months of earnings before handing over, so in total a sweeter deal for the sellers. The handies still receive their fair share of attention as well and based on the amount of enquires in the market we could expect a further lift on values going forward.  The tanker side is still fairly quiet, but with the increased activity in the spot markets and general optimism for a recovery to take place soon, we expect more interest. It seems older vessels are now sensibly adjusting closer and more related to scrap values, which is probably a sign that the support from sanctioned cargoes is easing off. Most activity is on the product segments with MRs being the most liquid asset – in an illiquid market. Prices have no clear direction, and flat is probably the best comment to make.

It is with no surprise that we are closing this week with yet another flurry of dry cargo transactions. From Handysize to Newcastlemax dry snp markets are joying of sustained liquidity, providing additional support and confidence to an ever increasing number of market players looking to acquire tonnage in view to yield the returns offered by an even more sustainable freight market. The Panamax/Kamsarmax segment seem to have captured the bulk of the enquiry this week. The sisterships “PEAK PEGASUS” & “PEAK LIBERTY” (82k dwt, 2013/2015, Tsuneishi Fukuyama) have been sold to Globus Maritime at a respective Usd 27m and Usd 30m while the 2019 Chinese built “SEACON SHANGHAI” was sold at a firm Usd 36m. The Japanese controlled “SEA VISION” (77k dwt, Imabari, 2015) invited offers on Wednesday after having north of 10 parties showing outright interest – best levels received are understood to be hovering around the Usd 29m mark, however the vessel remains in negotiation and we should be in a position to report further early next week.   A similarly unsurprising state of affairs on the tanker front but with a persistent lack of activity. These subdued SnP markets are however not necessarily reflective of the underlying sentiment which is somehow positive with a building anticipation that better days are not far off. Notable news this week is an apparent pick up in demolition with 4 VLCCs reported to have hit the beaches. Increased scrap rates have indeed been driving pockets of tanker activity with a number of overaged crude carriers also finding further trading buyers over the past few weeks. A tonnage phase out which is of course welcome in an already tight supply environment for Tankers which have seen no new order inked over the whole month of August.

Volume of transactions in the dry snp markets remains unhindered week after week with 15 vessels changing hands. The buying enquiries remain spread out across sectors with active buyers bidding across all sizes. The Ultramax/Supramax front is clearly leading the charge having captured 10 out of the 15 weekly reported sales. Although we continue to experience a relative climb in prices, the stream of potential sellers entering the market alleviates the upward pressure on values by diluting competition across a number of available candidates. Saying that the trend remains very much positive with TRF selling its two Hantong ultramax sisterships built 2016 and 2015 for an enbloc price of Usd 55m while Latsco achieved Usd 20.5m on its IVY DELTA (55k dwt built IHI 2011).  Tanker SnP remains subdued in terms of market activity - headlines were however stolen by SFL announcement of its acquisition of 3 x 2019 Suezmax tankers believed to be contracted at New Times by Trafigura. The transaction combines a TC back agreement to the sellers for a minimum of 5 years.

Despite Tanker chartering market seeing signs of recovery we continue to see subdued snp activity, with a growing list of buying enquiry failing to be met by any realistic sale candidates. In terms of concluded business, the M/T Starlight Venture (291k dwt, blt HHI 2004) is reported sold to Nigerian buyers at USD 30 mill. Lot of talks as well this week concerning the troubled MR M/T Marvin Independence (50k, blt Hyundai Mipo 2018). The vessel is a high spec, LNG-ready, IMO II, 20 grade MR that eventually went for auction at USD 17.1 mill to Greek buyers. We understand there are still several ongoing legal outstandings surrounding the vessel and its sale that may impact the transaction.  In the other hand, activity remains high in the Drybulk space with headlines being stolen by the Capesize sector this week which has seen Turkey’s Ciner emerge as the buyer of 3 x 2016 built units. The SWS and Dalian built vessels, M/V Stella Naomi, M/V Stella Hope and M/V Stella Nora – were sold at an enbloc price of Usd 132 mill including the balance of index-linked TCs attached. The sale provides a clear target and benchmarks for the owners that we have seen place fresh candidates in the market this week. Elsewhere, Malaysian Bulk Carriers joyed of the recent appreciation in values witnessed in the supramax front by selling its two Shin Kurushima built sisters M/V Alam Madu and M/T Alam Molek (both 58k dwt, blt 2014). The vessels were sold to Meghna of Bangladesh who is reported to have paid 26 mill each.

Subdued freight rates in the Tanker space are keeping S&P activity limited with only a handful of deals to report this week. The Judicial Managers of Xihe Holding have sold another VLCC - namely the M/T Chang Bai San (318k dwt, blt SWS 2012)  which achieved USD 41,50 mill – USD 2,65 mill down compared to the sister M/T Qi Lian San which was sold back in late April. On the older units we have seen M/T Katsuragisan (311k dwt, blt 2005 Kawasaki) sold for USD 30.3 mill. Fairly in line with expectations given current demolition rates but substantially lower than M/T Olympic Legend (309k dwt, blt 2003 Samsung) which got USD 31,5 mill in July. The latter was seen as very strong.  Dry cargo markets continue to joy of a number of transactions with a steady flow of sale candidates being placed on the market to meet the ever-increasing demand for tonnage. Supported by the solid footing provided by the charter markets sellers are raising their price expectations driving potential buyers above last done levels in order to secure a deal. Supramax and Ultramax segments continue to capture the bulk of the enquiry with vessels across all vintages regularly changing hands.

Despite a number of markets still in the midst of seasonal holidays, the dry snp market continue to draw sustained interest with a flurry of transactions to report this week. The Ultramax sector has seen three 2014 Jinling built units change hands for a price of Usd 67 m enbloc marking a further step up in values for Chinese built vessels. In comparison, the "SANTA BARBARA ( 2013, Iwagi, 61k dwt) was sold at Usd 24.5m this week underlying the premium priced in for Japanese designed units. Notable activity in the Handysize sector as well which has seen 8 vessels sold this week. With buying enquiry remaining strong and signs of ongoing negotiations across all sectors we expect the volume of transactions to remain.   Tanker markets remain subdued in terms of concluded business with pockets of activity on the vintage crude carrier front with owners driven to sell by high residual values off the back of continuous strong rate offered by cash buyers for demolition, however with expected decline going forward.

After a seasonal pause in our weekly reporting we are greeted back by promising snp markets which seem to have seen no sign of softening. Headlining the tanker space this week is the highly coveted product sector which has seen Ridgebury acquire a total of 6 vessels for an enbloc price of Usd 61m. Enquiry has indeed been high in the segment however with most players scouting for younger and scarcer sale candidates. Ridgebury therefore is offering a well needed benchmark in what has been a sustained illiquid deal environment. Elsewhere we continue to see vintage crude carriers achieving what can relatively be considered as healthy levels supported by a strong demolition market.    The dry sector has lost no steam over the summer with ten units changing hands this week. Interest remains high from a range of buyers looking to lock in the returns offered by an ever established freight market. Notable activity this week is the sale of a 2017 Hudong built Kamsarmax achieving a staggering price of Usd 31m, “TRANS AFRICA”.

In the tanker space we have witnessed some interesting transactions just before the holiday season kicks in and we see a continued lift in values on the older and bigger tankers. Olympic managed to squeeze out an extra bonus when they sold their M/T Olympic Legend (2003, Samsung, 309k dwt) at Usd 31.5 mill. No attenuating circumstances such as BWTS or scrubber that could have condoned this higher price even more so considering that she is due for docking later this year. It’s a good Usd 2.5 mill up from Maran’s sale of similarly aged VLCC only a couple of weeks back. A continued interest for modern tankers is proven yet again by JP Morgan’s move who have confirmed this week the purchase of 2 x 114k dwt LR2 resales from CMB. Although the vessels were originally caught up in the Hanjin Subic liquidation at building stage, they were subsequently completed in South Korea and have now achieved Usd 55 mill each. A relative strong price given the original yard and history of construction but one that underlines the current newbuilding markets with yards uninterested to go meet the tanker demand having taken on a flurry of more competitive container orders on their orderbooks.  Perhaps the first week within this past month that most dry players have had the time to digest more recent activity with only a handful of sales to report. As previously reported the Cape market saw a number of units being placed for sale over the past weeks which are now changing hands. Namely the scrubber and BWTS-fitted “BULK DENMARK” (2010, Koyo, 181k dwt) which was picked up by Thenamaris at Usd 31m. JP Morgan also invited offers on their 2012 HHI built Capesize “TRUE ENDURANCE” earlier this week after having up to 10 parties registering their interest.

This week comes to a close with yet another flurry of transactions in the Dry cargo markets with up to twenty sales to report. Weekly benchmarks barely have time to set before being broken by ever increasing values making any potential purchase a constant moving target for buyers eager to capture the returns offered by fruitful freight markets. The Supramax and Ultramax segments have captured the vast majority of transactions with twelve vessels changing hands this week resulting in substantial gains on asset values. Notably we have seen 2017 built SDARI 64s achieving Usd 25m while the "BULK PATAGONIA" (2012, Kawasaki, 58k dwt) was sold at a firm Usd 20.5m. Elsewhere the Greek controlled "SERENE SUSANNAH" (2010, STX Dalian, 58k dwt) was sold at Usd 15m. Worth noting in this context that the same owners sold the exact sistership "SERENE LYDIA" at Usd 8.5m in February this year. These renewed values are already on the brink of becoming a short lived history with buyers putting forward levels above last done in a bid to secure tonnage in an increasingly competitive environment.   After a spike of niche VL activity last week the tanker market has seen close to zero transactions this week; however with skyrocketing dry values we are witnessing a shift of enquiry into the tanker segments with several buyers preferring to chase tonnage in illiquid tanker market that have seen values flatten over the past weeks. Notable activity in the product sector with whispers of a number of mid 2000 built MRs in the process of being sold.

The continued depression over the sport markets has slowed down the S&P activity even further in the tanker space. However, we have seen a new benchmark on modern VLCCs in a deal between two listed entities. Frontline added two more VLs with the purchase of M/T Nissos Antiparos and M/T Nissos Santorini from Okeanis Eco Tankers – both vessels are 318k dwt, built at Hyundai and with scrubbers installed. The price of USD 90 m shows a clear upturn and that there is willingness for the right ships of good specs. An obvious comparison and indicator is Hunter Group’s sale of M/T Hunter Atla (blt 2019 at DSME) back in February at USD 84.5 m.  In the Dry space, we have a new benchmark of around 10 year old Chinese Capesize with the sale of “SPRINGBANK” (2010, New Times, 177k dwt) at USD 26.5 m. Except for few auction sales recently, the most comparable one is the “PACIFIC CANOPUS” (2012, Dalian, 180k dwt), sold for USD 21 m end March. Taking the age difference into consideration, we would estimate an increase of about 50% in value the past 3 months for this vintage. The lack of modern Japanese units available along with the steep development in pricing on these units have increased the focus on Chinese built tonnage. Charter hires paid are not justifying sufficient premium for the prices asked for Japanese built tonnage lately. Same is illustrated with the sale of “ELINDA MARE” (2010, New Century, 80k dwt) at USD 18.5 m. Just a month ago, sister vessel “XIN FENG” was sold for USD 16.5 m. We expect new benchmark in the Supramax sector with the “BULK COSTA RICA” (2010, NACKS, 58k dwt) inviting offers today. Reportedly over 10 buyers have purchased the report and the expected sales price is in the very high teens.

As expected and reflected throughout our previous reports, this week has seen an increased momentum in the capesize sector. With most fundamentals pointing towards a sustained period of increased rates the cape market is most definitely catching up in terms of SnP activity. We understand that 4 vessels have changed hands this week, partly driven by sellers looking to capture the upside on units purchased earlier in the cycle. An asset play made quite apparent by the ongoing negotiation taking place on the "CAPE LEGACY" ( 2011, Daehan, 180K dwt) purchased at USD 32.5 m in 2015 and now understood to be aiming  for numbers in xs of USD 30 m. Understand the sale is yet to be finalised however illustrates particularly well the current drive witnessed in the market. Elsewhere, Cobelfret have sold their 2011 built HHIC "LOWLANDS TENACITY" at USD 29.5 m which suggests that the abovementioned targets should be achievable in the near future.   Notable activity in the Tanker space lies on the overage front with a rise in steel prices driving the value on vintage front. Last week's reported sale of the “JUPITER" ( 2000, Daewoo, 300K dwt) is now confirmed at USD 27 m marking a substantial appreciation in value. The measure of this increase becomes particularly apparent considering that Mercuria bought the vessel in January this year for USD 19.5 m. Worth noting however, that post purchase Mercuria retrofitted the vessel for FSO activities applying a positive pressure on pricing. Nevertheless, we expect these increased scrap rates to drive the second hand value of these vintage units upwards and drive potential sellers out of the woods.

Another busy week in the Dry cargo markets which have seen a number of transactions continuing to consolidate the now well established upward trend we have been witnessing across all segments. Supramax and Ultramax  prices have seen another jump with the sale of the “NORD OLIVE” (2014, Oshima, 56k dwt) which was sold by Norden at Usd 22.5m while the Japanese controlled  “WHITE HAWK” (2012, Oshima, 61k dwt) was sold at Usd 20.9m. To put the longevity of the abovementioned trend in perspective, Norden acquired the vessel in December last year at a price of Usd 14m. Chinese designs have also followed suit with Hayfin disposing of the last of their 14 Ultramax units; namely the “GH DAWN RUN” (2018, Yangfan, 64k dwt) which was sold at Usd 23.5m to Greek buyers. Elsewhere the Cape segment also joyed of improved values with the “BULK KYUSHU” (2006, Imabari, 180k dwt) achieving Usd 20.5m whereas only last month the 2004 Koyo built “MINERAL KYOTO” was sold for Usd 15.5m.   Tanker markets remain quiet in terms of concluded transactions however some notable activity this week on the VLCC front with Athenian Tankers selling the “ATHENIAN VICTORY” (2009, HHI, 317k dwt) at Usd 42.5m. This breaks a long period of inactivity for Korean designed units of region ten years of age with most recent comparable sales being those of the Xihe Holding units, which saw a number of Chinese VLs being sold through the liquidation process undertook by the judicial managers.

The Dry cargo markets have most definitely regained the headlines this week with freight rates continuing on their unhindered rally supported by a flurry of snp transactions who have become tribute to the overwhelming positive market consensus that these renewed rates have settled for the foreseeable future. On the Kamsarmax front, JP Morgan invited offers on the 3rd of June on their sisterships “PEAK PEGASUS” & “PEAK LIBERTY” (82k dwt, 2013 / 2015, Tsuneishi Japan). Sellers invited up to 10 outright buyers to bid and both vessels have now been committed enbloc at Usd 23.75m & Usd 26.75m respectively. To put levels in perspective, same owners disposed of the 2013 built sistership “PEAK PROTEUS” in May at a price of Usd 21.5m marking an increase of approximately 10% in less than a month. This positive trend is spreading across all sectors, even more so this week in the Supramax segment where the Japanese controlled “DONAU K” (58k dwt, 2012, Kawasaki) achieved a price of Usd 19.6m marking a substantial jump in values considering that only two weeks ago the same age sister ship “PACIFIC HERO” was sold at Usd 18m. With a buying enquiry showing no signs of slowing down and a number of underbidders left to try and secure alternative units, we expect additional tonnage being placed for sale by sellers looking to capture the ever increasing value offered by these improving markets.  Very little to report on the Tanker front this week with persistent subdued rates holding any potential buyers from going to meet the ever thinning list of potential sale candidates. Most activity being found in the mid 2000 built crude carriers where we continue to witness signs of ongoing activity suggesting further sales in the near future.

With the rally we are seeing both in the Dry cargo and container market, there is not much to write home about in the tanker market. The chartering market continues to struggle, with VLCC and Suezmax’s producing negative charter returns. SKS have sold their “SKS SATILLA” (2006, HHI, 158K DWT) for USD 23.25m. The price achieved falls in line with the sale of the one year younger sistership “SKS SPEY” (2007, HHI,158K DWT) which was sold for USD 24m a few weeks ago. Moreover, we understand that the LR2 “CHAMPION PLEASURE” (2008, Namura,105K DWT) has been sold in an off-market transaction to Union Maritime for USD 18.1m. The price represents a small downtick in values when comparing to the one year younger “CHAMPION PROSPERITY” (2009, Sasebo,115K DWT) which was sold end April for USD 19.7m.  Another week with activity on all dry segments except for Capesizes, which seem to be taking a breather with lack of modern candidates being marketed for sale. China Development Bank Leasing steals the headlines acquiring the ex-Hayfin / Celsius fleet of 6 x Ultramaxes and the ex-Clipper controlled 11 vessel fleet of handysizes and Supra/Ultramaxes paying about USD 270 m for the two fleets in total. Noteworthy sales include new benchmarks for 15 year old Japanese Supramaxes setting the price tag at abt USD 13 m with the sale of the Olympic Oshima and Mitsui 2006 built Supramaxes “OLYMPIC PEACE” and “OLYMPIC PRIDE” at USD 25.5 m enbloc. For reference, the previous sale of a 2006 Japanese built Supramax, “CORAL ISLAND” (2006, Oshima, 55k dwt), was end February for USD 10 m. Lastly, as we have written in the recent reports, we are seeing an increase on value of Chinese tonnage with the sale of the Dolphin 57 “OLYMPIC PEGASUS” (2011, COSCO Guangdong, 57K DWT) at USD 14.8 m. Just a month ago, the “SILVIA AMBITION” (2011, Yangfan, 57K DWT) was sold for around USD 12.5 m. Costamare has reportedly purchased the “INTERLINK COMITY” (2010, Huatai, 37K DWT) for USD 12.8 m. The sister vessel, “SREDNA GORA” was sold for USD 11.6 m just few weeks back. We expect this trend to continue with the sharp increase of price of Japanese tonnage.

In the Tanker market, most focus is still on the older vessels, but we sense that Chinese purchase interest is cooling off a bit and the last week has seen fewer transactions concluded. Recent changes in the Chinese import policies (quotas) seems to have an effect and there is a significant drop in purchase enquiries with Chinese addresses. If this continues, we could expect an effect on the pricing of the older units, but on the other hand do strong steel prices play an important role also here, with a continued push on the demolition prices. New Shipping are reported to have sold their M/T “NEW DIAMOND” (299k dwt, 2000, Mitsui) to demo/cash buyers GMS for USD 22 m – or $564,50/ton (gross). It’s important to note that M/T ”NEW DIAMOND” and the likes are among the lightest VLCCs built in that period, and whilst these have LDT in the region 38500-39000 tons, the larger (and heavier) Koreans of same age often are in the region of 43000 tons and some pushing towards 48000 tons. To put things in context – we are approaching USD 25 m demolition prices on some VLCCs, and hopefully more will follow Mr. Polemis’ example.  We continue to see Dry bulk asset prices catching up with the chartering market. This week, Enesel Group backed Valhalla, decided to take profit on some Ultramaxes with the sale of 2 x DACKS resales being delivered 2022 for USD 29.2mil each to Genco. This sale is sure to set a new benchmark for resales on both Chinese and Japanese built Ultramaxes. Furthermore on handies, M/V “SIDER SYROS” (38k dwt, 2016, Minaminippon) was sold at firm USD 20.7 m to Orient shipping, which demonstrates the strength of the market and will set another strong benchmark for Japanese built handies.

Stealing the headlines this week is the transaction announced by Frontline who has confirmed the purchase of six VLCC resales currently under construction at HHI. The vessels were part of an eight ship series originally contracted by Central Shipping with deliveries ranging from Q1 2022 until Q1 2023.  The aggregate purchase price stands at Usd 565.8m setting benchmarks for resale VLCCs at Usd 94.3m per unit. Current market environment seem to be validating the deal for all parties involved with buyers achieving relatively lower levels against current newbuilding offer and sellers booking a significant upside on the original contract price which is reportedly around Usd 90m per ship. Additionally these early contracts are offering prompter deliveries in a newbuilding environment that sees both pricing on the rise and slot availability for conventional tonnage slip into 2024. Elsewhere in the Tanker space we continue to see a sustained second hand activity for units built in mid-2000 across both the product and crude sectors with a steadily increasing buying enquiry suggesting upward pressure on pricing in the short to medium term.   The Dry Cargo markets have seen a pick-up in activity on the capesize front with a number of buyers entering the market looking to secure additional tonnage. In terms on concluded business the Japanese controlled “AUSTRALIA MARU” (180k dwt, built 2012, KOYO) has been sold to Seanergy at Usd 33.5m. The vessel is both BWTS and scrubber fitted and is achieving levels in line with the upward momentum witnessed in the segment. Seanergy captured most of the snp activity on the cape front with the “AUSTRALIA MARU” being their fifth acquisition this year. Elsewhere Norden has sold their 2014 built “NORD HUDSON” built at NACKS for a price of Usd 21.1m which again represents a relative jump against last week’s comparable sales. To conclude we have witnessed some notable activity in the Handysize market with six vessels changing hands this week.

The holidays are over in most regions, and activity is picking up again. Zodiac have scored on their 4th VLCC from Xihe, with the purchase of M/T JIN HUA SAN (317k dwt, blt 2009 SWS) at USD 36.8 mill. This is $2,5 mill up from the sister M/T TAI SAN (also SWS 2009) that was done back in October last year. Still – these forced sales are not representative for the general market, and with the growing interest we expect prices to continue climbing. As we all know, there is still not much support to get from the physical markets but increasing steel prices have an impact both on the NB prices and demolition values, and as such pulling everything up. These tendences are evidenced with two 2004 built VLCCs sold - M/T STARLIGHT VENTURE (291k, blt 2004 HHI) at USD 30.6 mill and M/T NEW CENTURY (299 dwt, blt 2004 Universal) at USD 31 mill which clearly show the trend. An easy reference here is DHT’s sale of their three 2004 models only a month ago. Despite their scrubbers and Cap 1 rating the price obtained was a fair bit lower at USD 29,6 mill (on average) each. We would guess the buyers of these could score a nice profit by flipping as the scrubbers should give a further premium compared to the most recent deals. The fuel spread seems to continue to widen. Okeanis Eco Tankers’ LR2s – all 115k, built Hyundai 2015 and with scrubbers have been widely discussed in the market. SOCAR was pointed out as the buyer, but this week it surfaced that Torm managed to pull it together at the end. A nice deal for both parties it seems, and the official price is USD 40,25 mill each. With the shipyards leaning back, and the general good interest, we expect prices to keep moving north.  Another week with dry sales of all sizes and new benchmarks set. Notable sales include the 2012 Japanese built Kamsarmaxes “SPRING AEOLIAN” and “TANGERINE ISLAND”, both sold for region USD 21m each. This compares with the 2012 Japanese built Kamsarmax “KINOURA” which was sold for USD 18m end of February, and illustrates clearly the development. With the increased prices and competition on Japanese vessels, we also witness a firming trend on the value of Chinese tonnage. Sister vessels “PEDHOULAS FARMER” and “PEDHOULAS BUILDER” (2012, Zhejiang Ouhua, 81k dwt) have been reported sold for USD 22m each. The scrubbers and BWTSs fitted on both have a clear effect, but this is still a strong substantial jump compared to the previous 2012 Chinese built Kamsarmax sold, “EVERGLORY” end February at USD 16m. We see an increased amount of interest from buyers for around 10 – 15-year-old bulkers, and with the steep increase of the demo prices along with the firm dry market, we expect a continued rise across all sectors and age in dry.

Despite a week shortened by a number of national bank holidays, the markets continue to joy of healthy amount of transactions. On the tanker front, activity has picked up on the mid 2000 product carriers with three vessels changing hands this week and signs of a number of ongoing inspections and negotiations suggesting further activity in the near future. Empire Navigation have sold the Chinese built “MR ARIES” (2009, GSI, 50k dwt) at Usd 13.5m setting a benchmark for MR units of Chinese design. To put values in perspective, the last comparable sale was of a 2008 Korean built deepwell unit sold last week at xs of Usd 13m. The relative lack of  transaction in other tanker segments is not reflective of the current appetite for tonnage with buyers being met by a fading offer from sellers that are taking a standby stance in view of better days ahead.   Dry SnP markets continue to see a flurry of sales with the Supramax segment capturing most of the activity this week with 6 vessels changing hands. Dolphin 57 design units are seeing their value on the rise with Cosmoship disposing of their sisterships “LEGACY & OLYMPIC” (2011/2012, Jinling, 57k dwt) at USD 28m. Indicative of the unhindered rally in values witnessed over the past several months, these vessels were acquired by the sellers in September last year for an enbloc price of Usd 17.8m.

We have seen healthy activity levels across the board as owners are looking to place their chips for the long awaited upswing in the tanker market. Ridgebury stole the headline this week and have bought 4 x 2007 and 1 x 2006 Dalian built VLCC’s at USD 120m. The vessels all have a BB attached to Euronav until 2021, giving them downside protection before the chartering market is expected to recover. Furthermore, Thenamaris bought the 2 year younger sister ship “NEW CREATION” for USD 37.5m. International Seaways have sold their CAP 1 rated “SEAWAYS TANABE” (2002, HITACHI, 300K DWT) to Chinese buyers for USD 24m, which falls in with last week’s sale of the “MARAN CARINA” (2003, DSME, 306K DWT) at USD 24m when we take survey positions into account. Liquidity in the vintage Suezmax space remains healthy and we understand that Tsakos have sold the “SILIA T” (2002, HHI, 164K DWT) for USD 15.8m. The deal falls in line with pricing achieved on the “EUROFAITH” (2004, HHI, 151K DWT) which also changed hands this week for USD 18m, once relevant discounts for age applied. In the product market, Cido are rumoured to have committed the “LR2 POSEIDON” (2009, SASEBO, 110K DWT)  and  “LR2 POLARIS & LR2 PIONEER”(2008, SASEBO, 110K DWT) on subject finance terms for low 60s enbloc to undisclosed buyers. Pricing looks attractive compared to last week’s sale of the uncoiled “CHAMPION PROSPERITY” (2009, SASEBO, 115K DWT) which achieved a price of USD 19.8m after seeing a hefty amount of interest.   With the Golden week coming up in China and the Easter holidays in Greece, we have seen good activity across all the segments in dry although expect this to come off next week. Notable sales on the dry side include the widebeam Kamsarmax resales ex-Chengxi Shipyard from Foremost Group with delivery this year to Yasa Shipping of Turkey at USD 28.5m each. With newbuilding prices at region USD 27 – 28m in China, we regard the deal as a favourable one for the buyers considering delivery in the strongest dry market we have seen in a decade. Scrubber and BWTS-fitted “EMERALD STAR” (2014, TESS CEBU, 82K DWT) have been reported sold for USD 25.1m after receiving initial offers at region 23-24m. “PACIFIC BRIGHT” (2013, Hantong, 57K DWT) sold for USD 14.8m illustrates a substantial increase (about 50%) in value of Chinese built Supramaxes comparing to same age Dolphin 57 “GLOVIS MADONNA” sold for USD 9.7 m early this year. The sale is also a good indicator for the discount to Japanese design, when comparing to the sale of “LOWLANDS PATRASCHE” (2013, TESS CEBU, 58K DWT) at USD 18.2m.

Activity level remains high in most tanker segments. Even on LR1s the tension increases, and a few deals being negotiated and/or placed on subs. Whilst not many new firm sales to report in the larger segments, there are ongoing discussions, and new deals and probably new benchmarks will surface soon. There is a general upwards trend for asset values in most segments, and with the sale of Aframax STAVANGER BLISS (105k dwt, blt Sumitomo 2008) at USD 19.5 mill, we have a clear indicator when compared to the LR2 CHAMPION PROSPERITY (115k dwt, blt Sasebo 2009) at USD 19.8 mill last week. Even though reported not to be in perfect condition – at least on paper, CHAMPION PROSPERITY is a more attractive vessel with her size, coating and age in her favor. Higher transaction volume and increasing values inevitably makes for wider bid/ask spreads, and we may see deal-making dragging out a bit in time as the underlying earnings are not showing any positive signs as yet.  The dry market continues the upward path and the BDI is now at 2788, the highest level since 2010. The capes are now leading the charge and there are rumours that EIBHLIN (182k dwt, Univeral, 2011) is done at xs USD 30mill, with some even reporting USD 31-32mill. If true, this would be a huge step up from UNITED BREEZE (181k dwt, Imabari, 2012) which was sold only a month ago for USD 29.5mill. Genco has picked up SERENA R (64k dwt, Yangfan, 2016) for USD 20.5mill. This sale adds to a good volume of 5yrs old Chinese Ultras, which have consolidated around last done price levels and created a strong benchmark.

Momentum continues to build in the tanker SnP markets with an increasing number of transactions materialising this week. The Japanese controlled LR2 “CHAMPION PROSPERITY” (115k dwt, built Sasebo, 2009, Coated) invited offers after having north of 20 buyers inspecting. The vessel is now committed at a price of Usd 19.8m to Greek buyers. The strong interest is not only a clear indicator of the growing appetite for quality tanker tonnage but when compared to the sale of the one year older “FALCON EXPRESS” (115k dwt, built Sasebo, 2009, Coated) sold last month at Usd 14.5m; the price achieved this week points to a clear upward trend in values which should remain unhindered with a number of buyers finding themselves looking for alternative opportunities in a market with a thin supply of sale candidates. Also increasing activity across most product segments as seen by East Med’s purchase of SOCATRA’s two HMD resales. Both vessels deliver in 2022, and the price is reported at Usd 35.5 mill each – presumably on novation basis. Even for LR1s which normally is a pretty illiquid class we see more deals surfacing.  The dry markets seem to have met some relative stability following the steep appreciation in values witnessed over recent weeks. Most reported transactions are now falling in line with last done, consolidating benchmarks across sectors. Saying that, buying enquiry remains strong with sign of ongoing negotiations however a constant stream of tonnage being placed for sale seems to be keeping a lid on competition and contributing to the abovementioned flattening in prices – famous last words.

A shift of activity this week with the tanker sector seeing an increased level of activity. Vintage crude carriers have joyed of strong buying interest with DHT reported to have disposed of three 2004 DSME built scrubber-fitted VLCC’s. The number of comparable VLCC's now sold amount to seven over the past month with Far Eastern buyers leading the charge. Notable activity in the product space with the sale of “OVERSEAS GULF COAST” (2019, HMD, 50k dwt) which was sold to Eastern Pacific Shipping at a price of Usd 32.5m. The transaction breaks a long streak of inactivity for units of such vintage considering that the last comparable sale dates back end of last year. This notable illiquidity on the modern front is particularly well illustrated by a relatively flat value curve.  We have seen a substantially lower number of dry sales compared to the frenzy witnessed over the past few weeks. Notable sale this week is “NORD STELLAR” (2016, Hudong, 82k dwt) sold for Usd 25.5m to Greek buyers. Same vessel was sold for Usd 20m early December last year, ex-name SBI Zumba.

Activity in the dry snp market is sustained with sales ranging across all sectors. Compared to the substantial jumps witnessed over the past few weeks, values seem to have relatively stabilised for the time being with levels paid broadly falling in line with last done. However few particular segments such as very modern Japanese and top tier Chinese Kamsarmax/Ultramax have caught up in terms of liquidity this week resulting in values marking a more significant jump. Notably we are now seeing very modern tonnage achieving relative premiums against current newbuilding prices. With the lack of such second hand candidates being openly marketed for sale, we expect the sellers to keep the upper hand against an ever increasing buying enquiry. The recent uptick in values of Japanese handysizes seem to have changed the focus of buyers to Chinese tonnage which should trigger a narrowing of the gap currently witnessed between Chinese and Japanese built vessels.   With subdued freight rates continuing to loom across most tanker segments buyers are not yet finding the incentive to increase their bids; this against a background of sellers that share a more general consensus that a market upturn is underway for the 2nd half of this year. This trend is evident by the nature of the this week’s reported sales whereas 6 out of 11 transactions are bank driven.
