Values of 10 year product tankers seem to have bottomed out after a period of continuous downward correction with the sale of 2010 Iwagi built MR “NORD INSPIRATION” at a reported sales price of Usd 15.75m.

The 25 vessels changing hands this week across all dry segments are to say the least a clear indicator of the sentiment engulfing the dry markets. As expected the Capesize sector has followed suit with three sales this week leading values upwards. The Japanese controlled “UNITED BREEZE”  (2012, Imabari, 180k dwt) has achieved Usd 29.5mill being the 5th Cape sale this month. To put levels in perspective, the one year older “COLOGNY” (2011, Tsuneishi Cebu, 180k dwt) was sold last month at Usd 22.9mill which, even when taking into consideration the discount carried by the Cebu design against Imabari, illustrates particularly well the appreciation in pricing.   The Kamsarmax/Panamax sector has seen 12 sales this week with notable activity on the modern Kamsarmax front with the “KARLOVASI” (2016, Oshima, 82k dwt) being sold to Norden at Usd 27mill. The last comparable sold unit of similar design and vintage dates back to December last year when the “SAKIZAYA NOBLE” (2017, JMU, 80k dwt) was sold at Usd 25.5mill. The Ultramax and Supramax sectors continue to joy of very strong levels of buying enquiry with a consistent stream of sale candidates being placed on the market by owners looking to extract the value currently offered by competing buyers.

The strong physical dry bulk market has been picked up by capital market participants with rising asset values and continued strong rates translating into higher share prices and premium pricing to NAV, which in turn may tempt other listed companies to follow Belships example of raising capital for growth. We had another week where we saw the values increase across the line. Seanergy acquired Capesize BULK SWITZERLAND (2010, Imabari, 181k dwt) at Usd 25.6 mill, which is up from the sale of COLOGNY (2011, TESS CEBU, 180k dwt) at Usd 22.9 mill a month ago and will set a new benchmark for 10 year olds. Other notable sales include LADY GIOVI (2007, Mitsui, 82k dwt) reported sold for Usd 16.1 mill to Castor Maritime. For comparison the one year younger Oshima built Kamsarmax FORTUNE RAINBOW was sold for Usd 14mill three weeks back. Another interesting sale was EASTERN EDELWEISS (2012, Hantong, 57k dwt), which was liquidated in bank sale in June last year for Usd 8.1 mill, now resold for Usd 11.8 mill.   Although activity in the tanker markets remains limited in terms of completed transactions, we see an increasing number of buying enquiries seeking to take advantage of the current correction in values and position themselves for the upcoming market rebound which seems to have become the general consensus among most market players. Many buyers were in the running for ex Xihe owned VLCC CHANG BAI SAN 2012 SWS built which ended up being sold to Pantheon for Usd 44 mill. In the clean sector, the two sisterships LEOPARD SUN (2013, SPP, 50k dwt) and LEOPARD MOON (2013, SPP, 50k dwt) have now been sold at Usd 21.4 mill each setting a well needed benchmark for units of such vintage considering that the last comparable sale dates back to November. We expect volume of sale to remain limited in the short term with sellers choosing to stand their ground therefore widening the existing bid offer spread.

Another week that has seen a flurry of dry transactions with values continuing their unhindered upward drive. The Supramax/Ultramax sector has seen five vessels changing hands with the notable sale of Japanese controlled BASIC PORTLAND (61k dwt, 2016 Sanoyas) which achieved Usd 21.5m from Greek buyers. The transaction illustrates well the current momentum considering that only last week the same owners disposed of BULK HERO ( 61k dwt, 2016 Shin Kurushima) at Usd 20.5m. Signs of ever increasing buying enquiries with ongoing negotiations that clearly means that the upward trend is set to continue. On the larger segments, Panamax/Kamsarmax also joy of strong activity with four vessels being sold whereas Capesize slowly seem to follow suit with a number of candidates being placed for sale suggesting further sales in the near future. Also worth mentioning the Newcastlemax resale 2021 SWS at Usd 53m where initial expectations were region Usd 50m. Prices are clearly moving north in case anyone was in doubt.  OPEC+ rolls over current production levels into April, and Saudi Arabia will only gradually return its 1mbpd additional cut. Not exactly what tanker owners would be hoping for, and leaves downside risk for earnings the next couple of months. However our outlook for improving tanker rates in the second half of the year remains unchanged; certainly a view shared by many owners who are increasingly getting ready to move for attractive candidates. Our read being that we have passed the bottom as far as values go (save for the oldest ones) and sellers will increasingly hold the upper-hand. Exciting times ahead.

Crude spot market remains sad and depressing, but another modern VLCC was sold this week when Hunter announced the exit of its 1,5 year old HUNTER ATLA (delivered Sept 2019). A price of USD 84.5 mill paid by ADNOC is considered firm by some market players, but in our books it is a fair level – especially in light of the recent pricing from leading shipyards. Generally speaking, there are not many sellers of modern tonnage in this space today. Still, we see an impressive number of takers for older crude tankers, and prices keep up fairly well.  Given the scrap-levels on offer, the poor earnings in the (conventional) market and the increasing bunker prices we had expected more older ships sold for demolition. There is a strong demand in the product market and both MR and LR2 tonnage in decent condition and age do get a lot of attention.  The dry markets continue to display strength. Supramax rates are up excess 40% the last week, breaking USD 20k/day on Wednesday for the first time in a decade. Even crazier, the historically less volatile handies are also on fire where the Baltic has recorded over a month of daily consecutive gains and are now at excess USD 19k/day. There are a lot of bidders on available ships for sale and we expect values to quickly follow suit. Also this week we see a lot of activity on region 10yrs old Kamsars, and again the values are increasing slightly from last week. Less transactions for the modern Eco units, but that is not due to a lack of buyers. There are many owners scavenging the market for Eco units in fear of future IMO requirements, but there is simply very few units for sale. The only one this week was the BULK HERO (61k dwt, Universal, 2016) sold at at USD 20.6mill, which will represents a new benchmark on the 5yrs old Ultramax.

Boom! A surprisingly strong dry market has caught most off guard, and we have this week seen the highest rates for both Panamax and Supramax since 2010. The surge is on back of strong demand for grains and coal in the Far East, but also a general pick up in demand all over. We continue to see a flurry of deals for region 10yrs old Kamsarmax with the KINOURA (82k dwt, Tsuneishi, 2012) sold at USD 18mill, the EVERGLORY (81.5k dwt, Qingdao Beihai, 2012) sold at USD 16mill and the GLOBE ELECTRA/DANAE (81k dwt, STX, 2010) sold at USD 15.75mill each. All in all the sales point towards rising values, with the KINOURA being an exception. The market being most bullish on the Japanese built tonnage which is expected in an upturn, and in the next phase we expect that re-pricing of the Chinese built tonnage will outperform.    Tanker sale and purchase markets remain subdued with limited liquidity. The ever deepening bid/offer spread renders transactions hard to materialize with potential sellers holding back in view of better times. Only three sales to report this week with new downward benchmarks being set in the MR sector with the sale of the Japanese controlled pump-room unit BRIGHT FORTUNE (48k dwt, Iwagi, 2020) at USD 13.75mill.

Stock-listed dry companies are wasting no time monetizing their newly repriced shares as hard cash to scale their business. Eagle Bulk has acquired three 2011 Dayang built Supramaxes at region USD 29m financed with USD 21m in cash and 329k common shares which proves its financial flexibility as a listed company. We expect more such deals to materialize as long as P/NAV pricing remains favorable. Good activity in general on the dry side with several 10yrs benchmark sales to report this week. Lemos-backed Valhal Shipping picked up the scrubber fitted Capesize COLOGNY (180k dwt, 2011, TESS CEBU) for USD 22.9m. The last benchmark sale for a 10yrs old was the scrubber fitted CAPE ISTANBUL (176k dwt, 2011, HHIC-Phil) which went for USD 19m early this year. Albeit not directly comparable, the whopping USD 4m gap undoubtedly demonstrates the positive shift in sentiment. Another benchmark deal was the KIND SALUTE (96k dwt, 2011, Imabari) at USD 16.5m with docking due May 2021. To compare, SANGEET (96k dwt, 2012, Imabari) was sold for USD 15.5m late last year. Lastly, on Ultras we saw the ULTRA WOLLONGONG (62k dwt, 2011, Oshima) exchange hands at USD 13.8m.   Four mid-2000 built Aframax have been sold this week reaffirming the downward trend in values witnessed so far this year especially for units of such vintage. Teekay has disposed of its two 2008 built sisterships EXPLORER SPIRIT & NAVIGATOR SPIRIT (105k dwt, 2008, Tsuneishi) at Usd 16m each while Castor Maritime has purchased DUBAI HOPE & DUBAI HARMONY (115k dwt, 2005, Samsung) at Usd 13.6m. The correction in values becomes particularly apparent when compared to the sale of the 2009 built STAVANGER FALCON &  STAVANGER EAGLE (105k dwt, 2009 Sumitomo) which were sold earlier this year at USD18.25m each.

With the announcement that Star Bulk acquired 3xUltramaxes and 4xKamsarmaxes from Scorpio in a cash and stocks deal and that the remaining 3xUltramaxes are rumoured to be committed, Scorpio is finally exiting the dry bulk segment. There has been rising prices throughout the sales process the last few months on the back of an increasingly bullish sentiment on dry. For comparison, the SBI ZEUS 2016/Mitsui/60kdwt was sold for Usd 18.5 mill end October while the SBI CRONOS 2015/I-S/60kdwt was sold this week for Usd 19.6 mill. This represents at least an increase of 10% in the midst of a grand sell off, which really support the dry story. The straightening of the depreciation curve is in full motion, but further big increases on values would have to come from rising resale prices. The sale of URSULA MANX 2021/TESS-Zhoushan/82kdwt this week and UNA MANX 2021/TESS Zhoushan/82kdwt reported last week at Usd 29.5 mill each demonstrate that resale prices are still hovering around newbuilding prices.    GNMTC of Libya has acquired two more scrubberfitted LR2 newbuilding resales after its recent purchase of a similar resale just delivered from a Japanese builder. The last two vessels will very soon be delivered ex Cosco Shipyard and the price of Usd 52.5 mill each is about 5% lower than the first deal which one would expect as a minimum when comparing Japan vs China yard pricing. Whilst GNMTC might be considered an “exotic” buyer we certainly subscribe to this being a market deal and underlines where ask levels are for brand new tonnage. Goal posts may quickly be moved in what is becoming a sellers’ market for brand new ships, despite the present dire state of the spot market. Values for older/vintage VLCC are still holding up nicely, but the other crude segments of this age have a more brutal reality check with the majority of enquiries being for the 8-10 year old crude and LR2 tankers. Bets will continue to be placed on a rebound of fortunes come 2nd half/end 2021 and into 2022.

Public-listed bellwethers continue to seize attractive buying opportunities in the crude sector. Following DHT’s well-timed acquisition of two 2016 DSME built VLCC tankers last week, Euronav came out on top in the competition for two Suezmax newbuildings at Daehan, both with delivery in January 2022. These were cancelled contracts and sold by the yard, not as resales but by entering into new contracts between the builder and Euronav with what we understand is 30% down-payment. Daehan invited offers on Tuesday and the deal was done the next day with several strong names in the running. We can confidently conclude that the bottom is behind us as far as values for very modern tankers goes. Big question now being who else will sell at these levels. As such we see an upside for the modern ones. Leading yards are also upping the prices.     The dry S&P market is powering. Whilst 2nd hand values moved sideways last year, strong demand now makes for a more dynamic pricing and values are up by abt 10% for the modern units and abt 20% for 15 year olds since Mid-December.

On the tanker market we have seen notable activity with three modern VLCC’s sold this week setting some much needed benchmarks for units of similar vintage. Following its purchase in November of TRF HORTEN built 2018 at HHIC-Phil at Usd 72m, Delta Tankers of Greece has now acquired the one year older sistership HUDSON for Usd 71.5m. Both vessels were sold by TRF who is also a 50% shareholder of the sisterships ECO QUEEN and ECO FUTURE built 2016 DSME which are sold at Usd 68m each to DHT Holdings. We expect liquidity on the modern front to pick up momentum in the near future supported by an increasing amount of enquiry with a market consensus anticipating a recovery for the second half of this year. Newbuilding prices have certainly passed their bottom spurred by a combination of increased steel prices, strengthening local currencies vs USD and a strong influx of large container vessel projects.  Dry SnP markets continue to joy of high volumes of transactions with vessels changing hands across all sectors. Pricing-wise it seems that most market players are still looking to digest the recent appreciation in values that we witnessed last week with buyers looking to figure out whether this is indeed the start of a sustained upward trend in values rather than a one off glitch in what has been until now a relatively flat market.

It has been a strong week for dry earnings, with Capesizes pushing above USD 26k/d from last week’s level of USD 17.5k/d. However, gains have been levelling out in recent days on the back of a very volatile paper market. The S&P activity is brisk across all segments with a large number of vessels transacted. Older Capesize values are the first to benefit from the newfound optimism which is well illustrated by the sale of OCEAN COMPASS (2006/Imabari/180kdwt) which achieved a price of Usd 17.5 mill this week. This appreciation in values for older units is not only supported by a firming chartering environment but also by strengthening demolition rates which is approaching USD 500/LDT. We expect this momentum to continue with sellers starting to raise their price expectations leaving an increasing amount of buyers competing over a thinning number of available candidates.  Activity on the tanker front is limited to tonnage of around 10 year of age and older with a number of older crude carriers changing hands this week. Three sales to report in the VLCC sector where Navios Maritime has sold its NAVE CELESTE (2003/DSME/300kdwt) at Usd 25mill to Chinese buyers. Activity on the modern side remains subdued with weakening freight rates leading any potential seller to take a step back rather than face current bids by buyers looking to secure substantial discounts against last done.

New lockdowns are here but so are gradually vaccines, which hopefully means we may soon apply normal forecasting parameters again. All going well we expect decent average tanker earnings in 2021 based on a return of oil production and a turnaround in sentiment in 2nd half of the year. However the near term tanker outlook remains soft and 2nd hand values will remain under pressure. On that note, the year kicks off with a notable MR deal. Top Ships is reported to have sold three scrubberfitted MR newbuildings with delivery in February and March 2021 ex HMD. The price is reported to be just below Usd 34 mill each.  It’s a promising start of the year in the dry segments and the transaction volume remains steady across all segments. Capesize values may see an uptick on the back of an unexpected strong start.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel for tanker earnings and rates may have already bottomed for now as the delta in terms of tanker demand looks decidedly positive over the next few months. We expect a stronger rate comeback for 2nd half 2021 as the oil market is not out of the Covid woods just yet and it is likely to take some more time before oil demand recovers to levels where production may be sustainably and meaningfully increased. These expectations go a long way in explaining the lack of modern tankers changing hands for which the bid/ask spread has been consistently wide. However there are now unconfirmed reports that the Libyan state-owned company GNMTC is in the process of acquiring an Aframax newbuilding resale due for delivery ex Sumitomo in early 2021. This being a tender process we expect pricing to be firm but still it is expected to reaffirm that determined buyers of brand new tankers with a very specific buying requirement have to pay up and face sellers’ asking levels.    JP Morgan continues to be an active buyer of large bulkcarriers. Following its purchase in November of two 2016 JMU built Capesizes for Usd 38.9 mill, the company is now reported to have acquired one Capesize built 2011 and one Newcastlemax built 2017. The latter is Chinese built and scrubber fitted but in our books the price of region Usd 37.5 mill is fairly neutral as far as any scrubber premium goes. Maran is reported to have acquired a sister vessel from the same stable on similar terms. All in all, dry values are moving sideways across the board.

As anticipated values in both the tanker and dry S&P markets have largely stabilised with a healthy and steady amount of ships being sold across most segments at prices falling in line with recent transactions. However a softer sentiment is certainly more evident for older tankers than for bulkers. Sales activity on the modern tanker side is negligible against a stream of modern bulk tonnage changing hands. Scorpio Bulkers continues unabated its selling spree of its modern fleet with the sale of SBI ZUMBA (81k DWT, 2016, Hudong) at Usd 20mill, which is in line with the sale of SBI Reggae (81k DWT, 2016, Hudong) last month. We also have a benchmark sale on Post-Panamax with the  sale of SANGEET ( 95k DWT, 2012, Imabari) at Usd 15.5mill to Polembros. The sale illustrates the decline in values since last done, which was SUNNY SMILE  (95k DWT, 2013, Imabari) sold at Usd 21.5mill to the same buyer back in the summer of 2019.

A sustained amount of activity across SnP markets this week with a number of vessels changing hands. In the dry markets Scorpio Bulk has disposed of a further three units. The levels achieved on all three Ultramax vessels fall in line with last comparable transactions. With a continuous stream of sales candidates meeting the current buying enquiry we expect the values to continue moving sideways for the foreseeable future.  Tanker markets continue to see a high level of interest especially across the MR and Aframax segments which have seen the vast majority of sales. An increasing number of ten to fifteen years old MR tankers are being placed for sale suggesting values are most likely to remain under pressure. The same applies to older Aframax tankers as clearly illustrated by this week’s sales, although it should be noted that the price for the two 2003 built BAKU and AZERBAIJAN reflects that the vessels have been in lay-up for some time. Younger ones are faring better with PAMISOS (105k dwt 2011 HHI) achieving the same price as the same age sister vessel KALAMI went for in early November. Sign of ongoing inspections and negotiations suggest we will be in position to report further transactions in the near future.

The creditor controlled sale of the Xihe fleet is still underway with administrators inviting offers on three VLCC’s this week. The 2013 Jiangnan built VLCC JING GANG SAN is now sold at a price of Usd 45.2mill while we understand that the two sisters HUA SAN and LU SAN  (318k DWT 2008 and 2009 SWS) are under close negotiations with price expectations in the region of Usd 30mill and Usd 33mill respectively. This downward correction in values can be witnessed across most tanker sectors which is particularly well-illustrated in the Aframax segment by the sale of the Japanese controlled LR2 unit CHAMPION PRINCE (105k dwt 2012 HHI coated) which achieved Usd 24.1mill. Only a few weeks ago same owners disposed of the the sister CHAMPION PRINCESS, also 2012 built, to GESCO for Usd 26.4mill.  Activity in the Kamsarmax segment remains high with a further two vessels changing hands this week. Namely the Japanese controlled CETUS OCEAN (83k DWT 2013 Sanoyas) sold at Usd 17.3mill and LEDA (82k DWT 2013 Tsuneishi Fukuyama) at USD 16.7mill. Worth noting that the CETUS OCEAN was sold with BWTS installed hence the mark up in pricing. Scorpio Bulk’s sell-off continues unabated with four NACKS 2015 built Ultramaxes sold to Pacific Basin. All units were scrubber fitted and the reported price of Usd 16.75mill each is therefore more or less in line with recent sales of non-scrubber fitted  comparable units.

This week has seen a flurry of transactions in the dry sale and purchase markets with vessels changing hands across all segments. The increased buying enquiry witnessed over the past weeks in the kamsarmax segment has met a flow of sales candidates with 7 units changing hands this week alone. Four of which were sold as part of Scorpios Bulks divestment programme. Off the back of this increased liquidity values remain well supported and we expect  them to remain flat as long as tonnage continues to be made available for sale.    Despite only a handful of sales to report  on the tanker front, activity remains high in the sector with a number of upcoming inspections and ongoing discussions. We expect further activity in the Aframax segment with four units inviting offers next week. This is following a number of sales which should give a clear idea of what direction values will take going forward.

Whilst 2nd values for the older VLCC tankers are still holding up relatively nicely, the other crude segments are faring worse. The sale of Suezmax BACALIAROS built 2003 SHI at Usd 15.3 mill represents a 30% drop in values since the peak in February when a same age Korean built Suezmax was sold for Usd 22 mill. Also pressure on Aframax values as seen by this week’s sales. Offers are invited mid next week for tranche 2 of the Xihe creditor controlled sale of three VLCC’s built 2008, 2009 and 2013 (all China). We understand the latter has by far received most attention from potential buyers.  Finally some positive Covid-19 news with effective vaccines being announced. However the near term challenges for both the oil and  tanker markets will remain unchanged. IEA revises down 2021 oil demand by 0.1 mbpd, stating that “vaccines are unlikely to significantly boost demand until well into next year”.  We still expect relatively sluggish rate development for the rest of this year and during most of the first half of next year. Given our more positive outlook for the second half of the 2021 and into 2022, however, this should give some interesting S&P opportunities going forward.  The dry sector remains active with the majority of transactions being in the 10-15 year bracket. Prices are however still best case moving sideways in the majority of sectors.  An increasing number of 5-10 year old Kamsarmax candidates are coming for sale from Japan which could set new benchmarks going forward.

The buying interest in VLCC tonnage remains steady and firm. Two more 2002 built are sold at prices in line with last dones. Following Hunter Groups’ recent sale of two 2019 HHI built VLCC’s at Usd 84.2 mill each, we now have another noteworthy sale. We understand TRF HORTEN built 2018 HHIC-Phil has been sold to Delta Tankers for Usd 72 mill. Adjusted for age this is some 10% down compared to the Hunter deal. The vessel is built at Hanjin’s previous Philippines facility with a retrofitted scrubber which explains part of the difference. However, in a more stable market we would expect a difference around 5% so this may arguably point to further downwards correction in values. As far as replacement cost bench-mark goes, we do not see much further downside potential in newbuilding prices from the Korean majors.  The combination of a strengthening WON vs USD and increased steel prices tells us that we are at bottom levels now. Tellingly, several VLCC contracts are in the making in Korea which may ease the pressure on the yards. With the new-found optimism in the container markets we will not be surprised also to see the Korean yards benefitting from increased ordering activity for the big sizes.   Despite the weakening freight market the dry S&P market is full of life with a large number of vessels changing hands across all sizes. There are unconfirmed reports of two 2016 JMU built scrubberfitted Capesizes being committed in the high 30’s, we expect to have more details next week.

Another busy week in both the wet and dry S&P markets. Subjects are now lifted on Hunter Group’s sale of two 2019 built VLCC’s to ADNOC. The Usd 84.2 mill agreed is in line with expectations but still a far cry from where we were at the outset of the year. The creditor controlled Xihe tanker fleet sell-off continues. Following the sale of tranche 1 vessels, inspections are now invited for additional tankers including three VLCC’s built 2008, 2009 and 2013 in China.  Any “normal” sales efforts are inevitably affected by this process and prices achieved are likely to continue being a cold shower for values across the board. Crude earnings are certainly not helping the short to medium term outlook either.  Bulker values are still very transparent and in a sideways trajectory. All sizes see a healthy transaction volume with several noteworthy sales. The Usd 25 mill reported for 2017 JMU built Kamsarmax GEMINI OCEAN is the same as SAKIZAYA JUSTICE built 2017 Namura achieved at the end of August.

No sign of any impending winter season as far as crude spot rates goes. Vintage VLCC’s continue to attract steady buying interest with another three vessels sold this week.  Price levels concluded are on par with recent transactions.  A 2011 Korean built Suezmax tanker is being offered for sale which should give good direction of where we stand on values for the semi-modern, non-eco ones.  We expect low 30’s will prove to be best case for this vessel.     Scorpio Bulkers continues its sales activity.  Five Ultramax and three Kamsarmax bulkcarriers have thus far been sold, raising over Usd 140 mill for its move into the offshore wind sector.  Values are moving sideways and this will remain the case for as long as the number of ships for sale remains high.

The Interim Judicial Managers of Xihe Holdings called for offers this week on 3 x VLCC’s (2010 & 2011) and 2 x LR2’s (2008 & 2009) all built at SWS. We understand the VLCC’s saw a hefty amount of interest and around 8 bids where placed. The jury is still out, however early reports suggest that the vessels are closed to being committed at USD 110mill en bloc. If confirmed, it represents a solid correction in values in light of the recent sale of the “TAKAOKA” (2011/Universal/300kdwt) which was sold for USD 45m last week. Albeit a discount is expected in light of the auction process, that the vessels have been idle for some time and Chinese built. Furthermore, ADS Crude sold “ADS SERENADE” (2002/Hitachi/300kdwt) to UAE based buyers for USD 25.5m, leaving the company with only one vessel left in their fleet. The sale falls in with the sistership “ADS STRATUS” they sold in September also for USD 25,5m.   In the dry sector Nissen Kaiun have sold yet another cape this week, namely the “HUGE HAKATA” (2012/Koyo/180kdwt) for USD 21m to clients of Zodiac. Moreover, Oldendorff have sold the “TILDA OLDENDORFF” (2011/STX/180kdwt) for USD 18.7m to Alpha Bulkers.   “Scorpio Bulkers” stole the headline this week by selling 4 x Ultramax’s bringing their total sell-off to excess of 100m since the company announced their move into offshore wind. Navigare is understood to have picked up the “SBI  PHOENIX” & “SBI SAMSON” (2017/Chengxi/63kdwtI) for USD 17m each, whilst the  “SBI HERA” (2016/Mitsui/60kdwt) was sold for USD 18.5m to undisclosed buyers. Lastly, the “SBI HYPERION” (2016/Nacks/61kdwt) was sold for USD 17m. Scorpios sell-off is making them the market maker in the Ultramax segment at the moment.

A number of sales to report across all sale and purchase markets with a notable pickup in activity on the tanker front.  The week began with Japanese owners inviting offers on the clean trading LR2 unit “CHAMPION PRINCESS” (Abt 105k dwt built 2012, HHI). The vessel had been inspected by up to 10 Buyers and is believed to have received up to 6 offers to finally end up in the hands of Great Eastern Shipping at a price of Usd 26.4m. The substantial buying interest can in part be explained by an extensive period of inactivity in the sector with virtually no transactions, which, coupled with a falling chartering market has lead  buyers to chase a considerable correction in asset values.  A correction that becomes particularly apparent when looking at the last comparable sale of the Aframax “NANYANG STAR” (Abt 105k dwt built 2012, Sumitomo) sold at Usd 29.8m in March this year. We expect further activity in the Aframax/LR2 sector with a number of vessels inviting offers over the coming days.  NYK has also disposed of its VLCC “TAKAOKA” (Abt 300k dwt built 2011, Universal) which was sold at Usd 45m earlier in the week. This follows the sale of “TOKITSU MARU” (Abt 300k dwt built 2011 , Mitsubishi) which was sold from the same owners at Usd 45m last week.  In the dry sector Scorpio Bulkers has sold the sisterships “SBI SOUSTA” & “SBI CONGA”(Abt 81k dwt built 2016 &2015, Hudong) for region Usd 18.5m each. This brings the tally to three vessels sold over the past two weeks and we expect the selling exercise to continue in line with the company’s strategy of shifting capital and focus to its recently announced offshore & renewable venture.

In what we understand was a deal concluded a couple of months ago, Dynacom is reported to have purchased a nine year old Japanese owned/built VLCC for Usd 45 mill. This is as such the second VLCC of this age sold at more or less same levels so we can safely conclude that values have taken another tumble. Values for vintage VLCC are moving sideways with SEAWAYS MULAN built 2002 reported gone at levels in line with last week’s sale of PANTARISTE, also built 2002. We see more and more vintage available for sale with further deals expected to materialize soon. As expected, more tanker newbuilding contracts are coming to light with Atlas Maritime this week reported to have signed for two Aframax tankers at Daehan for mid Usd 40 mill. Additional Suezmax and VLCC contracts are also being done at levels in line with expectations. This, together with dismal spot rates are certainly not lending support to any positive development for crude values. Following inspections by around 10 buyers, offers are invited on Monday for LR2 tanker CHAMPION PRINCESS built 2012 which, together with the Xihe tanker sell-off, will be the ones to watch in the near future.   The increased activity out of Brazil has seen Capesize earnings skyrocketing, the BCI has more than doubled in under 3 weeks. This marks another dramatic market move in a year that has been the most volatile ever for Capes. In general, we find fundamentals to be more than sound and expect it to be so for another year and a half at least. For the smaller segments things are also moving in the right direction, albeit slower. We see demand coming back by varying degrees in all major discharge regions (Europe, Japan, Korea, India, South East Asia), whereas China remains strong notwithstanding the last month and a half’s slowdown. Fresh YTD spot market highs for Supramax are highly likely during Q4, but we are less certain of that for Kamsarmax. Vessel deliveries will fall markedly the next year and a half which, coupled with a continued economic recovery and massive stimulus measures, could make for very interesting times ahead. The renewed dry optimism is evident in the very significant number of second-hand transactions every week. Values are at a robust floor and from here any movement should be north.

Newbuilding contracting is becoming an increasingly attractive option spurred by much reduced yard prices. NAT this week announced contracts for two Suezmax newbuildings at Samsung at a price believed to be in the mid 50’s. The last time NAT placed Suezmax contracts at Samsung was in October 2016 at more or less same price.  Post-Lehman these represents to date the low-points in Suezmax prices from the Korean majors. Logic dictates that Chinese prices for such tankers should now be close to Usd 50 mill. We will not be surprised to see additional tanker orders coming to light in the near to medium term. In the present earnings climate, values for modern tankers are inevitably bench-marked to replacement cost and as such we have YTD a significant drop in values. A prompt resale Suezmax tanker from Korea was for instance at the outset of the year valued at region Usd 68 mill. No longer. Rumours abound all week related to the sale of a 2011 built VLCC, it appears to be Minerva’s PANTANASSA built 2011 HHI. The reported price of Usd 46 mill reaffirms softening prices.    Transactions of modern bulkcarriers have been few and far between so the sale of Tess-82 (Zosen) PRECIOUS SKY built 2015 with SS passed and BWTS installed is at Usd 22 mill a notable benchmark. Capesizes extended the earnings gains yesterday with rates gaining 23% to USD 22.8k/d. This should bode well for more action in the Capesize S&P market as well.

Another week with no sale and purchase activity on modern tanker tonnage. Market players are too far apart, with buyers looking to do a good deal in the current subdued market and sellers holding on to their price ideas with the crazy ride the last 12 months fresh in mind. Owners of vintage units with SS/DD coming up is however easier to convince and the sale of KRITI SPIRIT (160kdwt/2000/DSME) and KRITI SFAKIA (160kdwt/2000/HHI) at region usd 14.5 mill each display that values have found a temporary floor in line with last done SONANGOL KIZOMBA (160kdwt/2001/DSME) at usd 16.5 mill one month ago.   Continued high snp activity on dry, but still primarily on older units. New sales candidates more than offset vessels being sold, especially on Supramaxes/Ultramaxes, which is putting a lid on values and could potentially result in values sliding should the expected uptick in rates in the 4th quarter not materialize.

There is increased talks of floating storage again as crude oil prices fell region 10% this week, primarily at the front-end of the curve. This combined with Trafigura taking in 14 VLs for region 6 months TC, the last 1-2 weeks has created positive momentum and lifted rates from opex levels to Usd 20,000-25,000/day. The sale of ADS STRATUS (300,000DWT, Hitachi 2002) at Usd 25.5 mill demonstrates that market players still are able to find some middle ground in what has been a widening bid/ask spread on vintage VLs.   There is a flurry of deals being done in dry, but with a steady flow of vessels coming for sale we have not seen bidding rounds taking off. Buyers are selective and not easily carried away, albeit many in numbers. We continue to see action in the Kamsarmax segment - a notch down on price from last week when corrected for DD position and scrubber - with IKAN BAWAL (83,500DWT, Sanoyas 2012) and KEY CALLA (83,500DWT Sanoyas, 2010) sold at Usd 16 mill and Usd 12.75 mill, respectively.

While a few owners have been able to lock away VLCC’s for six months at rates in the low to mid 30s the spot market is at opex levels presently. It is really just a numbers game at this point, with about one of three MEG cargoes lost over the three last month’s vs same period last year.  Sale of modern conventional tankers is just not happening and the bid/ask spread is getting quite wide.  The dry story is much easier to read with a good transparency on values throughout.  Attractive vessels/designs are showing some gain as seen by the sale of Tess-82 LOWLANDS KAMSAR built 2010 at slightly above Usd 15 mill. Offers were invited on Wednesday and a sale was quickly concluded.  Expectations were that the price should end up somewhere between Usd 14-14.5 mill so we can safely concluded that this was a notch up.  The vessel has just passed the second Special Survey with BWTS fitted.

Another week that has seen a flurry of activity across all segment of the Dry Cargo markets with close to 20 sales reported this week. In terms of values we continue to see an increasing number of more modern units being traded, setting consolidated benchmarks for assets of all vintage. Notable transaction in the Ultramax sector being the sale of the 2019 Oshima built Ultramax "ADVENTURE III" which was sold to clients of Meghna shipping at Usd 24.25 mill setting a clear picture for modern Japanese designs. Similarly in the Kamsarmax market we have more clarity on the modern Japanese front following the sale of the 2017 Namura built “SAKUZAYA JUSTICE” sold at Usd 25 mill. Generally although buying interest remains high, the steady stream of sale candidates is diluting competition giving buyers enough options to keep values relatively flat.   Not much to report in the tanker sector except for the 2000 HHI built VLCC “BAG MEUR”, which we understand has been committed at region Usd 21.2 mill which is another confirmation of the erosion in values for vintage tankers. The same age "MARINA M" also HHI built, was in comparison sold for Usd 32 mill about 2 months ago, albeit with SS passed.

The recovery in the dry markets is still feeble but at least we continue to have a decent S&P volume. Last week we reported the sale of a Kamsarmax newbuilding with prompt delivery ex Oshima at Usd 30.5 mill, we now understand that this transaction has failed to materialize. Two Capesize sales are certainly on the low side – nine year old PACIFIC ENDURANCE BUILT Koyo at Usd 18 mill is well below expectations, the vessel was initially reported to be withdrawn but subsequently understood to be sold after all. Furthermore, the price for 2013 Koyo built JUBILANT EXCELLENCE gives no encouragement for an uptick in values in the near term.  It comes as no surprise that values for vintage crude tankers continue to soften, however various reports that Suezmax SONANGOL KIZOMBA built 2001 is sold in the mid Usd 12 mill is incorrect and we understand the deal was done in the mid Usd 16 mill to Dubai based buyers.

A resurgence of the coronavirus in parts of the world with associated lockdowns re-imposed is like cancer for the world economy and inevitably shipping. Whilst we continue to see a steady flow of bulkcarriers changing hands, the 2nd hand market has failed to fully ignite and caution is prevailing. That being said, dry values are well supported and both buyers and sellers should have enough transparency to transact in light of the above mentioned liquidity.  The crude tanker S&P market is more in a limbo. The brand new ships are inevitably being revalued in line with falling replacement costs and earnings are far from lending support to any significant activity nor premium above assumed replacement cost. The result is zero sales volume of very modern ships. The vintage crude tankers have a double whammy – low earnings/storage play gone and recently also much reduced demolition prices. Values are clearly adjusting downwards. Two 2001 built suezmax tankers are in play with deals expected to be concluded in the mid-teens. That leaves the semi-modern, non eco ships built say from 2008 to 2012 which is where we expect to see increased sales activity going forward. As always, it’s “just” a question of price but buyers will hold the upper hand.

The sale of fifteen year old VLCC “OTOWASAN” at Usd 26.25 mill is a reality check for vintage tankers. To compare apples with apples it should be noted that the vessel will be delivered with her third special survey due, but it’s still a far cry from the Usd 38.1 mill which Euronav achieved in April for the same age TI HELLAS with survey just passed. In a “Korea Inc” deal SK Shipping has acquired 5 brand new VLCC’s from a Korean fund with 10 year charters attached to domestic oil major GS Caltex. Suezmax “ADVANTAGE SKY” built 2010 Rongsheng was sold yesterday by online auction for Usd 25.5 mill. The vessel has been under arrest in Durban since August 2018; at the first auction in April 2020 the highest bid was Usd 18.8 mill. Crude values are softening across the board, clean values are best case moving sideways.  Euronav as always first off the block in the reporting season, its VLCC fleet averaged a stellar Usd 81500 pd in Q2 and its suezmax fleet Usd 60,000 pd.    Modern bulker sales have been few and far between YTD but this week sees the sale of two 2017 Japanese built Kamsarmax bulkcarriers at Usd 26 mill.  This underlines a firming of values – in June a 2020 Japanese newbuilding resale achieved Usd 28.5 mill.

Another week that has seen a flurry of activity in the dry markets with numerous vessels changing hands and an increasing number of modern quality tonnage being made available for sale. The Capesize segment seems to gradually be following suit with some owners deciding to take advantage of the buying momentum witnessed in the smaller sectors by putting a couple of units onto the market. Namely the Japanese controlled “PACIFIC ENDURANCE” (2011/Koyo/180kdwt) and the sistership “JUBILANT EXCELLENCE” (2013/Koyo/180kdwt) –  both owners are inviting inspections on their respective units and understand that 5 buyers are lined up to get onboard the 2011 built unit while the “JUBILANT EXCELLENCE”  will be made available for inspection while in DD in China beginning of August. Elsewhere the 5 year old Ultramax  “ALAM MULIA” (2015/Iwagi/61kdwt) has been sold by Malaysian owners at Usd 18.8m. This sets a much needed benchmark for modern Japanese built Ultramax considering that the last sale dates back to February this year. The levels achieved are more or less in line with recent sales in the sector reaffirming the premium that Japanese built condone against their Chinese and Korean counterpart, even with Japanese design in China. This becomes particularly apparent when compared the sale of the” DEVONGATE” (2014/Dacks/61kdwt) which achieved Usd 16m earlier this month.  In the tanker markets second-hand activity remains very much subdued across all sectors with very few sales to report. A striking lack of activity on the modern front has lead a number of buyers to  explore the Newbuilding route where shipyards are striving to become competitive against a stagnant and much less flexible second hand value environment. As such there are signs of a number of ongoing discussions taking place across China and Korea for orders ranging from MRs up to VLCCs.

We have a strong start to the second half of the year for all dry segments and the bottom for period rates and asset values have likely passed for all segments and vintages. We now have a robust floor on values and the dry S&P activity is increasingly on fire. Kamsarmax and Supra-/Ultramax aged eight to twelve years are in particular demand. Following inspections by nine buyers, the Japanese controlled Kamsarmax KM YOKOHOMA built 2011 Sanoyas was promptly sold at region USD 15m, levels which fall in line with expectations. BW Dry’s recent deal on subjects for the sale of its three ten year old; Japanese built Kamsarmax BW ACORN, BW BARLEY and BW EINKORN failed to materialize, and they were instead quickly sold to new buyers this week. We understand Centrofin is the buyer of the latter two and Orion the buyer of BW ACORN. This vessel was in fact contracted as newbuilding by Orion and sold to BW Dry in 2018.   Any movement in dry values will be north in the near to medium term and we shall soon be seeing more modern tonnage being offered for sale.   It is time-out in the tanker S&P market. Values remain under pressure and there is no sense of urgency to acquire assets unless a particularly attractive deal comes along.

As expected the increased level of buying enquiry in the dry sector has resulted in a notable pick up in activity with a number of inspections and negotiations taking place this week. Japanese owners invited inspection of the 2011 Sanoyas built Kamsarmax “KM YOKOHAMA” and up to 9 buyers are now outright with offers invited next week. This firm interest has inevitably driven additional sellers onto the market with new Kamsarmax units being placed for sale. We expect this increased competition to drive values upward and also activity to continue to spill over into other segments including the Supra-/Ultramax segment where we have seen 5 units change hands this week and a number of firm discussions are taking place. Although most reported sales are of more vintage units, this increased liquidity has provided extra support to values enabling potential sellers of more modern units to engage with renewed confidence.  The tanker sector remains subdued and unless sellers reduce their ideas substantially, we do not see much appetite to secure tonnage in the current market environment.

Another week that has seen a flurry of transactions in the dry snp markets with a number of vessels changing hands across all sectors. In the Capesize segment the Japanese controlled “GRACEFUL MADONNA” (2010 Koyo 180kdwt) has been sold to clients of Eastern Pacific at Usd 20.7m with DD passed and BWTS installed. The deal is setting a well needed benchmark for Japanese built Cape units of this vintage considering that the last comparable sale dates back to February. Elsewhere the majority of units being sold remain of early to mid-2000 built tonnage with the Handysize sector seeing increased activity on the more modern side of the spectrum.  On the tanker side activity remains subdued to say the least with only two sales to report.

Dry markets continue to see the vast majority of sale and purchase activity with 8 sales to report this week. The panamax market have seen three 2005 built vessels change hands setting clear direction for 15 year old units, while the smaller segments have seen increased liquidity for more modern tonnage. Although new benchmarks have been set, consensus among most market players is that values are at or have passed the bottom and we should start seeing sellers showing a little more resistance by revising their expectations upwards. That being said, determined sellers now face a more receptive audience allowing an exit at numbers which was not realistic short time ago. Interesting times ahead in this sector.  Tankers are certainly not the flavor of the month and we are moving into uncertain territory for values with no transactions taking place.

The dry S&P activity continues to pick up with a large number of vessels reported sold. Whilst older units still account for majority of sales we now have an interesting bench-mark set by the sale of the Japanese controlled Oshima Kamsarmax resale which was sold to Greek interests at $ 29m. Furthermore three 2010 Japan built Kamsarmaxes are also reported to be committed on subjects at region Usd 40 mill en-bloc. The buying momentum now shaping up leads us to conclude that the downside risk on values is limited. Buyers hoping for a re-run of 2016 values will wait in vain.  Tanker values are sliding and vintage vessels remain most at risk.

This week continues to see most sale and purchase activity take place in the dry market where a number of vessels have changed hands. This increased liquidity in the sector has enabled the relative downward correction that most market players expected in light of the global disruption. However the consensus seem to be that we are near the bottom in terms of values with a relatively positive market expectation for the quarters to come. Saying that values are on average down between 15 to 20% since pre-covid transactions therefore still representing an attractive play from a buying perspective. We expect to see more deals take place in the coming weeks which should provide a clear indication as to what direction this SnP market will take.   No change in the tanker market where we witness very little activity with the few exceptions on the overaged front with sellers willing to transact. Past sellers of more modern units have now most definitely taken a step back unwilling to entertain discussions at today’s levels.

The sense of urgency to buy tankers is waning and values are slowly correcting downwards. Two 2000 built VLCC’s have been sold for region Usd 24 mill each which is Usd 6 mill lower than the recent peak at Usd 30 mill for the same age LUCKY TRADER concluded at the end of April. However it should be noted that LUCKY TRADER had her Special Survey passed and gave prompt delivery. Values for vintage tankers will be most exposed going forward but across the board we see the bid/ask spread widening in line with falling newbuilding prices and expectations. Judging by history we are likely to enter a period of limited sales activity with a wait-and-see attitude prevailing.  For bulkers we see a clear buying momentum building up and we may indeed be getting closer to a more robust floor on values which should trigger increased S&P activity. Sales volume YTD has been dominated by 10 year olds and older which is where we expect such a floor first to be established.  The more modern ones should then follow suit, perhaps with another 10-15% correction downwards.

A pickup in activity this week, with a number of countries around the world returning to some form of relative normality. In the tanker space, the majority of vessels changing hands remain those of older vintage, whereas mentioned last week sellers are more lenient and willing to go meet buyers at levels below the last done that were set over the past stronger weeks. On the more modern side of the spectrum, the stand-off remains with the few remaining potential sellers still holding off for levels set at the peak of the aforementioned market.   As expected, following the recent increase of Buying enquiries, the dry SnP markets are seeing a number of transactions taking place with new benchmarks being set. A number of potential sellers have now got clearer visibility on the potential bids and are willing to test the market by making candidates available for inspections.  Although the panamax and post-panamax segments have seen a couple of units being sold this week there still is a notable lack of activity in the capesize market rendering it difficult to assess where pricing currently lies. This price dislocation being particularly well illustrated by the Taiwanese controlled MV “NEW STAGE” (176,877 dwt built 2008 Namura) which was withdrawn after seeing a top offer of Usd 14m against sellers expectation of Usd 16m.

Tanker sale and purchase activity remains subdued with most players now having taken a step back from potential acquisitions in light of weaker charter markets. Owners of modern tonnage are still hopeful in achieving yesterdays benchmark rendering the bid offer spread hard to bridge, we do however see sellers of more vintage units gradually correcting their expectations in order to dispose of their older vessels in what can still be considered a relatively strong exit environment.  With an increased level of buying enquiry for dry tonnage it comes to no surprise that most transactions this week are found in the Dry SnP Markets. This pick up in liquidity is driven by the Supramax sector where four units have changed hands this week at levels that clearly reaffirm the current downward trend in values. The lack of sales of medium/large sized units is in no case reflective of the current appetite that potential buyers have for Kamsarmax and Capes, however we have yet to see enough candidates made available for sale. We do however expect to see a pick up in activity in those larger segments once momentum picks up and sellers decide to go meet these renewed bids.

Momentum in the tanker markets seems to have taken a downturn this week with most players digesting weeks of high rate volatility which was mainly driven by a now fading storage play. As a result there are no new sales to report this week but quite to the contrary we are seeing a number of older transactions fall apart in light of the weaker charter markets. Notably a number of owners who had managed to take advantage of the buying appetite for vintage crude tonnage are seeing their buying counterparts unable to execute.   Buying enquiry seems to therefore gradually shift to the Dry SnP markets where the everlasting pressure on charter rates is taking its toll on values. A number of sales this week have indeed seen a relative value correction with an increased amount of sellers deciding to trigger at today's market rather than face the uncertain outlook currently shared by most market players.

Thenamaris is reported to have acquired on NSF terms a VLCC newbuilding from Sinokor with delivery ex DSME in September 2020 for region usd 93.5 mill which is spot-on what Euronav paid for sister newbuildings also from Sinokor in early March.  This is still a far cry from the Usd 106 mill paid for prompt delivery VLCC newbuilding, also from DSME, in January and confirms that recent spot earnings and values for brand new ships are decoupled.  The answer is that no one believes the recent massive earnings spike is sustainable and we have indeed this week seen crude spot rates falling off. CM Lemos has booked two newbuilding Suezmax tankers at HHI for usd 59 mill each without scrubber, and as the year develops we will continue to see competitive pricing from Korean and Chinese yards.   Dry values are dropping. The sale of Supramax ROYAL EPIC built 2008 Mitsui at Usd 7.8 mill is a telling example, but mind you we are still about 20% off what was done at the recent bottom in 2016. We have yet to see any tangible modern reference sales, but buyers are increasingly getting ready to move for bulkers.  We understand the sale of Kamsarmax CERBA built 2010 STX at usd 13 mill has failed on Sellers’ subjects.

A busy week in the tanker S&P markets with a continued string of older tankers changing hands.  We are reporting three older VLCC’s sold at storage induced prices, however we understand the sale of GRAND LADY was concluded some time ago. A large number of older Aframax and MR tankers are for sale, but transactions taking place underpin that values for same are not seeing any gain and are best case moving sideways. Not since Euronav’s acquisition of VLCC newbuilding resales at Usd 93.5 mill in early March have we seen any modern/brand new tankers being transacted.   Talk of the week has been the massive surge in the share price for NAT aka “the come-back kid”. Following an airing on CNBC a week ago by its CEO Herbjørn Hansson, a massive 110 million shares were traded on Tuesday worth about Usd 807 mill.  Its market cap broke the Usd 1 bn mark but is now at Usd 880 mill.   The dry S&P market is still kind of alive, albeit we have yet to see any noteworthy modern units being sold. Chinese Dolphin 57 Supramaxes see prices drop; AMAZONIT DOLPHIN 57k built 2011 Hantong invited offers earlier this week with best bid at low Usd 7 mill. This is in line with the sale of CONTI PERIDOT built 2011 Taizhou which this week achieved low Usd 7 mill in a bank controlled sale.

Another week for the history books in the crude and clean markets with latter now also on fire with spot rates hitting all-time high levels.  The S&P activity is mostly unaffected, except for older VLCC's which remain hot commodity.  Four such vessels are sold this week alone of which two 2005 built at a reported Usd 38 mill each.  This is approximately Usd 5 mill more that same age YUGAWASAN fetched only three weeks ago.    The price for the LR1 tanker ETERNAL DILIGENCE built 2006 Onomichi is surprisingly low, but we expect it’s a function of few buyers having been able to inspect the vessel.

Cheap oil all around with storage play still providing impetus to buying interest for older VLCC’s in particular.  It’s all about presenting candidates at one of the very few places where inspection can be conducted and with prompt delivery on offer.  Tellingly, a 1998 built VLCC is understood to be working firm at region Usd 25 mill basis prompt delivery Singapore. The 2005 built VLCC TAKASAKI was inspected in Singapore by six buyers this week with a sale expected to be concluded in a week’s time.  There are unconfirmed reports that Middle Eastern buyers are in the process of  acquiring the three VLCC’s RENE built 2005 Imabari, MAERA built 2002 Mitsui and KELLY built 2000 Mitsui but we await further details.    Euronav announced the sale of its 2001 built Suezmax CAP DIAMANT at Usd 20.8 mill.  The deal was concluded some time back and the vessel has already been delivered to its new owner.  There are a large number of Aframax tankers for sale built early-to-late 2000 however sales activity has failed to ignite this time around.  The bid/ask spread has proved difficult to bridge with potential sellers opting to ride the wave while it lasts.  Tangible bulker deals remain few and far between but the sale of handysize IKAN LANDUK built 2013 Onomichi is a rare exception.  The price reported is very much in line with our value estimates.

As evidenced by the flurry of period fixtures being reported across the board, the strong rates in the tanker markets see owners striving to lock in  tonnage on lucrative long term charters.  Activity in the S&P markets remain subdued to say the least.  Buying interest remains in principle high for older crude carriers able to offer prompt inspection and delivery, however the hurdles very much persist for any sale discussion to take off.  In terms of concluded business, following inspections by up-to eight buyers only last week the 2005 built VLCC YUGAWASAN has now been sold to Greek buyers at USD 33.3m. The vessel is SS due in August and price achieved was more or less in line with expectations.  We expect to see more activity in the sector with another Japanese controlled 2005 built unit being placed for sale this week.  Owners are inviting inspections in Singapore mid April where a similarly large number of prospective buyers is expected to inspect.  However it remains to be seen how the new raft of restrictive measures announced in Singapore today will impact inspections and whether all necessary arrangements can be taken at this vital port.  A steady trickle of bulker transactions are still being done, however until we see tangible deals for larger and more modern vessels the jury is still very much out as to where values are heading.

Tanker owners continue to enjoy the ride.  Floating storage is presently the name of the game and our tanker analysts estimate fifteen to twenty VLCC's have been taken up for storage up until now.  The 2005 built VLCC YUGAWASAN was inspected this week in Singapore and upto eight prospective buyers went on-board with a sale expected soon. The three Chinese controlled VLCC's NEW CREATION built 2009 Dalian, NEW TALISMAN built 2009 Bohai and NEW CORAL built 2010 Jiangnan are reported committed on subjects at Usd 43 mill each but we await further details.  The sale of 2012 Japanese built Aframax NANYANG STAR is a bit of a cold shower for values.  After a previous deal failed to be confirmed, reports suggest the vessel has now been sold below Usd 30 mill.  Dry sales are thin on the ground and we have yet to see new benchmarks for capesize with the rumoured failure of GREAT NAVIGATOR built 2006 Universal which had been reported sold to Greece for region Usd 14 mill. Capesize NEW STAGE built 2008 Namura is reported to have been inspected by five parties this week of which four Greek and one Chinese. Buyers and Sellers are generally out of sync on pricing, but we are slowly seeing opportunistic buyers appear who are ready to take advantage of the current market downturn.

With oil prices selling off further the forward curve has steepened; making floating storage plays more attractive.  Sellers of older VLCC’s able to give prompt delivery has now another window of opportunity to exit at strong levels.  AET is for instance reported to have achieved region/excess Usd 30 mill for its 2003 Japanese built BUNGA KASTURI.    Some smaller cap deals are in the making particularly in the clean sector but overall the S&P activity is very muted.  The same goes for anything dry except for a small trickle of handy- and supramaxes still changing hands.  Dry bulk equities had another awful week with most listed names now down more than 50 per cent y-t-d.  The escalating Covid-19 pandemic makes it increasingly difficult to transact S&P with anything resembling normality.  Pre-purchase inspections, crew changes and most legal aspects of a financial closing are severely disrupted.

VLCC spot rates have reached unprecedented high levels with Suezmax and Aframax following suit.  How this will impact S&P activity is hard to predict as the COVID-19 pandemic escalates, but short term we should see renewed chase for older tankers able to give prompt delivery.   Several buyers are for instance next week inspecting the Japanese controlled VLCC YUGAWASAN built 2005 Mitsubishi which is expected to be sold soon thereafter.  Reports that the 2000 built Suezmax MOGRA is sold at Usd 17 mill certainly lend support to a robust floor for the older units.  Otherwise it’s all doom and gloom.  With the world’s fourth largest COVID-19 infection rate per capita, the Norwegian government yesterday imposed the most wide-reaching restrictions ever in peace time.  Equity markets are bracing for a severe meltdown, and in the coming weeks and month’s sentiment and macro backdrops will continue to weigh on the shipping sectors.

Euronav making another counter-cyclical move for a fourth newbuilding VLCC resale with delivery in Q1 2021.  This is an exact sister to the three newbuilding resales it recently acquired, and with the Covid-19 outbreak now edging closer to a global pandemic, such later delivery may prove to be an advantage.  The jury is still out as to how values for older crude tankers will develop but the sense of urgency to buy early-to-mid 2000 built units is temporarily gone.  Whilst there are still buyers around we see a downside risk for values.   For product tankers, values are mostly holding up and we will continue to see a steady flow of transactions.  Sellers of larger dry sizes are opting to take a step back amidst the prevailing wide bid/ask spread.  Ultra-/supramax and handysize values are more balanced with ditto higher transaction volume.

Plenty of sales to report in the dry sectors with Oman Shipping making a swoop for three modern Ultramaxes.  Another active buyer of Ultramax is Meghna Group of Bangladesh which proved an astute buyer also during the last down-turn in 2016.  Values for this segment seem to have found a decent floor for transactions whilst the bigger sizes are certainly more in limbo.  Tellingly, Kamsarmax BRIGHT PEGASUS built 2013 Zhoushan has failed to attract serious interest and sellers' price ideas of low to mid 20's (with scrubber retrofit prior delivery) seem far fetched at the moment.  With non-scrubber fitted capesize earning close to zero it comes as no surprise that tangible deals are few and far between.  We can but only hope for a rebound in markets come March/April.  Slow steaming, anchored vessels, scrubber retrofit delays, vessel delivery delays, high scrapping, Vale iron ore shipments rebound, and pent-up China demand could hopefully create a “squeeze” like last year but as we speak it's all down to how the virus outbreak plays out.

Following days of speculations we understand that the Japanese controlled Aframax NANYANG STAR 105k dwt built 2012 Sumitomo has been committed at a price of Usd 33m. Although the sector has seen a healthy number of transactions since Q4 last year, most candidates changing hands have been on the older end of the spectrum. The levels achieved fall in line with market expectations in this uncertain market environment where bids are limited and where most sellers are holding on to their price ideas in view of the widely expected market recovery. In the product sector the Japanese controlled pumproom MR EAGLE MELBOURNE built 2011 Onomichi has invited offers this week and we understand firm negotiations are underway in the region of Usd 18.5m.   A number of transactions to report on the dry sector with a pick up in activity on the Handysize and Panamax  segments, with four reported sales in each sector. The consensus among market players seems to be bullish for the upcoming quarters leading to an increased buying enquiry with buyers looking to position themselves by taking advantage of the subdued freight markets in order to secure levels below last done.

Deal of the year to date being Euronav’s purchase of three scrubber fitted VLCC newbuildings from Sinokor with delivery ex DSME at the end of 2020 and early 2021.  The average price of Usd 93.5 mill each is a far cry from the Usd 106 mill recently paid for a sister VLCC newbuilding with very prompt delivery.  Latter deal was of course spurred by the very high spot earnings at the time.  The Usd 93.5 mill is more or less equal to assumed delivered cost for a similar newbuilding contract being placed today, albeit with a year’s later delivery in such case.  Whilst we doubt there are other sellers willing to exit at these numbers the Euronav transaction is a cold shower for values.  The sense of urgency to pay up for crude tankers with prompt delivery is waning and no one knows how long  the Corona virus will continue to affect world trade.  We are indeed in uncharted territory.    The dry market remains challenging and many offers in hand fail to meet the sellers’ price expectations. Following inspections by close to ten parties, the Tess-82 MAGNOLIA built 2011 had offers this week and we understand the highest was at region usd 16 mill versus the sellers’ price ideas of Usd 18 mill.  The good news is that recycling activity is picking up with three Capesize and one Newcastlemax  sold this week for about Usd 390-400 pldt.

Shipping markets continue to feel the impact of the corona virus crisis with uncertainty as to how long China will take to return to normal trading activities. The country's coal consumption of major coastal power groups has fallen to a record low as industrial activity is heavily disrupted by various shutdowns taking place.  We are in uncharted territory as the outbreak develops and sellers face an uneven playing field with some recently reported deals failing to materialize; the 2011 DSME built Kamsarmax SUNNY YOUNG is for instance again for sale and a number of transactions being stalled.  However the underlying dry demand is strong and many buyers are positioning themselves for potential future acquisitions in hope to land the right deal.  Several inspections are taking place in the tanker sector, albeit with few tangible deals to report except for older tonnage which continues to attract buyers in line with recently concluded levels.

The combination of coronavirus, weak refinery margins and talks of the US releasing the Cosco vessels (25-30 VLCCs) has proved a toxic mix for the tanker markets and the jury is still out as to possible effect on asset values.  We should soon see whether the positive buying sentiment experienced over the past few weeks will subdue as a result.  SFL Corp managed to achieve a firm price for its 2002 built VLCC FRONT HAKATA at slightly excess Usd 34 mill.  The 2012 Sumitomo built Aframax NANYANG STAR received offers this week after being inspected by 4 parties. However levels remain unclear at this stage and we expect to get more clarity early next week which should give a clear indication on the course values will take going forward.  With this week  ending on the lowest BCI on record it is no surprise that dry values are unquestionably under pressure. As a result buying appetite is on the rise trying to find willing sellers at these revised levels while some sellers are resisting by choosing to withdraw rather than follow this downward trend. Saying that, we do expect new benchmarks to be set across segments.  In the capesize sector all eyes are on the Japanese controlled MINERAL HOKKAIDO built 2008 Imabari which has been marketed for sale earlier in in the week with imminent inspections. Meanwhile on the Supramax front  new benchmarks have been set with the sale  of the TRITON VALK built 2009 Mitsui (no BWTS) at low Usd 11 mill.

The limited number of reported transactions this week  is not necessarily reflective of the level of buying enquiry witnessed in the tanker SnP markets. Particularly on the modern front, where the markets found some renewed momentum off the back of  the recent sales both in the Aframax sector with the AQUAFREEDOM built 10/2019  changing hands at region Usd 55.8 mill, and in the VLCC space where the Hartree scrubber-fitted VLCC resale fetched Usd 106 mill earlier this month.  These benchmarks have given some additional confidence to a number of potential sellers encouraging them to entertain buying interest on their units. Sentiment also remains strong for older vintage crude carriers with 4 early 2000 built suezmax tankers being sold over the past 2 weeks. Values in the sector have clearly found an equilibrium and we expect further transactions in the near future.  The challenging freight environment in the dry cargo sectors has pushed sellers to revise their price expectations leading to an increased amount of buying enquiry.  Same is particularly well illustrated by the number of inspections taking place across the board.  Japanese owners invited inspections this week on the 2011 built Tess-82 MAGNOLIA, and we understand that up to 10 parties are now outright.  Deals concluded confirm the falling trend as seen by the sale of 2011 DSME built Kamsarmax SUNNY YOUNG at mid to high Usd 15 mill.

We finally have a reference sale for brand new scrubber fitted aframax tanker.  Minerva is reported to be paying region usd 55.5 mill for AQUAFREEDOM - delivered from Samsung in September 2019. This is in line with our value estimates. Rumours abound about another 2019 built VLCC being sold for region usd 107 mill but details are still sketchy. Several early 2000 built suezmaxes are in play in the usd 19-22 mill range and we expect to soon report more such sales.  Dry values are under pressure. There are many buyers waiting to strike but consensus seems to be that values have yet to reach its floor in the near to medium term. Tellingly, negotiations for the 2010 Japan built capesize CAPE AGNES was aborted as the sellers’ price idea of usd 22 mill was not met.  We understand the best bid came at region usd 19.5 mill.

The amazing earnings have ignited the tanker S&P market with particularly modern, scrubber fitted crude tankers hot commodity.   It comes as no surprise that sellers’ price ideas for modern/brand new tankers are finally being met.  Deal of the week being Hartree’s sale of a scrubber-fitted VLCC newbuilding with delivery ex DSME in January for usd 106 mill.  The buyer is reported to be a new joint venture between George Economou, Idan Ofer and the Norwegian investor Øystein Stray Spetalen.  One more VLCC resale is also rumoured sold by Hartree to Korean buyers at same level. The price is about 8% up on last done which was Hunter’s sale of a sister newbuilding to Korean buyers at usd 98 mill in June 2019. The last time VLCC’s were sold at similar levels was in 2014 when Gener8 acquired 4 newbuilding contracts from Scorpio at usd 105 mill each, albeit with delivery in 2016.  More deals for very modern, scrubber fitted tankers are in the making.  The dry case remains challenging and values are coming off.  Increased sales activity for supra- and panamax at lower levels with prices arguably down by usd 1-1.5 mill since December.   For capesize the present bid/ask spread is hampering sales activity.  CAPE AGNES 180k built 2010 Koyo is, for example, reported to have seen region usd 20 mill but sellers have yet to bite the bullet.

The tanker S&P market is pretty subdued but our read is that many buyers are on standby with a strong level of enquiries waiting to strike in the new year.  Whilst brand new ships are fully priced, we see continued upside on values for the semi-modern tonnage across the board.   The dry case has lost steam with cape earnings taking a beating. Next year will start with a large number of kamarsarmax newbuildings hitting the water and as such it’s fair to expect a challenging quarter in sight. Relevant transactions are few and we end the year with a steady and large overhang of ships for sale.  Any movement in dry values in the near future will be down.  The scrubber case is looking very promising as 2020 approaches with the compliant fuel spread now in excess of usd 300/ton.

Despite sustained period of healthy earnings in the tanker chartering markets, it seems the upcoming seasonal holidays are gradually slowing down potential S&P interests. The firm spot markets continue to support Sellers quest for premiums over last dones in order to conclude any potential sales. Saying that, a couple of Buyers are willing to go and meet sellers expectations in order to secure prompt spot tonnage, particularly on the region 10 year and older vintages. This is well illustrated by the sale of the Zodiac controlled JUPITER SUN (ABT 115K DWT SASEBO 2007) which was sold at USD 28.7m. This is the second vessel sold by Zodiac to this buyer, worth noting that the Jupiter Sun is scrubber-fitted hence the premium against the same age sistership Virgo Sun which was sold last month. Regardless both levels represent a significant  jump from last concluded transactions.  With signs of ongoing negotiations for tanker units of similar age we expect a number of Buyers to take positions before year end. The majority of eyes are now however, focused on 2020, patiently waiting to assess the actual impact that the new regulatory constrains will have on the markets.    New revised benchmarks are being set in the Dry SnP markets with three deals being done across segments. The Capesize GOTIA (ABT 178K DWT SHANGHAI WAIGAOQIAO 2012) was sold at Usd 23m, the Kamsarmax MENARO (ABT 81K DWT JIANGSU JINLING 2016) achieved Usd 22.75m while the Dolphin 57’ design Supramax BAOJI (ABT 56K DWT XIAMEN 2013 C4x36 T) was sold at Usd 11.6m. These levels illustrate particularly well the subdued sentiment we have been witnessing from potential Bulker Buyers which, as indicated by the abovementioned sales, has driven values down by 5 to 10% since the summer.  This negative trend can also be demonstrated by the lack of Japanese built vessels changing hands with Sellers preferring to withdraw their units rather than following this downward direction.

The tanker S&P market remains somewhat subdued in terms of completed transactions despite signs of  a number of buying enquiries.  Main reasons being a resilient bid offer spread  with the bellwethers having already placed their cards and others are now preferring to see how the beginning of 2020 plays out.  In what looks to be good timing, Advantage Tankers is reported to have acquired two 2009 Chinese built VLCC’s for usd 38 mill each.  We understand this is a deal done some time back which explains the low price, even allowing for Chinese built discount.  Teekay starting to clear out its older suezmaxes with the 2003 HHI built ISKMATI SPIRIT gone for usd 19.3 mill.  This follows Teekay’s recent sale of same age ASKHINI SPIRIT to Chemnav at same level.  The LR1 GULF CASTLE built 2009 HMD is in play with offer reportedly seen in excess of usd 18 mill.    Steady flow of bulker sales with a softening undertone on values.  Chinese buyers taking advantage of the huge supply of vessels for sale.

The sales activity is dominated by older vessels, both wet and dry.  Recent bulker sales reaffirm a softening in dry values across the board and there is certainly no lack of vessels for sale.  Several bulker deals are in the making with varying reports that AZUL FORTUNA 204k dwt built 2005 Universal is close to being sold for high usd 15 mill. If confirmed, this will be a notch down from the sale of one year older sister AZUL INTEGRA a month ago at usd 16 mill.  Tanker values are in positive trajectory but we have yet to see any very modern units being transacted.  Increased buying interest now also for LR1’s with reports that GULF CASTLE 75k dwt built 2009 HMD is under negotiation after being inspected by up to 10 buyers before inviting offers earlier this week.

The headline story this week has been the auction sale of six year old VLCC “BRIGHTOIL GEM.”  This was an online auction sale (local “Ebay”) in China and we understand only two buyers participated.    This is clearly a bargain for the buyers, our read being they are USD 10 mill in the money after DD and BWTS completed.  We fail to understand the commercial logic behind  this deal and we do not consider this a bench-mark sale due to the sales process. Most other deals coming to light this week are yesterday’s news.  The only significant deal concluded at today’s numbers is Zodiac selling aframax VIRGO SUN 115k dwt blt 2007 Sasebo at USD 26 mill.  In our book this equates to low 30’s for a suezmax of similar age.  Zodiac as always proving to be an agile player willing to take a profit when possible.  Zodiac purchased the vessel in October 2013 for low 25’s.  Dry bulk values are falling on the back of a growing pool of sales candidates. Kamsarmax KM TOKYO built 2010 Sanoyas is rumoured sold at high 15’s which is certainly on the low side of expectations.

The chase is on for mid to late 2000 built aframaxes with several 2007/2008 built units rumoured being committed in the Usd 26-28 mill range. If confirmed, this is approximately a Usd 2m appreciation in value since last done. Early 2000 built Vlcc’s are still in play with clients of MMT, Singapore leading the charge with 4 vessels bought in the past couple of months all basis prompt delivery. Signs of ongoing negotiations suggest we should see further similar units change hands in the near future.   Dry s&p markets continue to be muted this week with an ever increasing uncertainty stemming from falling freight markets which coupled with an increasing number of sales candidates are making it difficult for sales to materialise. Values are therefore subject to downwards pressures.  The s&p situation for very modern both bulkers and tankers is very similar - the bid/ask spread is too wide to result in any tangible deals. The returning question is clearly which buyers shall pay up for such very modern assets. Most of the public listed companies are very vocal in that no further capex is in the cards, now it’s all about returning dividend to shareholders.
