Add to this that many PE funds are looking to exit, we are left with the backbone of  cash-rich private owners looking to extract value from a potential modern tonnage acquisition. However most of these have already placed their bets at prices well below today’s asking prices and are quite happy to see the market play out.

The 2007 Japanese owned VLCC “PHOENIX VANGUARD” did, as expected, receive several offers this week and was quickly sold.  The price is reported to be in the usd 41.5 – 42.5 mill range.  Whilst this is 8-10% up on the previous deal which failed, it comes in the lower end of our expectations considering the original deal was concluded back in June and the spot market has since then settled at very healthy numbers; albeit considerably less than the initial spiky ones.  Early 2000 built crude tankers remain in demand and sellers able to give prompt delivery will be able to see new higher levels.  Several such deals are in the making. However sellers should be cautioned that the number of determined buyers is fairly thin on the ground and now may prove the right window of opportunity to exit; come Q1 and Q2 the number of older sales candidates will for sure increase.  It’s all about prompt delivery and a realistic runway for buyers to make a decent return.  The dry s&p market is lacking direction with many buyers taking a wait-and-see attitude.  The freight market is not lending support to the case and buyers are gaining the upper hand.There’s a very large number of ships for sale across the board, albeit few very modern ones.

Hartree is reported to have sold a brand new DSME built VLCC for close to usd 103 mill to Korean buyers.  This means, as expected, that we have broken the usd 100 mill mark for such ships able to give prompt delivery. We believe the number of buyers willing to pay these numbers is still thin on the ground but nevertheless this is clearly a new benchmark. As such a similar spec resale Suezmax able to give prompt delivery with scrubber onboard should be worth region usd 70 mill. Offers are invited next week for the 2007 DSME built VLCC PHOENIX VANGUARD and we understand close to ten buyers are outright. Older crude tankers are in demand as seen by the sale of VLCC’s ASTRO CHALLENGE and ENERGY R / POWER D built 2002 and 2003 which falls in line with the recent Ridgebury deal for same vintage.  Also we see much interest for MR’s across the board but modern eco ones have yet to see any sales activity.  We see a continuation of the decoupling between the rates and the values on dry. The explanation that most point to is the sluggish period rates caused by the FFA curve being in steep backwardation, which in turn is caused by bleak macro outlooks. Another explanation is that the number of bulkcarriers for sale is still large which goes a long way in explaining why values are best case still moving sideways.

The S&P activity is picking up in the tanker market. Rates having stabilized at lower, albeit still very firm levels, should bode for more predictable price levels in sight.  However, as we speak, the bid/ask spread is still quite wide with determined buyers running the risk of chasing after shadows in pursuit of particularly modern crude tankers. Rumors abound that a Korean VLCC resale has been committed at region usd 107 million on fairly long subjects.  The jury is still out as to what a brand new VLCC on water/with prompt delivery is worth, given a straight-forward sale. In any event we have for sure passed the usd 100 mill mark and as such we are moving into a pricing territory decoupled from newbuilding replacement costs.    This at a time when yard prices are soft. Based on history this delta would have resulted in increased newbuilding contracting but that’s far from the case now.  Two factors go a long way in explaining this – owners are uncertain about the longevity of the earning spike and even more importantly, owners are nervous and uncertain about the right propulsion system for the commercial life-span of a newbuilding.  MOL has the enviable position of soon inviting offers for their 2007 built VLCC PHOENIX VANGUARD after a previous deal at region usd 39 mill failed to materialize. The price will for sure be higher this time around.      Interest and transactions in the product space are also increasing with several first generation eco-spec MR’s for sale.  Grindrod Shipping for instance today invited inspections of its 2 x SPP 2013 built MRs LEOPARD MOON and LEOPARD SUN. We expect this vintage MR’s will command a price in the very high 20’s.  Following its recent purchase of two 2016 built Capesizes, JP Morgan is now inviting inspection of its TRUE ENDURANCE built 2012 HHI. The Chinese cabotage market is picking up and we are seeing interest for Tier II Supra- and Panamaxes. More ships ending up in the domestic market should have a positive impact for the overall market balance for these sizes. Once imported, they usually leave the international market for good as there are considerable costs related to importation.

Nothing can escape gravity, not even shipping rates. The rollercoaster ride in the tanker rates seen end of last week, leading to sky high hypothetical levels in asset prices, have taken a breath after a series of deals on subs failing and bringing the expectations down. We expect higher benchmarks going forward in the tanker sector and buyers biting the bullet as not only the spot rates but also the period market will likely support the price tags if the market establishes at these levels. The deals in the making and the ones already being reported done are reflecting same. Ridgebury Tankers has reportedly sold 3 x 2001 built VLCCs for region USD 100mio enbloc. The vessels were purchased for region USD 22mio each end 2017. Greek buyers, namely Avin and Union Maritime, have reportedly picked up the three Brightoil Aframaxes at auction in the region 20/21.5mio each, reflecting the vessels having all certificates overdue and must sail straight into the dock before enjoying this market. Next benchmark for Suezmaxes of the older vintage, will most likely be the 2 x 2000 Samsung built ladies, Jag Lakshita and Jag Lateef owned by GESCO, who are now inviting inspections.   The bulkers move sideways and with all eyes on tankers, one should not underestimate the potential upside going forward on acquiring quality tonnage at reasonable prices taking the current charter market into account. After a series of withdrawn vessels from Japanese owners due to price expectations not being met just prior to the tanker spike, we are again seeing modern tonnage being sold. Buyers who are not ready for the high tanker price tag, might increase the already existing competition, leading to increased prices here as well. Besides the reported concluded deals, we understand the 2019 Oshima built Ultramax MV Adventure III have seen offers in region USD 27.5mio, illustrating that quality modern tonnage are attracting firm levels.

Another week for the history books in the crude market with fantasy rates across the board. The S&P market is now in a major vacuum with sellers impossible to pin down on price. In any event, buyers anchored to yesterday’s values will simply not succeed in enticing potential sellers - determined buyers need as such to mentally press the “ctrl/alt/delete” button. With what can only be described as perfect timing, Zodiac this week purchased at auction VLCC BRIGHTOIL GALAXY 320k dwt built 2012 HHI for usd 61.5 mill. It’s easy to predict that the next auction sale of VLCC BRIGHTOIL GEM 320k dwt blt 2013 HHI, which is scheduled for 19th-20th November, will attract a number of keen buyers and ditto strong price. Talking of history books – the last time we had VLCC TCE in excess of usd 300k pd was in December 2007. At that time prompt resale VLCC was valued at Usd 153 mill, five year old at Usd 130 mill and a ten year old at Usd 104 mill. Furthermore, any ships at that time had a bunker consumption considerably higher than today and the HFO price was 50% higher. Taking into consideration the lower finance cost (Libor 60% lower) of the already lower cost of assets - it’s CLONDYKE!  Product tankers should pick up with crude shortly. Many LR2’s are rapidly going dirty plus crude tanker newbuildings are no longer stealing gasoil cargoes from product tankers.    Bulker values are still moving sideways as seen by the sale of Tess-82 MANGARELLA built 2009 Zosen at region Usd 15.6 mill.   Chances are we may see a spill-over effect from what’s going on in the crude markets whereby buyers who have missed the train there will increasingly put money to work for bulker purchases.  Based on historical correlation between earnings and values, we believe particularly the 5-10 year olds are undervalued by Usd 2-4 mill. Dry will remain a robust earnings case.
